Database dictionary, migration plan, data quality gates LLM / AI / RAG Как проверять AI behavior и снижать hallucination risk? AI eval spec, baseline, grounding evidence Quality, Testing & Evals Как доказывать качество до completion claims? Test/eval matrix, evidence format, gaps Security, Privacy & Compliance Какие security/privacy gates блокируют delivery? Security risk review, ASVS/SSDF mapping Delivery, Release & Operations Как выпускать и поддерживать систему? Release readiness, SLOs, runbooks, DORA metrics Codex / Agentic Workflow Как Codex работает в большом проекте без потери context? Control-plane files, handoffs, automation candidates

docs.title: Единый шаблон deep research
docs.text:
Каждый раздел должен отвечать на одинаковый набор вопросов:

  1. Purpose: какую проблему большого проекта закрывает раздел.
  2. Applicability: когда раздел обязателен, optional или not applicable.
  3. Concepts: какие идеи должен понимать инженер или агент.
  4. Development methodologies: какие методологии применять и где они вредны.
  5. Documentation artifacts: какие документы, diagrams, contracts или templates нужны.
  6. Tooling: какие tools выбрать по stack, scale и ownership.
  7. Verification: какие tests, evals, builds, checks или reviews дают evidence.
  8. Ownership: кто owner артефакта, кто reviewer, кто evidence owner.
  9. Risks: security, privacy, cost, performance, migration, compliance, operational risk.
  10. Codex routing: какой skill, subagent или workflow запускается и где approval boundary.
  11. Failure modes: как раздел превращается в бюрократию, stale docs или false confidence.
  12. Promotion path: когда manual workflow становится playbook, skill, plugin или automation.

docs.title: Принцип применения
docs.text:
Для больших проектов используйте lightweight maturity levels:

Level Когда подходит Требование baseline MVP, один владелец, низкий риск Минимальные requirements, plan, tests, runlog team Несколько инженеров или subagents Ownership, handoffs, architecture boundary, docs impact production Пользователи, данные, release process Security/privacy review, release readiness, rollback regulated PII, payments, healthcare, finance, enterprise governance Explicit approvals, audit evidence, source-backed policies

docs.title: Как использовать с Product-Agent OS
docs.text:
• REQUIREMENTS.md держит business, product, acceptance и source-of-truth constraints.
  • PLAN.md держит architecture boundary, slices, exact files, rollback and docs impact.
  • TEST.md держит deterministic checks, contract checks, runtime checks and accepted gaps.
  • EVALS.md держит subjective/AI/domain quality gates.
  • RUNLOG.md держит current evidence, decisions, failures and residual risks.
  • AGENTS.md держит durable project rules.

docs.title: Источники и Context7
docs.text: Primary sources должны храниться в source registry. Context7 используется как retrieval layer для developer documentation, но official status сохраняется только если underlying source официальный. Для этого раздела были перепроверены FSD, Storybook и OpenAPI через Context7, а security/operations источники проверены прямым web research 2026-05-24.

docs.title: API & Integrations
docs.text:
Source status: official + verified methodology + local implementation evidence + tool-assisted

Источники: OpenAPI Specification v3.2.0, AsyncAPI Specification v3.1.0, RFC 9110: HTTP Semantics, RFC 9457: Problem Details for HTTP APIs, RFC 9700: OAuth 2.0 Security BCP, OWASP API Security Top 10 2023, JSON Schema, CloudEvents, GraphQL Specification, gRPC Introduction, Pact, OpenAPI Generator, Stoplight Open Source API Toolkit, Google API Improvement Proposals, Context7 research, research dossier.

docs.title: Deep research цель
docs.text:
API & Integrations слой защищает public contracts, event contracts, generated clients, consumers, auth, error model, compatibility, rollout, deprecation policy and external-system write boundaries.

Главный принцип: API-изменение нельзя считать локальным изменением кода, пока не понятны contract source of truth, consumers, security model, compatibility impact, observability and release path.

docs.title: Поддержанные факты
docs.text:
• OpenAPI Specification v3.2.0 описывает HTTP APIs в language-agnostic формате: operations, parameters, request bodies, responses, examples, security schemes and reusable components.
  • AsyncAPI Specification v3.1.0 описывает message-driven APIs в machine-readable and protocol-agnostic формате.
  • RFC 9110 задает HTTP semantics; проект не должен изобретать локальные значения для methods, status codes and content negotiation без compatibility reason.
  • RFC 9457 Problem Details является сильным default для machine-readable HTTP error payloads, если существующие клиенты не требуют другой формат.
  • RFC 9700 OAuth 2.0 Security Best Current Practice должен использоваться как security baseline для OAuth-based APIs.
  • OWASP API Security Top 10 2023 дает API-specific risk vocabulary для threat modeling and security review gates.
  • JSON Schema current official dialect is 2020-12; payload contracts should state the dialect instead of relying on validator defaults.
  • CloudEvents v1.0.2 provides a standardized event metadata envelope option when cross-system event interoperability matters.
  • GraphQL projects should pin the specification target and govern schema complexity, deprecations and authorization instead of saying only "GraphQL".
  • gRPC uses Protocol Buffers as the default IDL and message interchange format; .proto files become source contracts.
  • Pact consumer-driven contract tests complement schema contracts because they capture real consumer expectations.
  • OpenAPI Generator can generate clients, server stubs and documentation from OpenAPI documents; generated SDKs need manifest, ownership and versioning.
  • Stoplight/Spectral is a candidate JSON/YAML lint path for projects with API style guides.
  • Google API Improvement Proposals are vendor-specific, but the transferable pattern is a local, versioned API style guide.

docs.title: Assumptions
docs.text:
• Product-Agent OS should not choose REST, GraphQL, gRPC or events as a universal default. API style is selected by consumers, latency, ownership, ecosystem, tooling and operational risk.
  • Contract-first is required for new public APIs, SDKs and provider/consumer splits; contract-aware development is acceptable when an existing code-first service has a maintained contract.
  • Rendered docs, Swagger UI, generated HTML and screenshots are not source of truth. The machine-readable contract or explicit gap is the source of truth.
  • Internal APIs can still have consumers. "Internal" only reduces exposure; it does not remove compatibility review.
  • External writes are side effects. Agents must use staged drafts, approval records and rollback paths before mutating external systems.

docs.title: Инструкции применения на проекте
docs.text:
1. Классифицируйте integration: internal HTTP API, public API, partner API, webhook, async event stream, GraphQL, gRPC, SDK, external provider or automation integration.
  2. Назовите contract source of truth: OpenAPI, AsyncAPI, GraphQL schema, .proto, JSON Schema, Pact contract or explicit gap.
  3. Зафиксируйте provider, consumers, owners, generated clients and runtime environments.
  4. Классифицируйте change: additive, behavior-compatible, potentially breaking or breaking.
  5. Обновите contract до или вместе с code. Contract drift должен блокировать completion claim.
  6. Добавьте examples для success, validation failure, auth failure and important domain failure.
  7. Опишите auth scheme, scopes, token claims, object-level authorization, rate limits and sensitive fields.
  8. Для HTTP errors используйте documented error model; RFC 9457 Problem Details является default, если нет compatibility constraint.
  9. Для events/webhooks опишите payload schema, headers, correlation ID, idempotency, retry, ordering and dead-letter behavior.
  10. Для generated SDKs обновите generator config, target languages, versioning and release notes.
  11. Добавьте contract tests: schema validation, provider verification and consumer-driven tests where consumer risk is high.
  12. Для external writes создайте staged artifact или approval record до фактического external mutation.
  13. Добавьте observability expectations: request IDs, correlation IDs, error counters, latency, rate-limit metrics and integration failure alerts.
  14. Запишите rollout, deprecation and rollback path in release artifact.

docs.title: Применяемые методологии разработки
docs.text: Методология Когда применять Как выглядит в проекте Contract-first development New public API, SDK, provider/consumer split Contract пишется или меняется до implementation; code/tests conform to it. Contract-aware development Existing code-first service Generated or maintained contract обновляется in the same slice as behavior. Consumer-driven contract testing Multiple consumers, microservices, frontend/backend split Consumers express expectations; providers verify before release. API lifecycle governance Draft, experimental, stable, deprecated, removed APIs Endpoint/message has lifecycle state, owner, compatibility policy and deprecation path. Backward compatibility by default Public, partner, mobile, SDK or event contracts Breaking/non-breaking classification before implementation. Error-contract governance HTTP APIs consumed by software clients Stable error types, status codes, examples and extensions. Event-contract governance Async messaging, queues, streams, webhooks Schema, metadata, retry, idempotency, ordering, correlation and dead-letter semantics. Integration security by design Authenticated API, external provider, sensitive data Auth matrix, scopes, object-level authorization, abuse cases and sensitive field review. Generated-client governance SDKs or typed clients are generated Generator, config, target languages, compatibility and release process are documented. API style-guide governance Large project or many teams Naming, pagination, filtering, versioning, status codes and examples are versioned/lintable. Two-stage review Public contract, migration, SDK, auth or event payload Stage 1 checks contract/security/compatibility; stage 2 checks implementation quality.

docs.title: Инструменты, артефакты и стандарты документирования
docs.text: Артефакт Зачем нужен Практический формат api-inventory.md APIs, owners, lifecycle states, consumers and source-of-truth files. Markdown/YAML table. OpenAPI document HTTP API source of truth. openapi.yaml, openapi.yml, openapi.json, pinned spec version. AsyncAPI document Message/event API source of truth. asyncapi.yaml, asyncapi.yml, asyncapi.json, pinned spec version. GraphQL schema GraphQL contract source. schema.graphql, deprecations, auth notes, complexity constraints. gRPC/protobuf IDL RPC contract source. .proto files and generator config. JSON Schema library Shared JSON payload contracts. JSON Schema 2020-12 or project-pinned dialect. api-error-catalog.md Stable HTTP error types, status codes, extensions and examples. RFC 9457 Problem Details where compatible. api-auth-authorization-matrix.md Auth schemes, scopes, roles, token claims and object-level rules. OpenAPI security schemes + OAuth BCP + OWASP API risks. api-consumer-map.md Human/system consumers, SDKs, generated clients, owners and approval path. Consumer/owner matrix. api-compatibility-record.md Breaking/non-breaking classification and migration impact. ADR-style record. api-contract-test-matrix.md Provider verification, consumer tests, schema tests and negative cases. Pact, schema validators, stack-specific API tests. generated-sdk-manifest.md Generator, version, config, target languages, owner and release process. OpenAPI Generator or stack-specific generator. webhook-event-contract.md Retry, idempotency, ordering, signature verification, replay and dead-letter behavior. AsyncAPI, CloudEvents where useful. external-integration-approval.md Read/write capability, sandbox credentials, staged draft, approval and rollback path. Project control-plane artifact. api-style-guide.md Naming, pagination, filtering, versioning, status codes, errors and examples. Local rules inspired by selected API guidelines. Deprecation plan Timeline, compatibility mode, communication, release notes and removal criteria. Release packet / changelog.

docs.title: Product-Agent OS routing
docs.text:
• api_migration usage mode routes API/SDK/event changes to migration planning before implementation.
  • workspace-discovery-auditor detects OpenAPI, AsyncAPI, GraphQL, protobuf, Pact, generated clients and external integrations.
  • implementation-planner blocks build if contract source, consumers, compatibility classification or owner review is missing.
  • test-eval-designer asks for contract tests, consumer tests, schema validation and negative auth/error cases.
  • risk-reviewer performs two-stage review for public contract, auth, event, SDK and external-integration changes.
  • pr-release-operator includes release notes, migration guidance, SDK impact, deprecation plan and rollback/disable path.

docs.title: Candidate readiness gates
docs.text:
• api_contract_source_present: OpenAPI, AsyncAPI, GraphQL schema, .proto, JSON Schema, Pact contract or explicit gap is named.
  • api_consumer_map_present: consumers, generated clients and owners are named for public, partner, mobile or multi-team contracts.
  • api_breaking_change_reviewed: migration plan, deprecation window and owner approval exist for breaking/potentially breaking changes.
  • api_security_reviewed: auth scheme, authorization rules, scopes, sensitive fields and abuse cases are documented.
  • api_error_contract_present: success and error examples are present.
  • event_delivery_contract_present: retry, idempotency, ordering, correlation and dead-letter behavior are documented.
  • generated_client_manifest_present: SDK generator/config/release impact is documented.
  • external_write_approval_present: staged draft, approval and rollback path exist before writes to external systems.

docs.title: Candidate eval fields
docs.text:
• Contract source is named and linked.
  • Consumers and generated clients are named.
  • Breaking/non-breaking classification is present.
  • Migration/deprecation plan exists for breaking changes.
  • Auth scheme and authorization rules are documented.
  • Success and error examples are present.
  • Event delivery semantics are documented for async integrations.
  • Contract verification command or missing-tool gap is recorded.
  • External writes are staged and approval-bound.

docs.title: Tooling candidates
docs.text: Tooling area Candidate Notes HTTP API contract OpenAPI Default source for REST-like HTTP APIs. Pin spec version per project. Event API contract AsyncAPI Default source for message-driven APIs and webhooks when useful. Shared JSON schemas JSON Schema Declare dialect; avoid validator-default ambiguity. Error model RFC 9457 Problem Details Good default for machine-readable HTTP errors. API lint Spectral / Stoplight Useful when the project has API style guide rules; adoption requires stack check. Code/doc generation OpenAPI Generator Useful for SDKs/stubs/docs; generated output requires ownership and diff review. Consumer contracts Pact Useful when real consumer expectations matter more than schema completeness. Event metadata CloudEvents Useful for cross-system event interoperability; not mandatory for simple internal events. RPC gRPC/protobuf Useful for typed, polyglot service-to-service APIs; .proto is the source contract. Query API GraphQL Useful for client-shaped reads; requires complexity, authorization and deprecation governance. API style rules Google AIP-style local guide Vendor-specific source used as inspiration for local governed style rules.

docs.title: Проверки
docs.text:
• Contract source is updated or gap is explicit.
  • Consumers and generated clients are named.
  • Breaking change has migration plan and owner review.
  • Auth/security changes have security review route.
  • Error model is documented and examples exist.
  • Event delivery semantics are documented for async integrations.
  • Contract check command is run or recorded as missing.
  • External write operations are staged and approval-bound.
  • Release notes mention SDK, consumer, deprecation and rollback impact when relevant.

docs.title: Failure modes
docs.text:
• Swagger UI or rendered docs are treated as source of truth instead of OpenAPI/contract files.
  • Internal API is assumed to have no consumers.
  • Event payload changes are released without consumer compatibility review.
  • Security schemes are documented in prose but missing from contract.
  • SDKs are regenerated without reproducible config and reviewable diff.
  • OAuth scopes or token claims change without authorization matrix.
  • Error payloads are improvised per endpoint.
  • GraphQL or gRPC is chosen as automatically superior without consumer and operational justification.
  • Contract tests duplicate only provider behavior instead of expressing consumer expectations.
  • Agent writes to external systems without staged artifact and explicit approval.

docs.title: Unsupported claims not adopted
docs.text:
• "Rendered API docs are enough." They are outputs, not source of truth.
  • "Internal APIs do not need compatibility review." Internal consumers still break.
  • "Schema validation is the same as contract testing." Schema validation does not capture all consumer expectations.
  • "GraphQL/gRPC/event-driven is always more modern." Style choice depends on consumers, operations and governance.
  • "OAuth exists, so API security is handled." Scopes, token claims, object-level authorization, rate limits and abuse cases still need review.
  • "Generated SDKs are mechanical." Generator config, versioning and consumer migration need ownership.

docs.title: Open questions for future implementation
docs.text:
• Which API lint tool should become the Product-Agent OS default: Spectral, Redocly CLI, framework-native checks or no default?
  • Should Product-Agent OS ship a generic api-style-guide.md, or only a selector that asks the project to choose one?
  • Which compatibility rules should be encoded separately for JSON Schema, protobuf, GraphQL and AsyncAPI?
  • Should API security gates be based on OWASP API Top 10, ASVS, SSDF or a combined project profile?
  • How should agentic API migrations handle generated clients across multiple repositories?
  • Which API test generators are mature enough for stack-specific default recommendations?

docs.title: Backend
docs.text:
Source status: official + expert reference + vendor documentation + local implementation evidence + tool-assisted

Источники: Twelve-Factor App, OpenTelemetry documentation, Google SRE SLO chapter, NIST SSDF, OWASP ASVS, CNCF Cloud Native Definition, Kubernetes probes, Hexagonal Architecture, Martin Fowler Microservices Guide, Azure Retry pattern, Azure Circuit Breaker pattern, Azure Queue-Based Load Leveling pattern, Azure Health Endpoint Monitoring pattern, Azure Saga pattern, Context7 research, research dossier.

docs.title: Deep research цель
docs.text:
Backend слой описывает service responsibilities, domain logic, jobs, queues, runtime configuration, observability, reliability, security, health checks, data consistency and operational safety.

Главный принцип: backend-изменение нельзя считать завершенным, если понятен code diff, но не понятны runtime behavior, failure modes, observability, rollback and production impact.

docs.title: Поддержанные факты
docs.text:
• Twelve-Factor App задает service-style vocabulary: explicit dependencies, environment config, backing services, build-release-run separation, stateless processes, disposability, dev/prod parity, logs and admin processes.
  • OpenTelemetry defines vendor-neutral observability concepts for traces, metrics, logs, context propagation, baggage, semantic conventions, collectors and language instrumentation.
  • Google SRE guidance frames SLO work around user-relevant SLIs and recommends a small number of indicators that represent what users care about.
  • NIST SSDF recommends secure software development practices that can be integrated into SDLC implementations.
  • OWASP ASVS provides a versioned basis for testing web application technical security controls and secure development requirements.
  • CNCF Cloud Native Definition characterizes cloud-native systems as loosely coupled, secure, resilient, manageable, sustainable and observable, supported by automation.
  • Kubernetes readiness, liveness and startup probes are distinct runtime health mechanisms; readiness prevents traffic from reaching a service that is alive but not ready.
  • Hexagonal Architecture / Ports and Adapters separates application logic from UI, database and runtime adapters so application behavior can be tested through ports.
  • Martin Fowler's microservices guide defines microservices as independently deployable services built around business capabilities and highlights design-for-failure.
  • Azure Architecture Center documents retry, circuit breaker, queue-based load leveling, health endpoint monitoring and saga patterns. These are vendor docs, but the patterns are useful backend resilience references.

docs.title: Assumptions
docs.text:
• Product-Agent OS should default to clear backend boundaries before recommending microservices. Microservices are conditional, not a maturity badge.
  • Backend docs must describe runtime behavior, not only package/module structure.
  • Retry, queue and distributed workflow behavior is unsafe unless idempotency, timeout, max attempts, replay and recovery are explicit.
  • SLOs are required for production/user-facing services unless an explicit gap is recorded.
  • Security-sensitive backend behavior includes auth, secrets, tokens, PII, money movement, privileged operations, external writes and irreversible side effects.
  • Platform-specific health checks should use the deployment platform semantics. Kubernetes probe vocabulary is a useful reference, not a universal runtime requirement.

docs.title: Инструкции применения на проекте
docs.text:
1. Классифицируйте backend unit: module, monolith subsystem, service, worker, scheduler, consumer, API backend, integration adapter or migration runner.
  2. Назовите service boundary: purpose, owner, inbound contracts, outbound dependencies, data ownership and deployment/runtime shape.
  3. Для complex domain свяжите boundary with bounded context and ubiquitous language.
  4. Применяйте Hexagonal Architecture / Ports and Adapters, когда domain logic должна быть независима от HTTP, database, queue or vendor SDK concerns.
  5. До реализации distributed behavior опишите retries, timeouts, idempotency, deduplication, backpressure, ordering, scheduling and replay.
  6. Для каждой remote dependency задайте timeout, retry, circuit breaker, fallback, alert and owner.
  7. Для jobs/queues опишите payload contract, retry policy, dead-letter behavior, idempotency key and replay procedure.
  8. Для distributed transactions сначала проверьте, достаточно ли local transaction/outbox. Если нет, документируйте saga/compensation and monitoring.
  9. Определите observability evidence: traces for request flow, metrics for service health, logs for decisions/errors and correlation IDs across boundaries.
  10. Для production services задайте SLI/SLO или explicit gap.
  11. Treat health endpoints as contracts: liveness, readiness and startup checks не должны быть синонимами.
  12. Документируйте config and secrets boundaries; secrets не должны попадать в docs, prompts, fixtures, logs or examples.
  13. Auth, sensitive data, money movement, privileged operations and irreversible side effects route through risk/security review.
  14. Для risky backend changes заранее укажите rollback, recovery or replay path.

docs.title: Применяемые методологии разработки
docs.text: Методология Когда применять Как выглядит в проекте Modular monolith first Early/medium product, unclear service boundaries One deployable backend with explicit module boundaries and ownership. Conditional microservices Proven independent scaling/team/deploy need Services map to business capabilities, have independent deployability and explicit failure contracts. Hexagonal Architecture / Ports and Adapters Domain logic is important and adapters change Core use cases depend on ports; DB/API/queue/vendor SDK are adapters. DDD boundaries Complex business domain Backend modules/services map to bounded contexts and domain language. TDD for domain logic Deterministic business rules and service logic Unit tests drive behavior before implementation. Integration-first backend testing Storage, queues, transactions, external adapters Tests exercise real or representative boundaries before release. Contract-aware service development APIs/events/external contracts OpenAPI, AsyncAPI, Pact, .proto or provider contracts updated with code. Twelve-Factor service discipline SaaS/cloud-style backend Config/env, dependencies, build-release-run, logs and admin tasks are documented. SRE-inspired reliability Production service with users or downstream consumers SLO/gap, user-relevant SLIs, runbooks and alert signals. Observability-driven development Debugging requires runtime evidence Traces, metrics, logs, correlation IDs, dashboards and alerts are captured. Resilience pattern design Remote dependencies, queues, load spikes, transient faults Timeouts, retry, backoff, circuit breaker, load leveling, backpressure and fallback. Secure SDLC Auth, secrets, sensitive data, money or privileged operations Security notes, abuse cases, audit logging and no-secrets evidence are required. Saga / compensating workflow Distributed transaction cannot use single ACID transaction Workflow state, idempotency, compensation, monitoring and recovery path. Runbook-driven operations Production service, worker or scheduled job Failure modes, dashboards, logs, restart/replay steps and escalation path.

docs.title: Инструменты, артефакты и стандарты документирования
docs.text: Артефакт Зачем нужен Практический формат backend-service-overview.md Purpose, owner, boundary, dependencies, data stores, APIs/events and runtime. Product-Agent OS template. Module/service boundary map What belongs inside the backend boundary and what is external. C4, Mermaid, Structurizr, ADR. Ports and adapters map Inbound ports, outbound ports and concrete adapters. Hexagonal Architecture note. backend-runtime-behavior.md Jobs, queues, retries, timeouts, idempotency, backpressure and failure modes. Runtime behavior doc. backend-dependency-failure-matrix.md Per dependency timeout, retry, circuit breaker, fallback, owner and alert. Resilience matrix. backend-observability-map.md Traces, metrics, logs, correlation IDs, dashboards, alerts and redaction notes. OpenTelemetry vocabulary. backend-slo-sheet.md User journey, SLI, SLO target, measurement window and alert policy. Google SRE-inspired sheet. backend-health-check-contract.md Liveness/readiness/startup or equivalent platform health semantics. Kubernetes/platform docs. backend-job-queue-contract.md Queue name, producer, consumer, payload contract, idempotency, retry, DLQ and replay. AsyncAPI/runbook. backend-data-consistency-record.md Transaction boundary, consistency model, outbox/saga/compensation and recovery path. ADR/runbook. Security notes Authn/authz, secrets, rate limits, audit logging, sensitive data and abuse cases. NIST SSDF / OWASP ASVS. backend-config-secrets-manifest.md Env/config keys, secret source, rotation notes and local/prod parity. Twelve-Factor/platform docs. backend-release-rollback-notes.md Migration, feature flag, rollback, replay and data recovery plan. Release packet. backend-operational-runbook.md Common failures, dashboard links, logs, recovery steps and escalation. SRE practice.

docs.title: Product-Agent OS routing
docs.text:
• workspace-discovery-auditor maps backend stack, commands, CI, APIs, DB, queues, workers, deployment and security signals.
  • requirements-author records service/user behavior, non-goals and runtime constraints before implementation tasks.
  • implementation-planner blocks risky backend work if service boundary, runtime behavior, rollback or verification is missing.
  • test-eval-designer selects unit, integration, contract, migration, runtime and observability checks.
  • risk-reviewer handles security, data, migration, performance, external dependency and irreversible side-effect risk.
  • pr-release-operator includes backend release notes, migration guidance, runbook impact and rollback/replay notes.

docs.title: Candidate readiness gates
docs.text:
• backend_service_boundary_present: purpose, owner, dependencies and data stores are named.
  • backend_runtime_behavior_present: retry, timeout, idempotency, ordering, replay and failure modes are documented.
  • backend_dependency_failure_matrix_present: remote dependencies have timeout/retry/fallback/alert/owner policy.
  • backend_observability_contract_present: logs/metrics/traces/correlation IDs and redaction notes are present.
  • backend_slo_or_gap_present: user-facing or production service has SLO/SLI or explicit gap.
  • backend_health_probe_contract_present: liveness/readiness/startup semantics are documented where applicable.
  • backend_security_reviewed: auth, secrets, sensitive data, money and privileged operations have review route.
  • backend_data_consistency_strategy_present: transaction boundary, consistency model and recovery path are documented.
  • backend_config_secrets_boundary_present: config and secrets handling is explicit.
  • backend_rollback_plan_present: migration, external write or production behavior change has rollback/recovery path.

docs.title: Candidate eval fields
docs.text:
• Service/module boundary, owner and purpose are present.
  • Dependencies and data stores are named.
  • Runtime behavior is documented for jobs, queues and remote calls.
  • Retry policy includes timeout, backoff, max attempts and idempotency.
  • Observability contract includes no-secrets logging and correlation IDs.
  • SLO/SLI exists or gap is explicit.
  • Health checks distinguish liveness, readiness and startup where applicable.
  • Security-sensitive behavior has a risk review route.
  • Data consistency and rollback plan exist for risky changes.
  • Verification commands include unit, integration, contract or runtime checks appropriate to the change.

docs.title: Tooling candidates
docs.text: Tooling area Candidate Notes Runtime service discipline Twelve-Factor Good default vocabulary for config, logs, processes and dev/prod parity. Observability OpenTelemetry Cross-stack vocabulary for traces, metrics, logs, context propagation and collectors. Reliability SLO/SLI sheets Use user-relevant indicators, not every available metric. Service architecture C4, ADR, Ports and Adapters map Useful when service boundaries or adapters change. Runtime health Kubernetes probes or platform equivalent Use only when deployment platform supports probe semantics. Resilience patterns Retry, circuit breaker, load leveling, health endpoint monitoring Vendor docs are references; implementation should be stack-native. Distributed workflow Saga/compensation docs Use only when local transaction/outbox is not enough. Security SSDF, ASVS, secret scanning, SAST/DAST where applicable Select by stack and risk profile. Local runtime signals Dockerfile, Procfile, docker-compose.yml, serverless.yml, k8s/*.yaml Discovery signals, not mandatory standards.

docs.title: Проверки
docs.text:
• Service overview updated for new or changed backend responsibility.
  • Unit tests cover deterministic domain logic.
  • Integration/contract tests cover storage, queues, APIs or external adapters affected by the change.
  • Retry logic has timeout, backoff, max attempts and idempotency evidence.
  • Observability changes avoid secrets and private data.
  • Health checks are tested or explicitly marked as platform-unavailable.
  • Rollback/replay path is named for risky backend changes.
  • Config and secrets boundary is documented without exposing secrets.
  • Runtime verification exists for deployable services where environment is available.

docs.title: Failure modes
docs.text:
• Backend docs describe packages but omit runtime behavior.
  • Retry logic is added without timeout, backoff, max attempts and idempotency.
  • Liveness and readiness endpoints are treated as the same check.
  • Logs expose secrets, tokens, private data or full payloads.
  • Worker can process the same message twice but has no deduplication policy.
  • Queue has no dead-letter, replay or poison-message procedure.
  • Service boundary changes happen without owner review or ADR.
  • Distributed workflow has no compensation or recovery evidence.
  • Microservices are introduced before module boundaries, deployment automation and observability are mature.
  • Completion is claimed after code inspection without integration/runtime verification.

docs.title: Unsupported claims not adopted
docs.text:
• "Backend means only business logic files." Backend includes runtime, data, queues, config, observability, security and operations.
  • "Microservices are the professional default." They are useful only with real ownership, deployment and scaling reasons.
  • "Retries make systems reliable." Retries without idempotency and backoff can amplify failure.
  • "Health endpoint exists, so readiness is solved." Liveness/readiness/startup have different operational meanings.
  • "Logs are observability." Logs are one signal; traces, metrics, correlation IDs and dashboards matter for runtime evidence.
  • "SLOs are only for large companies." Any production service needs user-relevant reliability expectation or explicit gap.

docs.title: Open questions for future implementation
docs.text:
• Should Product-Agent OS default to modular monolith guidance before microservice guidance in generated templates?
  • Which stack-specific backend templates should be generated first: Node.js, Python, Java, .NET, Go or framework-agnostic only?
  • Should health check templates be platform-neutral or Kubernetes-first with alternatives?
  • Which resilience library examples are mature enough for stack-specific snippets?
  • How should the plugin detect risky retry/idempotency changes from code alone?
  • Should SLO templates live under backend, delivery/operations or both?

docs.title: Business & Product
docs.text:
Source status: official + verified methodology + local implementation evidence + tool-assisted

Источники: Google HEART framework paper, Amplitude North Star Hub, Amplitude taxonomy planning, Amplitude implementation team organization, Product Talk Opportunity Solution Trees, The Lean Startup methodology, Strategyzer Value Proposition Canvas, Building an AI-Native Engineering Team, Codex verified operations, Codex AI app evals, Product-Agent OS development standards.

docs.title: Deep research цель
docs.text:
Business & Product слой отвечает на вопрос: зачем большой проект существует, для кого он строится, какая гипотеза проверяется, какой outcome должен измениться и какие evidence докажут, что change полезен, а не просто технически завершен.

В Product-Agent OS этот слой должен появляться до architecture, requirements slicing и implementation plan. Если пользователь, value proposition, opportunity, non-goal, success metric и guardrails не названы, Codex App, CLI, IDE extension или subagents могут построить правильный код для неправильной задачи.

docs.title: Поддержанные факты
docs.text:
• Google HEART описывает user-centered метрики и процесс Goals -> Signals -> Metrics для связи продуктовой цели с измеримыми сигналами.
  • Amplitude North Star подход фокусирует команду на primary value metric и input metrics, которые объясняют, как команда влияет на эту value metric.
  • Amplitude taxonomy guidance требует заранее определить events, properties, naming convention и data quality правила, иначе продуктовые решения строятся на неустойчивых данных.
  • Opportunity Solution Tree связывает desired outcome, opportunity space, solution space и assumption tests; opportunity не должна подменяться feature-идеей.
  • Lean Startup формулирует product development как эксперимент: "Should this product be built?", MVP, Build-Measure-Learn, actionable metrics, pivot/persevere.
  • Strategyzer Value Proposition Canvas требует описывать customer jobs, pains, gains и то, как offering снимает pains и создает gains.
  • OpenAI Codex guidance для AI-native engineering переводит инженеров от механического build-work к clarifying product behavior, architecture review, domain alignment and long-term quality.
  • Codex AI app eval guidance рекомендует превращать конкретное user-visible promise в repeatable eval suite до prompt/model/retrieval/agent changes.
  • Локальный Product-Agent OS уже содержит metric-spec.md, REQUIREMENTS.md, readiness gate metric_hardening_when_product_behavior_changes и release gate на post-release measurement.

docs.title: Assumptions
docs.text:
• Behavior-changing slice starts from target user, opportunity/problem, expected outcome, non-goals, acceptance scenario and metric status.
  • Internal refactors, dependency bumps and mechanical docs changes can mark product metrics as not_applicable when the reason is explicit.
  • Proxy metric is acceptable only with counter-metric, guardrail, qualitative review and post-release review.
  • Product analytics events are project contracts and need taxonomy, owner, privacy classification and validation evidence.
  • AI product behavior needs both eval evidence for behavior and product evidence for value when it affects a user-facing promise.
  • Workflow promotion follows manual thread -> playbook -> skill -> plugin -> automation only when value, verification, owner and safety boundary are explicit.

docs.title: Инструкции применения на проекте
docs.text:
1. Начинайте meaningful behavior change с product hypothesis: target user, problem/opportunity, expected behavior change, outcome, non-goals.
  2. Зафиксируйте value proposition: customer jobs, pains, gains, pain relievers, gain creators и evidence, откуда это известно.
  3. Разделите business outcome, product outcome и feature traction metric. Для discovery предпочтительнее product outcome, который команда может реально изменить.
  4. Для сложной или неопределенной области ведите Opportunity Solution Tree: desired outcome -> opportunities -> candidate solutions -> riskiest assumptions -> tests.
  5. Для MVP формулируйте Lean experiment: hypothesis, smallest build, measure plan, learning threshold, pivot/persevere decision.
  6. Назовите decision horizon: discovery, MVP, beta, production, scale. Не требуйте одинакового уровня формальности для всех горизонтов.
  7. Разделите primary value metric, input metrics, counter-metrics и guardrails. Primary metric показывает value, input metrics объясняют рычаги, counter-metrics ловят деградацию.
  8. Обязательно опишите proxy metric risk: как команда может улучшить метрику и одновременно ухудшить пользовательскую или бизнес-ценность.
  9. Добавьте qualitative feedback loop: interviews, support tickets, sales/customer-success signals, review notes или explicit evidence gap.
  10. Для analytics заранее создайте tracking plan: event name, owner, business question, properties, property types, privacy classification, retention, dashboard/report.
  11. Для AI-facing behavior добавьте eval plan: user-visible promise, seed cases, assertions/graders, baseline command, threshold, failure review owner.
  12. Для privacy-sensitive метрик укажите data minimization, consent/policy source, retention/deletion rule и privacy/legal owner.
  13. После release сравните actual signals с гипотезой и внесите lessons, failures и accepted gaps в RUNLOG.md.
  14. Не заявляйте product success по одному proxy metric без guardrail, qualitative review и post-release evidence.

docs.title: Применяемые методологии разработки
docs.text: Методология Когда применять Как выглядит в проекте Product hypothesis Любая feature, которая должна изменить пользовательское или бизнес-поведение REQUIREMENTS.md содержит user, problem/opportunity, expected outcome, non-goals, assumptions and evidence gaps. Value Proposition Canvas Новая аудитория, новый продукт, новая capability или сомнение в value value-proposition.md описывает jobs, pains, gains, pain relievers, gain creators and evidence source. Opportunity Solution Tree Discovery, roadmap choice, ambiguous user need, competing feature ideas opportunity-tree.md связывает outcome, opportunity, solution, assumption test and decision. Lean Build-Measure-Learn MVP, experiment, risky assumption, uncertain market/user value experiment-plan.md фиксирует smallest build, metric, learning threshold, pivot/persevere rule. HEART metrics UX/product quality нужно измерять через user-centered goals Выбираются релевантные Happiness, Engagement, Adoption, Retention или Task success; не все категории обязательны. North Star / primary value metric Продукту нужна единая value metric и driver tree metric-spec.md содержит primary value metric, input metrics, owner, baseline, target and time window. Metric hardening Любое product behavior изменение с measurement claim Counter-metric, guardrails, proxy risk, qualitative review, privacy classification and post-release review are required. Product analytics governance Usage data становится источником решений Tracking plan, taxonomy, naming convention, data owner, instrumentation owner and validation evidence. Data-informed decision making После появления usage data, feedback loop или release evidence Decisions cite metric, user research, support signal, eval result or accepted evidence gap. Outcome-driven planning Roadmap нужно разбить на measurable outcomes PLAN.md slice связан с expected behavior, measurement, acceptance scenario and release review. AI product evals Prompt/model/retrieval/tool/agent behavior влияет на пользователя Baseline eval exists before behavior change; suite tests app path users hit where feasible.

docs.title: Инструменты, артефакты и стандарты документирования
docs.text: Артефакт Назначение Минимальное содержимое REQUIREMENTS.md Product intent and behavior scope Target user, problem/opportunity, hypothesis, non-goals, constraints, acceptance criteria, metric status. metric-spec.md Metric hardening Primary metric, input metrics, counter-metric, guardrails, proxy risk, privacy classification, owner, post-release review. value-proposition.md Customer value fit Jobs, pains, gains, pain relievers, gain creators, segment, evidence source, open assumptions. opportunity-tree.md Discovery traceability Desired outcome, opportunities, candidate solutions, assumptions, tests, decisions. experiment-plan.md Lean MVP / assumption test Hypothesis, smallest build, measure plan, learning threshold, pivot/persevere rule, owner. tracking-plan.md Product analytics governance Events, properties, naming convention, owner, dashboard, validation command/report, privacy review. acceptance-scenarios.md Requirement -> scenario -> evidence Actor, context, trigger, observable outcome, deterministic/manual/eval check, evidence owner. EVALS.md AI behavior and subjective quality Dataset, rubric, grader/assertion, baseline, threshold, failure review, regression command. RUNLOG.md Current cycle evidence Decisions, experiments, failures, post-release measurement, accepted gaps and next review date. Release notes User-facing change and measurement plan What changed, who is affected, rollout scope, measurement window, rollback/disable signal.

docs.title: Product-Agent OS routing
docs.text:
• requirements-author owns the first product_hypothesis packet and must mark metric_scope as required, not_applicable or accepted_gap.
  • implementation-planner must stop when a behavior-changing slice lacks product hypothesis, acceptance scenario, metric/gap or owner.
  • test-eval-designer maps product behavior to deterministic checks, exploratory checks, product analytics validation or AI evals.
  • solution-architect uses product outcome, constraints and guardrails to choose architecture tradeoffs; architecture should not invent product goals.
  • pr-release-operator checks release measurement, metric hardening and post-release review before product success claims.
  • learning-loop-maintainer captures actual measurement results and decides whether the workflow should become playbook, skill, plugin or automation.

docs.title: Candidate readiness gates
docs.text:
• product_hypothesis_present: target user, opportunity/problem, expected outcome and non-goals exist.
  • target_user_segment_present: primary, secondary and explicitly excluded users are named when scope matters.
  • value_proposition_evidence_present: jobs/pains/gains and source or accepted gap are recorded.
  • opportunity_not_solution_present: at least one problem/opportunity statement is not just a feature request.
  • success_metric_present: primary metric or explicit not_applicable reason is present.
  • metric_hardening_when_product_behavior_changes: input metric, counter-metric, guardrail, proxy risk and owner exist.
  • analytics_tracking_plan_present: events/properties/taxonomy/owner/privacy are defined when product usage data is claimed.
  • qualitative_feedback_loop_present: user research, support/sales signal or accepted qualitative gap is recorded.
  • ai_product_eval_when_ai_behavior_changes: AI behavior changes have baseline eval or accepted baseline gap.
  • post_release_measurement_plan_present: review window, dashboard/report, owner and rollback/decision rule exist.
  • release_measurement_evidence_present: actual metrics, eval result, user feedback or explicit evidence gap exists before success claim.

docs.title: Candidate eval fields
docs.text:
• product_hypothesis_contract_present
  • target_user_segment_contract_present
  • value_proposition_trace_present
  • opportunity_solution_assumption_trace_present
  • metric_hardening_contract_present
  • analytics_tracking_plan_contract_present
  • privacy_classification_for_metrics_present
  • ai_behavior_eval_contract_present
  • post_release_measurement_contract_present
  • workflow_promotion_value_evidence_present

docs.title: Проверки
docs.text:
• REQUIREMENTS.md names target user, problem/opportunity, outcome, non-goal, assumptions and metric status.
  • Every behavior change has an acceptance scenario or explicit accepted gap.
  • metric-spec.md includes primary metric, input metric, counter-metric, guardrail, proxy risk and privacy classification.
  • Tracking events have stable names, property definitions, owner and validation plan.
  • AI behavior claims cite eval baseline/current results, not only prompt inspection.
  • Completion claims cite current evidence; planned measurement alone is not product success.

docs.title: Failure modes
docs.text:
• Feature idea masquerades as opportunity, so discovery starts from solution bias.
  • One metric becomes the goal and damages product quality, trust, support load or privacy.
  • Product hypothesis is written after implementation to justify existing work.
  • North Star metric is used for a small isolated slice where a local product outcome would be clearer.
  • Analytics events are added without taxonomy, property definitions, privacy classification or owner.
  • AI eval score is treated as product value without user outcome, qualitative review or post-release evidence.
  • Codex velocity is treated as business value without measuring what changed for the user or team.
  • Community claims or memory are promoted into core guidance without source status.

docs.title: Unsupported claims not adopted
docs.text:
• "A single metric proves product success." It is only useful with context, counter-metrics, guardrails and qualitative review.
  • "More usage always means more value." Usage can grow while satisfaction, accuracy, cost, trust or retention degrade.
  • "Product discovery can be skipped because Codex can build quickly." Faster implementation increases the cost of unclear intent.
  • "Evals replace product metrics." Evals test AI behavior; product value still needs user/business outcome evidence.
  • "Automation should follow every repeated workflow." Automation follows only after value, verification, ownership and safety boundaries are stable.

docs.title: Open questions for future implementation
docs.text:
• Should product_hypothesis_present become universal for every behavior-changing slice, or only user-facing/product-labeled changes?
  • Should Product-Agent OS generate separate value-proposition.md, opportunity-tree.md and product-brief.md, or keep them optional inside REQUIREMENTS.md until project growth demands separation?
  • What threshold should route a slice from simple metric-spec.md to full analytics tracking-plan.md?
  • How should post-release measurement be represented when the project has no production telemetry yet?
  • Should workflow promotion into skill/plugin require product metric evidence, or is explicit engineering time saved enough for internal workflows?

docs.title: Codex / Agentic Workflow
docs.text:
Source status: official OpenAI + verified methodology + local implementation evidence + tool-assisted + experiment

Источники: Codex best practices, Codex customization, AGENTS.md guide, Agent Skills, Subagents, Codex MCP, Codex hooks, Codex build plugins, Codex agent approvals and security, Codex memories, Codex workflows, Codex automations, Save workflows as skills, Run verified operations, Follow goals in Codex, OpenAI Agents SDK, Agents SDK orchestration and handoffs, Agents SDK guardrails and human review, Evaluate agent workflows, Context7 research, research dossier.

docs.title: Deep research цель
docs.text:
Codex / Agentic Workflow слой описывает, как большой проект использует Codex App, CLI, IDE extension, subagents, skills, AGENTS.md, memory, sandbox, approvals, MCP, hooks, plugins, Agents SDK и automations без превращения чата в source of truth.

Главный принцип: чат является рабочей поверхностью, но не durable state. Требования, решения, ограничения, evidence, approvals, handoffs и promotion decisions должны жить в AGENTS.md, control-plane файлах, task packets, run logs, source registry и staged artifacts.

docs.title: Поддержанные факты
docs.text:
• Codex customization layers include AGENTS.md, skills, subagents, MCP, hooks, plugins, memory, workflows and automations; they solve different persistence and capability problems.
  • Official Codex guidance treats AGENTS.md as durable project instructions and memory as recall layer, not source of mandatory project truth.
  • Skills package repeatable workflows with trigger, inputs, steps, references/scripts, verification and failure modes.
  • Subagents are useful for independent or specialist work, but require fresh-context task packets, ownership boundaries and handoff evidence.
  • MCP, hooks, plugins and automations are capability surfaces with permission, trust, data-boundary and side-effect implications.
  • Verified operations and goal-following workflows require structured inputs, current evidence, explicit approvals and auditable output.
  • Agents SDK concepts such as handoffs, guardrails, tracing and human review are useful for code-owned agent apps, but must stay distinct from Codex App/CLI/IDE runtime workflow guidance.

docs.title: Assumptions
docs.text:
• Chat is a work surface, not source of truth; durable state belongs in checked-in artifacts.
  • Reusable workflows should be promoted only after manual success, known failure modes and verification evidence.
  • Subagents and parallel workers need explicit file/subsystem ownership. Overlap should route to sequential work.
  • MCP and hooks should be reviewed as side-effecting capabilities before activation.
  • Automations are only for stable recurring workflows with owner, cadence, verification and disable path.
  • Model/reasoning policy should be role/risk based, not always maximum reasoning.

docs.title: Инструкции применения на проекте
docs.text:
1. Классифицировать задачу до старта: docs, web/front-end, backend, database, API, native/mobile, desktop, AI/eval, security, delivery/release, automation, plugin/skill, PR/review или long-running goal.
  2. Начинать с read-only inventory, если задача нетривиальная: AGENTS.md, релевантные docs, target files, existing patterns, команды проверки, sandbox/approval constraints.
  3. Для long-running/product work использовать control-plane files: REQUIREMENTS.md, PLAN.md, TEST.md, EVALS.md, RUNLOG.md.
  4. Держать durable project rules в AGENTS.md, а не в memory, private chat или повторяемых prompts.
  5. Обновлять AGENTS.md только после понятной повторяющейся ошибки, recurring PR feedback или устойчивого workflow rule.
  6. Использовать skills, когда workflow имеет clear trigger, inputs, outputs, steps, verification и failure modes.
  7. Создавать skill только из proven manual workflow: successful run, known failure/risk и проверяемый output.
  8. Упаковывать plugin, когда стабильный workflow надо распространять, ставить через marketplace или bundle-ить со skills, MCP, hooks, apps/assets.
  9. Считать MCP capability boundary: tools/resources/prompts, trust level, data boundary, side effects, approvals и secrets handling должны быть явными.
  10. Считать hooks executable policy: hook event, matcher, command, trust decision, failure behavior и disable path должны быть задокументированы до activation.
  11. Использовать subagents только для независимых или specialist задач. Каждый subagent получает fresh-context task packet.
  12. Не давать subagents пересекающиеся ownership зоны. Если файлы или contracts пересекаются, использовать sequential work с review checkpoint.
  13. Для parallel work использовать worktrees или явный ownership map: owned files, forbidden files, merge path, evidence output.
  14. Держать sandbox и approvals tight by default. External writes, GitHub/CI, publishing, production data, network-heavy work, hook activation и MCP side effects требуют explicit approval.
  15. Выбирать runtime по задаче: Codex App/IDE для ambiguity и steering, CLI для local engineering, codex exec для stable non-interactive jobs, GitHub Action для PR/CI, MCP для external tools, Agents SDK для code-owned agent apps, automation для stable recurring workflows.
  16. Задавать model/reasoning policy по риску: stronger reasoning для architecture, review, debugging, security, eval judging, migrations и ambiguous multi-step work; lower reasoning для bounded read-only или mechanical tasks.
  17. Использовать memory только как recall layer. Required rules, source policy, acceptance criteria, secrets policy и verification commands должны жить в checked-in docs.
  18. Любой completion/readiness claim должен ссылаться на current evidence: commands, checks, artifacts, runtime output, traces, screenshots, evals или explicit gap.
  19. Продвигать повторяемые workflows по цепочке: manual thread -> playbook -> skill -> plugin -> automation.
  20. Не активировать automation, пока нет manual stability evidence, owner, durable prompt, cadence, environment, verification и disable/rollback path.

docs.title: Применяемые методологии разработки
docs.text: Методология Когда применять Как выглядит в проекте Agentic delivery loop Любая нетривиальная работа Discovery -> smallest useful plan -> focused slice -> verification -> risk review -> handoff/release evidence. Control-plane docs-as-state Long-running или production work REQUIREMENTS.md, PLAN.md, TEST.md, EVALS.md, RUNLOG.md вместо состояния в чате. AGENTS.md durable rules Повторяются team/project conventions Repo layout, commands, standards, constraints, source policy и done criteria рядом с кодом. Progressive disclosure skills Workflow повторяется SKILL.md с trigger, inputs, outputs, scripts/references, verification и failure modes. Plugin packaging lifecycle Workflow нужно распространять .codex-plugin/plugin.json, bundled skills/MCP/hooks/apps/assets, owner, evals, update loop. Fresh-context handoff Нужен specialist/subagent Task packet с sources, assumptions, owned files, forbidden files, expected evidence, output schema, stop condition. Ownership-bound parallelism Можно безопасно параллелить Непересекающиеся files/subsystems, merge path, evidence output, fallback to sequential. Approval-bound capability governance Есть side effects или privileged actions Sandbox, approvals, MCP, hooks, CI, publish, production и external-write boundaries до действия. Evidence-before-completion Любой done/works/passes claim Текущие команды, artifacts, runtime evidence, traces/screenshots/evals или explicit gap. Memory hygiene Контекст повторяется между threads Memory помогает recall, но mandatory rules и secrets policy живут в checked-in docs. Automation promotion Workflow стал predictable Manual success -> skill/playbook -> candidate automation -> first-run review -> active schedule. Agent eval loop Качество agent behavior важно Baseline, one focused change, rerun eval, inspect traces/artifacts, log result, threshold. Runtime routing Есть несколько поверхностей исполнения Выбор между Codex App, IDE extension, CLI, codex exec, GitHub Action, MCP, Agents SDK, automation. Model/reasoning policy Важен cost/latency/quality tradeoff Default model/reasoning, escalation, downgrade и budget по role/workflow.

docs.title: Инструменты, артефакты и стандарты документирования
docs.text:
• AGENTS.md: durable project rules, source policy, commands, conventions, done criteria.
  • REQUIREMENTS.md: users, goals, non-goals, constraints, acceptance criteria, source constraints.
  • PLAN.md: smallest useful plan, ownership, gates, rollback, verification.
  • TEST.md: unit/integration/runtime/manual/eval checks and commands.
  • EVALS.md: subjective or long-horizon quality thresholds, datasets, judge criteria.
  • RUNLOG.md: decisions, command evidence, failures, residual risks, next action.
  • agent-task-packet.md: fresh-context packet для subagent/parallel worker.
  • handoff-contract.md: output schema, evidence fields, stop conditions.
  • worktree-ownership.md: parallel ownership map and merge boundaries.
  • skill-candidate.md: manual workflow evidence before skill creation.
  • skill-failure-log.md: trigger misses, missing inputs, unsafe actions, verification failures.
  • plugin-blueprint.md: users, bundled skills, MCP/hooks/apps, permissions, evals, owner.
  • mcp-permission-review.md: tools/resources/prompts, trust level, side effects, approval policy.
  • hook-activation-record.md: hook source, event, command, trust decision, failure behavior.
  • approval-record.md: external write or privilege escalation approval, scope, rollback.
  • automation-candidate.md: manual stability evidence, cadence, prompt, environment, verification, disable path.
  • model-reasoning-policy.md: role/workflow defaults, escalation/downgrade rules, budget.
  • context-memory-policy.md: что живет в chat, RUNLOG.md, AGENTS.md, memory и source docs.
  • agent-eval-case.md: input, expected behavior, trace/evidence, grader, threshold, failure label.
  • release-packet.md: final evidence, risks, approvals, next action for merge/release.

docs.title: Что еще включить в deep research
docs.text:
• Maturity levels: manual, repeatable, skill, plugin, automation, managed.
  • Runtime decision matrix: Codex App vs IDE extension vs CLI vs codex exec vs GitHub Action vs MCP vs Agents SDK.
  • Subagent safety policy: когда параллелить, когда запрещать, когда требовать worktree.
  • MCP permission model: read-only resources, side-effecting tools, secrets, trust level, approval policy.
  • Hook governance: activation, trust review, deterministic failure behavior, disable path.
  • Skill lifecycle: trigger tests, negative trigger tests, missing-input behavior, verification failures, failure log.
  • Plugin lifecycle: marketplace, versioning, permissions, bundled components, eval cases, owner/update loop.
  • Automation lifecycle: manual prompt test, first-run review, cadence, environment, worktree/local mode, disable/rollback.
  • Memory and context policy: что можно запоминать, что нельзя, как не хранить secrets/private context.
  • Agent evals: trace-derived datasets, tool-call correctness, handoff correctness, regression thresholds.
  • Model/reasoning policy: роль, риск, latency, cost, escalation, downgrade.

docs.title: Product-Agent OS routing
docs.text:
• project-lifecycle-orchestrator классифицирует task archetype, runtime surface и следующий lifecycle skill.
  • workspace-discovery-auditor начинает read-only и фиксирует project docs, target files, commands, patterns, risks and sandbox/approval constraints.
  • requirements-author превращает ambiguous request в users, goals, constraints, acceptance scenarios and source constraints.
  • implementation-planner блокирует plan-ready status, если нет source of truth, ownership, gates, rollback или verification.
  • agent-team-designer создает fresh-context packets, role ownership, handoff contracts and stop conditions for subagents/parallel workers.
  • test-eval-designer определяет current evidence: tests, builds, runtime checks, screenshots, traces, evals, artifacts.
  • risk-reviewer проверяет approval boundaries, unsupported claims, overlapping edits, security/data/release risks.
  • pr-release-operator собирает release/merge evidence packet and finish options.
  • learning-loop-maintainer переносит failures, repeated mistakes and improvement decisions into durable artifacts.
  • automation-promoter создает только candidate automation до manual stability evidence и explicit approval.

docs.title: Candidate readiness gates
docs.text:
• agentic_scope_classified: use-case archetype, runtime surface and task type are explicit.
  • source_of_truth_present: durable artifacts exist; chat is not the only source of truth.
  • control_plane_present: required REQUIREMENTS.md, PLAN.md, TEST.md, EVALS.md, RUNLOG.md exist for multi-slice work.
  • read_only_discovery_complete: current docs, files, commands, patterns and sandbox/approval context were inspected.
  • approval_boundary_present: external writes, privileged actions, MCP side effects, hooks, CI, release and production data have owner, approval and rollback/disable path.
  • fresh_context_handoff_present: any subagent/parallel worker has task packet with sources, assumptions, ownership, forbidden files, expected evidence and stop condition.
  • ownership_split_present: parallel files/subsystems do not overlap or fallback is sequential.
  • subagent_parallelism_safe: work is independent enough to justify subagents.
  • skill_promotion_evidence_present: skill has manual success evidence, trigger, inputs, outputs, verification and failure modes.
  • plugin_boundary_present: plugin has manifest, components, permissions, evals and owner/update loop.
  • mcp_permission_review_present: MCP capabilities, trust level, data boundary, side effects and approval policy are documented.
  • hook_activation_approval_present: hook event, matcher, command, trust decision and failure behavior are documented and approved.
  • automation_manual_stability_present: automation has manual test evidence, durable prompt, cadence, environment, owner, verification and disable path.
  • model_reasoning_policy_present: durable roles/workflows have default model/reasoning, escalation/downgrade and budget.
  • memory_policy_present: memory is recall only; mandatory rules and secrets policy live in checked-in docs.
  • agent_eval_workflow_present: agent behavior changes have baseline, eval cases, threshold, rerun command and failure labels.
  • agentic_evidence_before_completion: completion/readiness claim cites current evidence or explicit gap.

docs.title: Candidate eval fields
docs.text:
• Agentic scope and runtime surface are classified.
  • Source-of-truth artifacts exist and chat is not the only durable state.
  • Read-only discovery inspected docs, files, commands and sandbox/approval constraints.
  • Approval boundary exists for MCP, hooks, CI, release, external writes and production data.
  • Subagent packet includes sources, assumptions, owned files, forbidden files, expected evidence and stop condition.
  • Parallel work has non-overlapping ownership or sequential fallback.
  • Skill promotion has manual success evidence, trigger, inputs, outputs, verification and failure modes.
  • Plugin boundary includes manifest, bundled capabilities, permissions, eval cases and owner/update loop.
  • Automation has manual stability evidence, durable prompt, owner, cadence, verification and disable path.
  • Completion claim cites current evidence or explicit gap.

docs.title: Tooling candidates
docs.text: Tooling area Candidate Notes Durable rules AGENTS.md Project rules, commands, source policy and done criteria. Control plane REQUIREMENTS.md, PLAN.md, TEST.md, EVALS.md, RUNLOG.md Long-running product work state and evidence. Codex runtime config config.toml Model, reasoning and runtime defaults when project-owned. Handoff agent-task-packet.md, handoff-contract.md Fresh-context subagent work and expected evidence. Skills SKILL.md Repeatable workflow packaging after manual success. Plugins .codex-plugin/plugin.json Bundle skills, MCP, hooks, apps/assets and permission expectations. MCP review mcp-permission-review.md Tool/resource/prompt trust, side effects, secrets and approvals. Hooks hooks.json, hook-activation-record.md Event/matcher/command, trust decision and disable path. Automations automation.toml, automation-candidate.md Stable recurring workflow candidate and manual review evidence. Agent workflow readiness agentic-workflow-readiness.md Combined gate packet before promotion or orchestration.

docs.title: Проверки
docs.text:
• Workflow starts from classified use-case archetype and selected runtime.
  • Source-of-truth artifacts are present and current.
  • Read-only discovery inspected project docs, target files, commands and sandbox/approval context.
  • Subagent work has task packet, ownership, forbidden files, output schema and stop conditions.
  • Parallel work has explicit ownership or uses sequential fallback.
  • Skill promotion is backed by manual evidence and failure modes.
  • Plugin packaging includes manifest, bundled components, permissions, eval cases and owner/update loop.
  • MCP and hooks have capability/trust/approval review before side effects or activation.
  • Automation remains candidate-only until manual stability evidence exists.
  • Model/reasoning policy is explicit for durable agents/workflows.
  • Memory is not used as source of mandatory project truth.
  • Final claims cite current evidence.

docs.title: Failure modes
docs.text:
• Chat contains real requirements while project artifacts stay stale.
  • AGENTS.md becomes vague, obsolete or filled with one-off instructions.
  • Subagents edit overlapping files without ownership.
  • Handoffs omit source constraints, assumptions, evidence or stop conditions.
  • Skills are created from ideas without successful manual workflow evidence.
  • Plugins are packaged before permissions, evals and owner/update loop exist.
  • MCP tools are treated as safe even when they expose side effects.
  • Hooks are enabled without trust review or failure-mode documentation.
  • Automations are scheduled before prompt/tools are stable.
  • Memory stores context that should be checked into docs, or contains private/secrets material.
  • Completion is claimed from inspection-only evidence.
  • Agents SDK concepts are copied into Codex runtime docs without distinguishing runtime layers.

docs.title: Unsupported claims not adopted
docs.text:
• "Memory is project source of truth." Memory is recall only; durable rules and evidence belong in files.
  • "Subagents are automatically faster." They help only when work is independent and ownership is clear.
  • "MCP tools are safe because they are tools." MCP can expose data and side effects and needs trust review.
  • "Hooks are just convenience scripts." Hooks are executable policy and need approval, failure behavior and disable path.
  • "A repeated workflow should become automation immediately." Automation follows manual stability and first-run review.
  • "Agents SDK and Codex runtime are the same layer." Agents SDK is for code-owned agent apps; Codex App/CLI/IDE is the engineering runtime.

docs.title: Open questions for future implementation
docs.text:
• Which maturity labels should Product-Agent OS use: manual, repeatable, skill, plugin, automation, managed?
  • Should runtime routing be a single decision matrix or split by use-case archetype?
  • Which subagent tasks require worktrees by default?
  • Should MCP permission review be generated for every MCP config change or only side-effecting capabilities?
  • How should skill trigger tests and negative trigger tests be stored?
  • Which agent eval cases are enough before promoting a workflow to plugin or automation?

docs.title: Database & Data
docs.text:
Source status: official + expert reference + vendor documentation + local implementation evidence + tool-assisted

Источники: PostgreSQL Transaction Isolation, PostgreSQL Backup and Restore, PostgreSQL Constraints, PostgreSQL Indexes, PostgreSQL EXPLAIN, Liquibase core concepts, Liquibase rollback, Flyway migrations, dbt data tests, dbt model contracts, Great Expectations, OpenLineage, NIST Privacy Framework, Evolutionary Database Design, Prisma expand/contract pattern, Context7 research, research dossier.

docs.title: Deep research цель
docs.text:
Database & Data слой описывает schema ownership, migrations, constraints, indexes, transactions, backfills, data quality, privacy classification, retention, lineage, backup/restore and production data access.

Главный принцип: data change нельзя считать завершенным, если понятен SQL или ORM diff, но не понятны production impact, rollback/compensation, backup/restore path, data quality checks, privacy boundary and performance evidence.

docs.title: Поддержанные факты
docs.text:
• PostgreSQL transaction isolation documentation describes Read Committed, Repeatable Read and Serializable behavior, including serialization failure retry requirements for stronger isolation levels.
  • PostgreSQL constraints documentation defines integrity mechanisms such as check, not-null, unique, primary key, foreign key and exclusion constraints.
  • PostgreSQL indexes and EXPLAIN documentation support performance review through index design and query-plan evidence. EXPLAIN ANALYZE executes the statement, so write statements require transaction/rollback care.
  • PostgreSQL backup and restore documentation separates SQL dump and file-system-level backup approaches; production database work needs restore evidence, not only "backups exist".
  • Liquibase documents changelogs as ordered changesets tracked in DATABASECHANGELOG, and supports rollback definitions, preconditions, contexts and labels.
  • Flyway documents version-controlled migrations, versioned and repeatable migration concepts, dry-run/deployment reports and schema history.
  • dbt data tests are SQL assertions that return failing rows; zero failing rows means the assertion passes. dbt model contracts define and enforce model column names and data types.
  • Great Expectations defines executable Expectations for completeness, schema, uniqueness, validity, volume and custom SQL checks.
  • OpenLineage defines an open standard around dataset, job and run entities for data lineage.
  • NIST Privacy Framework supports privacy requirements, profiles, SDLC alignment and data-processing ecosystem risk management.
  • Evolutionary Database Design describes small version-controlled migration scripts, application changes in CI/deployment pipelines and transition phases for destructive changes.
  • Expand/contract migration introduces new structures in parallel, updates writes, backfills, validates, switches reads/writes and removes old structures after compatibility.

docs.title: Assumptions
docs.text:
• Product-Agent OS should not mandate PostgreSQL, Liquibase, Flyway, dbt, Great Expectations or OpenLineage. These provide vocabulary and candidate artifacts; actual tools come from project inventory.
  • Data work is risky when it touches production data, destructive changes, sensitive fields, external consumers, analytics, AI/RAG sources, public APIs or high-volume backfills.
  • Migration rollback can be reversible, compensating or irreversible. It is unsafe to call a destructive migration rollback-safe without evidence.
  • Manual SQL can be operational evidence, but it cannot be the only durable record for schema/data changes.
  • Production data must not appear in docs, prompts, examples, fixtures or templates.
  • Data quality checks must be repeatable. Ad hoc SQL in a chat thread is not enough for a long-lived project gate.

docs.title: Инструкции применения на проекте
docs.text:
1. Классифицируйте работу: schema change, data migration, backfill, retention/deletion, data quality, query/index performance, analytics model, lineage, backup/restore or production data access.
  2. Назовите database engine, environment, owner, data domain and schema/migration source of truth.
  3. Зафиксируйте, затрагивает ли change production data, PII/sensitive fields, external consumers, analytics, AI/RAG sources or public APIs.
  4. Для любого schema/backfill/retention change создайте database-migration-plan.md before implementation.
  5. Держите migrations small, ordered, version-controlled and repeatable; manual production SQL не должен быть единственным record.
  6. Для live/shared systems применяйте expand/contract или другой compatibility-preserving rollout before destructive changes.
  7. Для multi-step writes/backfills опишите transaction boundary, isolation assumptions, lock impact, retry behavior and idempotency.
  8. Для constraints and indexes опишите invariant/query, deployment impact and verification evidence.
  9. Для performance-sensitive changes приложите query plan evidence and expected runtime/lock budget.
  10. Для backfills опишите batch size, resume key, throttling, validation counts, observability and abort behavior.
  11. Классифицируйте rollback как reversible, compensating or irreversible. Irreversible change требует owner acceptance.
  12. Для production data заранее подтвердите backup/restore path and restore evidence.
  13. Классифицируйте PII/sensitive fields до docs, prompts, fixtures and examples. Production data cannot be copied into examples.
  14. Добавьте executable data quality checks для primary keys, nullability, relationships, accepted values, counts and critical business assertions.
  15. Для analytics or AI/RAG pipelines опишите data contracts and lineage или explicit gap.
  16. Для production data access требуйте approval, least privilege, audit trail and no-secrets/no-customer-data evidence.

docs.title: Применяемые методологии разработки
docs.text: Методология Когда применять Как выглядит в проекте Evolutionary Database Design Product schema evolves continuously Small versioned migrations, application changes and tests move together through CI/CD. Migration-first planning Schema, backfill or retention change database-migration-plan.md exists before execution. Expand/contract migration Live systems, shared DB, public consumers, destructive changes Add new structure, dual-write/backfill, switch reads/writes, remove old structure after compatibility window. Database DevOps / migrations-as-code Team-owned DB changes Migrations are versioned, reviewed, repeatable and automated. Data integrity by constraint Relational correctness matters Constraints, keys and indexes are explicit design artifacts. Transaction and concurrency design Multi-step writes, financial/accounting/state workflows Isolation level, locks, retries and idempotency are documented. Data quality gates Critical product, analytics or AI/RAG data Executable assertions validate keys, nulls, relationships, counts, drift and business rules. Data contracts Data model has consumers Columns, types, semantics, compatibility and owner are explicit. Privacy-by-design PII/sensitive/regulated data Classification, minimization, retention, deletion and access boundary are captured early. Backup/restore-first change management Production or irreversible data work Restore path and restore drill evidence exist before risky execution. Lineage-aware data operations Analytics, reporting, ML/RAG, cross-system movement Dataset/job/run lineage is captured or marked as a gap. Performance-by-design Indexes, heavy queries, high-volume backfills Query plan, lock/runtime budget and index impact are reviewed. Production data access control Agent/developer touches prod data Approval, least privilege, audit trail and no-secrets/no-customer-data policy are enforced.

docs.title: Инструменты, артефакты и стандарты документирования
docs.text: Артефакт Зачем нужен Практический формат database-inventory.md Databases, owners, environments, engines, connection boundaries and data domains. Product-Agent OS template. database-dictionary.md Tables/collections, fields, types, business meaning, owner, sensitivity and retention. DBML, dbdocs, SchemaSpy, Markdown. Schema source of truth Machine-readable schema or migration history used for review. Migrations, DBML, ORM schema, SQL DDL. database-migration-plan.md Change intent, ordered steps, dry-run, validation, rollout, rollback/compensation and approvals. Migration plan. database-expand-contract-record.md Parallel structures, dual-write/read switch, cleanup and compatibility window. ADR or migration record. database-backfill-runbook.md Batching, idempotency, resume, throttling, progress, validation and abort behavior. Runbook. database-rollback-feasibility.md Reversible, compensating or irreversible classification with owner acceptance. Rollback record. database-backup-restore-evidence.md Backup source, restore drill, restore target, RPO/RTO and verification result. DB/platform docs and runbook. database-data-classification-matrix.md PII/sensitive fields, legal basis, access boundary, retention and deletion behavior. NIST Privacy Framework profile. database-data-quality-checks.md Executable checks for keys, nulls, relationships, accepted values, counts and drift. dbt tests, Great Expectations, SQL checks. database-data-contract.md Consumer-facing data model columns, types, meaning, compatibility and owner. dbt model contracts or Markdown. database-lineage-map.md Datasets, jobs, runs, sources, sinks and owners. OpenLineage or data catalog. database-query-performance-review.md Query plan, index choices, cardinality, lock impact and expected runtime.
