docs.text:
The plugin must not blur implemented workflows with partial or pending coverage.

Status Meaning Modes done Route, workflow template, artifact template or explicit artifact, behavioral eval coverage and verification evidence exist. first-run-intake, bug_rescue, greenfield_idea, complex_system_acceleration, pr_review, legacy_onboarding, api_migration, ai_eval_regression, native_mobile_feature, desktop_local_first, data_migration, security_sensitive_change, ci_stabilization, release_packaging. done methodology gate Reusable behavior exists with template, skill, behavioral eval and fixture coverage. no-placeholder planning, generalized two-stage review, fresh-context handoff, acceptance scenarios, conditional DDD domain modeling, bounded-context-to-architecture traceability, ubiquitous language traceability, conditional FSD structure routing, metric hardening, evidence-before-completion, docs tooling selector with docs_as_code_impact statuses, conditional readiness gates with readiness_statuses. done documentation Operator-facing docs exist for route selection, eval behavior and Codex-only packaging scope. docs/product-agent-os/scenarios.md, behavioral-evals.md, codex-compatibility.md. done eval runner Deterministic transcript/session replay exists for synthetic or redacted sessions without external model calls. run_transcript_eval.py, product_agent_os/transcript_evals.py, product-agent-os-synthetic-sessions.json. partial Some reusable behavior exists, but the full planned contract is not complete. lifecycle trigger hardening.

docs.title: Generated project files
docs.text: File Owner Purpose Update rule AGENTS.md Orchestrator + user approval Durable project rules Only stable rules that apply across future tasks REQUIREMENTS.md Product Manager role Goal, users, scope, non-goals, acceptance criteria When product intent changes PLAN.md Architect role Decomposition, ownership, sequence, no-placeholder plan quality, risks, rollback Before implementation and when plan changes TEST.md Tester role Deterministic checks, manual QA, visual QA Before quality gate EVALS.md Eval designer role Subjective checks, LLM-as-judge rubric, thresholds For AI, UX, docs, long-horizon or subjective outputs RUNLOG.md Orchestrator Iterations, scores, decisions, evidence, handoff summary Every meaningful lifecycle step .codex/config.toml Orchestrator + user approval Project-scoped Codex defaults Staged; never overwrite blindly .codex/agents/*.toml Agent team designer Project-scoped custom agents Generated from role cards and profile .codex/hooks/* Hook author Deterministic guardrails and evidence capture Enabled only after validation .codex/workflows/*.md Workflow builder Reusable task packets Created from stable routes .codex/evals/*.json Eval designer Fixture evals and expected behaviors Updated from failure log

docs.title: System file update policy
docs.text:
Plugin updates system files through merge-safe sections.

Generated sections use stable markers:

<!-- product-agent-os:start <section-id> -->
...
<!-- product-agent-os:end <section-id> -->

Rules:

  • User-authored content outside managed sections is preserved.
  • Existing managed sections are updated only after a new plan is shown.
  • If a file exists without markers, plugin proposes an append or separate companion file.
  • If merge is ambiguous, plugin stops and returns a conflict report.
  • Source-backed claims require official source or experiment label.

docs.title: Context and information overflow policy
docs.text:
Plugin uses layered context.

Layer Contents Loaded when Hot AGENTS.md, active REQUIREMENTS.md, active PLAN.md, current task packet Every lifecycle step Warm TEST.md, EVALS.md, latest RUNLOG.md summary, active role cards Planning, build, review, eval Cold Archived runlogs, historical eval reports, old decisions, source cards Only when referenced External Official docs, Context7, MCP sources When freshness or library detail matters

Compaction rules:

  • RUNLOG.md keeps current best, latest iterations and handoff summary.
  • Older iterations move to docs/runlogs/archive/YYYY-MM-DD-<topic>.md or .codex/runlogs/archive/ depending on project convention.
  • Raw subagent logs are summarized into evidence, decisions and risks.
  • AGENTS.md stays concise; long guidance moves to docs or .codex/workflows/.
  • Skill bodies stay short; long details live in references/.
  • Memory is never used as citation source; important facts are retrieved or read from checked-in docs.

docs.title: Skills
docs.text:
Skill Job Required inputs Output Verification project-lifecycle-orchestrator Route the lifecycle and enforce gates User goal, workspace audit, current state Next action packet State transition is valid workspace-discovery-auditor Read-only project audit Workspace path WorkspaceAudit No writes; detected files exist requirements-author Create/update requirements Goal, users, constraints REQUIREMENTS.md Acceptance criteria present implementation-planner Produce executable plan Requirements, audit PLAN.md Ownership, tests, rollback named agent-team-designer Generate roles and custom agents Plan, complexity profile .codex/agents/*.toml TOML validates test-eval-designer Define tests and evals Requirements, plan, stack TEST.md, EVALS.md Thresholds and artifacts explicit risk-reviewer Review diff and project risk Diff, plan, tests Findings by severity No unsupported claims pr-release-operator Prepare PR/release packet Diff, checks, runlog PR body, release notes, rollback Evidence included learning-loop-maintainer Capture reusable lessons Final result, failures AGENTS.md suggestions, skill candidates Lessons classified automation-promoter Propose recurring runs Stable workflow, failure log Automation candidate packet Manual success history exists

Each skill must define trigger, boundaries, inputs, outputs, failure modes and final response contract.

Track 3 workflow templates cover task-packet jobs that are not packaged as SKILL.md bundles in the current implementation:

  • source-context-pack.md covers official-source and Context7 research packets.
  • worktree-ownership.md covers parallel ownership and worktree maps.
  • build-slice.md covers one approved implementation slice with verification evidence.
  • development-standards.md covers product hypothesis, architecture boundary, test-first/eval-first verification, bounded agent implementation, review and release measurement.
  • documentation-system.md covers docs-as-code source-of-truth artifacts for architecture, API, UI, code reference, database and release docs.

Track 7 artifact templates cover methodology outputs that are too concrete to leave as prose-only workflow advice:

  • adr.md for architecture decision records with context, decision, consequences, verification and rollback.
  • architecture-overview.md for C4-style system/container notes, quality attributes and architecture risks.
  • domain-modeling.md for bounded context, ubiquitous language traceability, aggregates, invariants, domain events, context maps and bounded-context-to-architecture traceability.
  • metric-spec.md for product hypothesis, baseline, North Star or primary value metric, input metric, counter-metric, guardrail metrics, proxy metric risk, privacy classification, retention period, data minimization, owner signoff, Goodhart checks and post-release review.
  • api-contract-review.md for OpenAPI, AsyncAPI, auth, errors, examples, compatibility and generated docs checks.
  • component-card.md for UI states, accessibility, public API and Storybook documentation.
  • database-dictionary.md for table meaning, sensitive fields, retention, migration history and schema verification.

Track 8 completed workflow templates cover scenario-specific first actions:

  • first-run-intake.md keeps first launch small for empty, broken, existing control-plane and complex system starts: mode, confidence, next smallest action, minimum artifacts, approval boundary and evidence gaps.
  • bug-rescue.md and bug-rescue-report.md enforce reproduction and root-cause evidence before fixes.
  • greenfield-idea-to-plan.md and greenfield-idea-brief.md block scaffold before selected direction and approval.
  • complex-system-acceleration.md and integration-catalog.md force ownership split, release gates and integration risk mapping before parallel work.
  • pr-review-readiness.md and pr-risk-review.md provide read-only changed-file review with spec compliance before quality/risk verdict.
  • review-slice.md, RUNLOG.md, pr-risk-review.md and risk-reviewer generalize that two-stage review to risky public-contract, migration, security-sensitive, data migration, release packaging and parallel slices.
  • agent-team-designer, handoff-contract.md, agent-task-packet.md and worktree-ownership.md require fresh-context handoff before subagent or parallel worker execution.
  • acceptance-scenarios.md, generated REQUIREMENTS/TEST/EVALS, development-standards.md, requirements-author, implementation-planner, test-eval-designer, project-readiness.json and behavioral-workflows.json require ATDD/BDD traceability before behavior changes: requirement -> scenario -> check -> evidence owner, Given/When/Then or equivalent behavior format, business rule, edge case, non-goal, explicit gap and evidence owner.
  • domain-modeling.md, architecture-overview.md, project-readiness.json, discovery.py, implementation-planner and fixture eval require conditional DDD domain modeling for complex backend/workflow/enterprise/data-heavy/multi-service/multi-context work, plus bounded_context_architecture_boundary_trace from every bounded context to an architecture boundary or accepted gap and ubiquitous_language_traceability from each domain term to requirement/source plus API/event/contract, UI label, code module or owner; simple CRUD or simple MVP work can mark DDD as not applicable or accepted gap.
  • component-card.md, development-standards.md, project-readiness.json, discovery.py, workspace-discovery-auditor and implementation-planner support optional fsd_structure for applicable web UI/component work; backend, native, simple CRUD and simple MVP work can mark Feature-Sliced Design as not applicable or accepted gap.
  • metric-spec.md, release-packet.md, generated REQUIREMENTS/PLAN/TEST/EVALS/RUNLOG, project-readiness.json, lifecycle skills and fixture eval require metric_hardening_when_product_behavior_changes for product behavior changes; product success claims need counter-metric, guardrail, qualitative review and post-release review evidence, not a single proxy metric.
  • docs-tooling-decision.md, documentation-system.md, generated PLAN/TEST/EVALS/RUNLOG, project-readiness.json, lifecycle skills, discovery.py and fixture eval require docs_tooling_selector and docs_as_code_impact statuses for stack-aware docs tooling without forced installs or unapproved external activation.
  • project-readiness.json, generated AGENTS/PLAN/TEST/EVALS/RUNLOG, lifecycle skills and fixture eval require conditional readiness gates with readiness_statuses, applicability, required evidence, owner and residual risk; detection alone can only support present_unverified.
  • legacy-onboarding.md and onboarding-map.md keep old or undocumented repos in read-only orientation with present_unverified claims before refactor.
  • api-migration.md and migration-plan.md route HTTP API and event contract changes through OpenAPI/AsyncAPI, consumers, generated clients, backwards compatibility, deprecation, rollout, release impact and owner review gates before implementation or release.

These workflow templates may be promoted to skills later only after manual success evidence and failure logs justify that promotion.

docs.title: Agent team
docs.text:
Generated custom agents are project-scoped in .codex/agents/.

Agent Purpose Default reasoning Default sandbox product-manager Requirements, scope, acceptance criteria medium / high read-only architect Decomposition, ownership, risks, rollback high / xhigh read-only explorer Read-heavy codebase and docs mapping low / medium read-only builder Scoped implementation medium / high workspace-write tester Test gaps, verification commands, eval reports medium / high workspace-write reviewer Correctness, security, regressions, missing tests high / xhigh read-only docs-maintainer Docs, changelog, release notes low / medium workspace-write release-operator PR packet, rollout notes, automation candidates medium / high read-only by default

Every role card includes:

All agent and skill handoffs use structured payloads.

If a handoff lacks goal, constraints, files_touched/files_proposed, or verification_evidence, the orchestrator rejects it and asks for a corrected handoff.

docs.title: Safety and approvals
docs.text:
Default project config proposal:

approval_policy = "on-request"
sandbox_mode = "workspace-write"
allow_login_shell = false

For read-only planning and review:

approval_policy = "untrusted"
sandbox_mode = "read-only"
allow_login_shell = false

Granular approval policy proposal for governed projects:

approval_policy = { granular = {
  sandbox_approval = true,
  rules = true,
  mcp_elicitations = true,
  request_permissions = false,
  skill_approval = true
} }

Approval required for:

  • external writes;
  • destructive commands;
  • permission changes;
  • global config changes;
  • credential, deployment, billing, database, auth, migration, production operation or source-of-truth update;
  • starting automation;
  • enabling broad network access.

Forbidden by default:

  • storing secrets in docs, prompts, memory, fixtures or examples;
  • editing generated/vendor/build artifacts unless explicitly allowed;
  • changing global Codex config;
  • creating recurring automation without manual stability evidence;
  • claiming checks passed without running them in the current lifecycle step.

docs.title: Hooks and rules
docs.text:
Plugin provides hook templates, not silent enforcement.

Hook Event Purpose Blocking session_start_context.py SessionStart Summarize active control-plane state no pre_tool_use_policy.py PreToolUse Detect destructive commands and forbidden paths yes for high-risk matches permission_request_summary.py PermissionRequest Explain why approval is requested no post_tool_use_evidence.py PostToolUse Append command evidence to active runlog buffer no stop_runlog_reminder.py Stop Remind to update RUNLOG.md when evidence exists no by default

Rules must be narrow, auditable and aligned with sandbox/approvals. Hooks must not store secrets.

docs.title: Runtime selection
docs.text:
Project need Runtime decision First-time project setup Codex App or CLI interactive One prepared task packet codex exec Large feature App/CLI with worktree per coherent unit PR review GitHub integration or Codex review flow Recurring stable check Codex automation or GitHub Action Programmable multi-agent workflow Agents SDK + Codex MCP GUI-only task Computer Use only when no dedicated tool exists

Runtime choice is stored in PLAN.md or RUNLOG.md, not hidden in chat.

docs.title: Context7 and source policy
docs.text:
The Track 3 source-context-pack.md workflow template records Context7 usage for library and official documentation retrieval when current docs are required.

Rules:

  • Official status applies only when underlying source is official.
  • Context7 results from community repositories are intake material until verified.
  • OpenAI product claims prefer official OpenAI docs.
  • Source-backed claims update source registry or project source notes.
  • Community tricks are stored as insights with trust_level and verification_status.

docs.title: Evals and verification
docs.text:
Plugin has its own eval suite and creates project evals.

Plugin fixture evals:

Case Fixture Expected behavior Happy path node-app Creates control plane, agents, test plan, runlog, no unsafe write Existing files existing-codex-config Preserves user content and proposes managed sections Missing tests empty-repo Names test gap and does not invent passing checks Unsafe write Any fixture Stages draft and requests approval Monorepo monorepo Creates nested ownership and avoids overlapping write scopes Source conflict docs-repo Marks conflict and requests verification Failed verification python-app Reports failure evidence and does not claim completion

Project evals:

  • deterministic checks: tests, lint, build, docs checks, schema validation;
  • LLM-as-judge checks: usefulness, clarity, source fidelity, handoff completeness;
  • artifact inspection: screenshots, generated reports, deployment previews, PR body;
  • regression checks: previous passing scenarios remain passing.

Stopping rule example:

quality_gate:
  deterministic_checks_required: true
  no_blocking_review_findings: true
  llm_judge_average_min: 0.90
  no_unresolved_source_conflicts: true
  rollback_note_required_for_risky_change: true

docs.title: Automation promotion
docs.text:
automation-promoter can only produce an automation candidate when all conditions are true:

  • workflow ran manually at least twice or has equivalent fixture evidence;
  • inputs and outputs are stable;
  • failure modes are known;
  • write policy is explicit;
  • verification is runnable;
  • owner and cadence are named;
  • external writes are staged or approval-gated.

Automation candidate packet:

automation_candidate:
  name: ""
  purpose: ""
  trigger_or_cadence: ""
  required_inputs: []
  write_policy: "read_only | draft_only | approved_write"
  verification: []
  failure_modes: []
  owner: ""
  rollback_or_disable: ""

docs.title: Optional Agents SDK runner
docs.text:
For advanced teams, plugin may include a companion runner design under scripts/agents_sdk_runner/.

Architecture:

  • Manager Agent owns lifecycle state and final output.
  • Specialist agents are tools or handoff targets.
  • Codex MCP performs workspace work with explicit sandbox and approval policy.
  • Guardrails validate handoff completeness, tool boundary, source fidelity and no secret retention.
  • Sessions preserve conversation continuity.
  • Tracing records tools, handoffs, latency and failures.

This runner is optional because many projects need Codex plugin + skills + .codex/ config before they need a programmable agent app.

docs.title: Failure modes
docs.text: Failure Detection Required behavior Scope too broad Requirements span unrelated systems Split into phases and ask for priority Existing project rules conflict AGENTS.md and proposed config disagree Stop and show conflict Context overflow Runlog or docs too large Build context pack and archive old details Agent edits outside ownership Diff touches unassigned files Stop or request approval Verification missing No test/eval command known Create test gap and avoid success claim Hook false positive Valid command blocked Log rule, propose narrower rule Automation too early No manual success history Keep as candidate, not active automation Source drift Official docs changed Mark freshness risk and refresh source Secret risk Potential credential detected Stop, redact, do not store

docs.title: Acceptance criteria
docs.text:
Plugin is production-ready when:

  • It can initialize existing and greenfield projects without overwriting user content.
  • It produces a clear infrastructure plan before writing.
  • It routes skills by lifecycle state and complexity profile.
  • It creates valid control-plane files and project-scoped .codex/ assets.
  • It supports full project lifecycle from idea to PR/release packet.
  • It logs evidence and decisions in RUNLOG.md.
  • It handles context overflow through hot/warm/cold context layers and archive policy.
  • It enforces approval gates for risky writes.
  • It has fixture evals for happy path, existing config, missing tests, unsafe write, monorepo, source conflict and failed verification.
  • It does not create active automations without stability evidence.
  • It documents residual risks and next action after every run.

docs.title: Implementation handoff
docs.text:
Implementation should be split into four build tracks:

  1. Plugin core and contracts - manifest, schemas, detection scripts, validators, fixture harness.
  2. Lifecycle skills - orchestrator and each lifecycle stage skill with concise SKILL.md, references and output contracts.
  3. Generated project infrastructure - control-plane templates, .codex/agents/*.toml, hooks, workflow packets and eval templates.
  4. Production hardening - fixture evals, safe merge behavior, source policy checks, automation promotion gates and optional Agents SDK runner.

Each track must have deterministic validation before the plugin is used on real customer projects.

docs.text: Роль Основной input Output Не делает Product Manager User request, business goal REQUIREMENTS.md, acceptance criteria Не пишет production code Architect Requirements, codebase map PLAN.md, component boundaries Не расширяет scope Builder Plan, ownership Code diff, tests Не меняет чужой write scope Tester Requirements, diff, test plan Test gaps, failing cases, eval report Не принимает неподтвержденные claims Reviewer Diff, risk model Findings ordered by severity Не переписывает без запроса Docs Maintainer Diff, sources, decisions Docs, release notes Не смешивает official/community Release Operator Verification, PR body PR, changelog, rollout notes Не пропускает failing checks

docs.title: Model and reasoning profile
docs.text:
Каждая роль должна иметь execution profile. Это особенно важно для programmable Agents SDK workflows и Codex custom agents, где модель и reasoning могут задаваться явно.

Роль Model policy Reasoning effort Escalation rule Product Manager gpt-5.5 или project default medium / high Поднять до high, если requirements конфликтуют или нужно выбрать tradeoff Architect gpt-5.5 high / xhigh xhigh для multi-system architecture, migrations, deep debugging Builder project default; gpt-5.4-mini для малых scoped edits medium / high high, если меняются shared contracts или несколько модулей Explorer gpt-5.4-mini или project default low / medium medium, если нужно синтезировать найденные зависимости Tester project default medium high, если failure non-deterministic или eval-driven Reviewer gpt-5.5 high xhigh, если review затрагивает security, data loss, concurrency, auth Docs Maintainer project default low / medium medium, если нужно сверять несколько official sources Release Operator project default medium high, если rollout irreversible или approvals неоднозначны

Минимальная role card:

role: "Architect"
owns: "Architecture, decomposition, risk analysis"
model_policy:
  model: "gpt-5.5"
  reasoning_effort: "high"
  cost_latency_budget: "quality-first"
  inherit_from_parent_when_unspecified: true
  override_allowed_by:
    - "run-level workflow config"
    - "human approval"
  escalation_rules:
    - "Use xhigh for multi-system migration or ambiguous architecture."
    - "Use medium for bounded implementation planning."
handoff:
  inputs: "REQUIREMENTS.md, codebase map, constraints"
  outputs: "PLAN.md, risks, open questions, verification strategy"

Project default должен жить в PLAN.md или project-scoped agent config. Durable rules о том, когда повышать reasoning, можно хранить в AGENTS.md; одноразовые runtime overrides лучше фиксировать в RUNLOG.md.

docs.title: Manager pattern
docs.text:
Для product delivery default - Manager pattern:

  • Manager держит цель, scope и gates.
  • Specialist agents выполняют bounded tasks.
  • Verifier/Reviewer проверяет результат.
  • Manager публикует итог и решает, что переносить в docs/skills.
flowchart TD
    M["Manager"] --> PM["Product spec"]
    M --> A["Architecture plan"]
    M --> B["Builder"]
    M --> T["Tester"]
    M --> R["Reviewer"]
    M --> D["Docs maintainer"]
    PM --> M
    A --> M
    B --> M
    T --> M
    R --> M
    D --> M

docs.title: Handoff rule
docs.text:
Каждая роль должна возвращать не только output, но и:

  • sources used;
  • assumptions;
  • files touched or proposed;
  • verification evidence;
  • open risks;
  • recommended next role.

docs.title: Product-Agent OS plugin

docs.title: Executive overview
docs.text:
Product-Agent OS plugin - локальный Codex plugin для проектов, где Codex App, CLI, IDE extension, subagents, skills, AGENTS.md, hooks, evals и automation candidates должны работать как управляемая delivery-система. Операторский маршрут сейчас такой: source docs -> registry -> docs tests -> check_docs.py -> strict MkDocs -> optional full closure, а live/runtime действия остаются approval-bound.

Нужно понять Основная страница Как читать generated graph и cockpit Project Code Graph Где проходит live runtime/provider/mutation boundary Live Runtime Governance Когда можно переходить к реальному testing Approval-Bound Real Testing Как проверять и модернизировать agents/skills Agent-Skill Modernization Loop Какие локальные команды есть у plugin CLI Reference Какие JSON/HTML/ledger artifacts считаются evidence Artifact Contracts Как закрывать Batch 34 и передавать Batch 35 Packaging And Closure

docs.title: Current operating boundary
docs.text: Surface Разрешено без нового approval Запрещено без отдельного explicit approval Static project graph Read-only scan, staged graph/cockpit, bounded query packets. Treat generated graph as source of truth or mutate target files from graph evidence alone. Local runtime Validate disabled-by-default runtime contract and graph-only fallback. Start live server, expose public routes or add write endpoints. Provider retrieval Stage provider gate/eval contracts and threshold fallback. Perform live external model/API calls or provider calls. Human review and mutation Stage review ledger, diff preview and dry-run mutation plan. Mutate canonical graph without accepted owner decision and rollback proof. Audit and real testing Stage audit/security/observability/readiness packets. Run browser automation, provider pilots, canonical mutation pilots or git release actions.

docs.title: Task 22 final documentation sync closure
docs.text:
Task 22 final documentation sync closure фиксирует Product-Agent OS full stack как рабочий путь для реальных проектов: inspect workspace, отделить prompt intent от workspace evidence, stage infrastructure, получить approved merge, пройти Codex-only runtime routing, применить conditional methodology gates и потребовать evidence before completion.

Tracks 1-9 are implementation provenance, а не основной пользовательский сценарий. Для оператора путь выглядит так: read-only audit -> staged proposal -> approval -> bounded implementation -> checks/evals -> review -> release or learning packet. История Track 1-9 объясняет, откуда появились package contracts, lifecycle skills, generated infrastructure, hardening, runtime runner, engineering standards, scenario workflows и methodology intelligence. Источники: Codex plugins, Build plugins, Agent Skills, Subagents, AGENTS.md, Codex hooks, Agent approvals and security, Codex workflows, Product-Agent Workflows.

product-agent-os - локальный Codex plugin для проектов, где Codex App, CLI, IDE extension, subagents, skills, AGENTS.md, hooks, evals и automation candidates должны работать как управляемая система delivery, а не как набор разовых prompts.

Плагин не заменяет владельца продукта и не включает автономные изменения сам по себе. Его задача - превратить workspace в управляемый lifecycle: read-only audit, требования, план, team ownership, staged infrastructure, проверки, review, release packet, learning loop и только затем automation candidate. Новый слой Engineering standards layer добавляет product hypothesis, architecture boundary, test-first/eval-first gates, docs-as-code, release measurement, discovery signals и concrete artifact templates как обязательные элементы зрелой разработки.

docs.title: Какие боли решает
docs.text: Боль Что делает plugin Длинная Codex-сессия теряет контекст Выносит цель, план, проверки и решения в control-plane files Требования живут только в чате Создает REQUIREMENTS.md с scope, non-goals и acceptance criteria Планирование смешивается с implementation Требует PLAN.md, ownership, verification и rollback до build slice Subagents работают без границ Проектирует роли через ownership, handoff artifacts и stop conditions Проверки называются задним числом Разделяет deterministic checks в TEST.md и quality gates в EVALS.md Агент пишет код без инженерной методологии Добавляет product hypothesis, architecture boundary, test/eval-first path, docs impact и measurement Проектные правила размазаны по memory Переносит durable rules в AGENTS.md, а текущие решения в RUNLOG.md Hooks и automations включаются слишком рано Ставит staged-first и candidate-only boundary до ручного approval Невозможно доказать, что работа verified Требует evidence: команды, fixture evals, source policy и review findings

docs.title: Кому подходит
docs.text: Сценарий Польза Solo developer Быстро структурировать feature и не потерять acceptance criteria Product engineer Вести работу от идеи до PR packet через проверяемые artifacts Engineering team Разделить worktrees, roles и write scopes без конфликтов AI product team Добавить eval-driven loop и source/context policy Governed workspace Сохранить approvals, staged writes, rollback и audit trail

docs.title: Основной lifecycle
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    A["Idea"] --> B["Workspace audit"]
    B --> C["REQUIREMENTS.md"]
    C --> D["PLAN.md"]
    D --> E["Agent team"]
    E --> F["Build slice"]
    F --> G["TEST.md / EVALS.md"]
    G --> H["Review"]
    H --> I["PR or release packet"]
    I --> J["RUNLOG.md learning"]
    J --> K["Automation candidate"]

Plugin держит lifecycle последовательным. Он не должен перескакивать из uninitialized сразу в build_active: сначала нужны context, requirements, plan, ownership и quality gates.

docs.title: Текущий Track 8 статус
docs.text:
Новый план различает готовые workflows, done methodology gates, partial methodology gates и pending сценарии:

Уровень Что это означает Сценарии done Есть route, staged workflow/artifact templates, behavioral evals и текущая verification evidence. first-run intake, bug rescue, greenfield idea, complex system acceleration, PR review, legacy onboarding, API migration, AI/RAG eval regression, native/mobile, desktop local-first, data migration, security-sensitive change, CI stabilization, release packaging. done methodology gate Есть reusable gate, templates, behavioral eval и fixture coverage. no-placeholder planning, generalized two-stage review, fresh-context handoff, acceptance scenarios, conditional DDD domain modeling, bounded-context-to-architecture traceability, ubiquitous language traceability, conditional FSD structure routing, metric hardening, evidence-before-completion, docs tooling selector, conditional readiness statuses. partial Есть часть системного поведения, но не весь planned contract. lifecycle trigger hardening.

docs.title: Границы
docs.text:
• Plugin работает внутри Codex. Он не требует отдельного OpenAI API key и не запускает standalone Agents SDK runner.
  • Infrastructure generation is staged-first: dry-run or staging directory before any target workspace write.
  • Hooks are packaged as templates and examples; they are not silently activated.
  • Automation artifacts are candidate-only until manual workflow is stable and explicitly approved.
  • Secrets, private customer data, raw private chat logs and local absolute paths must not попадать в docs, fixtures, prompts, memory or templates.

docs.title: Куда идти дальше
docs.text:

  • Engineering standards layer - как plugin внедряет DDD/FSD/TDD/ADD, docs-as-code и eval-driven quality без превращения их в dogma.
  • Methodology intelligence - read-only audit, Delivery Map, recommendations, owner questions and staged artifact boundary for Track 9.
  • Scenarios and usage modes - first response, minimum artifacts, approval boundary and verification gates for Track 8 scenarios.
  • Behavioral evals - expected behavior, forbidden behavior, fixture eval and transcript/session replay.
  • Codex compatibility - Codex App, CLI, IDE extension, .codex-plugin, skills, MCP and staged hooks support boundary.
  • Диаграммы и принципы работы - state routing, staged-first merge, approval gates and runtime runner flow.
  • Product-Agent Workflows - общий operating model без привязки к plugin package.

docs.title: Agent/skill modernization loop
docs.text: Source status: official + experiment

docs.title: Назначение
docs.text:
Эта страница описывает Task 24 agent_skill_metrics_loop для Product-Agent OS: локальный, read-only контур оценки agents, subagents, skills, prompt/policy packs, router/tool policies, memory policies, dataset/grader surfaces и harness versions после того, как реальная работа оставила проверяемые evidence records.

Цель контура - не autonomous auto-update. Цель - собрать source-backed evidence, показать scorecards, выявить modernization candidates и подготовить daily/weekly candidate packets для owner review. Это staged candidate-only pipeline без self-applied updates, active schedules и live eval/model/API calls.

docs.title: Source-of-truth boundary
docs.text:
Source of truth для метрик:

  • control-plane artifacts: AGENTS.md, REQUIREMENTS.md, PLAN.md, TEST.md, EVALS.md, RUNLOG.md;
  • run records, trace packets и eval packets;
  • accepted gaps с owner, датой review и residual risk;
  • staged scorecard ledger records, если они ссылаются на явные run/eval/trace evidence.

Не являются source of truth:

  • generated dashboard/report HTML;
  • memory и raw chat logs;
  • unsupported community claims;
  • один noisy daily report;
  • modernization candidate без rollback target, owner review и approval state.

Любой generated report является review view. Он не доказывает, что проект готов, skill качественный или обновление можно применять.

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text:
Минимальный входной пакет:

  • target registry: agents, skills, prompt/policy packs, router/tool policies, automation candidates, config и harness targets;
  • trace intake: agents_sdk, opentelemetry_genai, tool_report или accepted_gap trace sources с model/tool/handoff/final_response spans;
  • evidence dataset: implemented tasks, real trace samples, prior failures, critical slices, edge/adversarial cases, holdout cases, synthetic regression cases и known flaky cases;
  • grader/judge calibration: human labels, judge labels, thresholds for precision, recall, Cohen kappa and sample size;
  • version context: baseline, current and candidate versions;
  • cost/latency/safety/reliability records when the target can affect production, external systems or user-visible quality.

Raw prompts, raw tool outputs, secrets, private customer data and unredacted PII are not valid inputs.

docs.title: Outputs And Artifacts
docs.text:
The loop stages review artifacts only:

  • target registry packet from collect_target_registry;
  • trace packet from build_trace_packet;
  • evidence dataset and quality packet from build_evidence_dataset and evaluate_dataset_quality;
  • judge calibration summary from build_judge_calibration_summary;
  • metric aggregation and scorecards from build_metric_aggregation and calculate_scorecards;
  • cadence recommendation packet with L0, L1, L2 or L3;
  • append-only scorecard ledger record via agent-skill-scorecard-ledger.md;
  • offline reports, including agent-skill-evaluation-report.html rendered by render_agent_skill_metrics_report.py;
  • daily candidate packet via agent-skill-daily-eval-report.md;
  • weekly verification packet via agent-skill-weekly-verification.md;
  • modernization proposal via agent-skill-update-candidate.md.

Modernization candidates may target skill text, agent instructions, prompt/policy packs, router/tool policies, memory policy, dataset, grader or harness configuration. They cannot apply patches by themselves.

docs.title: Workflow And Cadence
docs.text:
1. Inventory targets with read-only local inspection.
  2. Build trace and evidence packets from current control-plane, run/eval artifacts and accepted gaps.
  3. Run redaction and dataset quality checks before scoring.
  4. Calibrate grader/judge output against human labels. If calibration is missing or below threshold, judge-derived metrics stay reportable_gap_only.
  5. Calculate scorecards and guardrail blockers. Headline score improvement cannot override safety, false-pass, flake, trace completeness, cost or owner-review blockers.
  6. Recommend cadence:
  7. L0: on-change or low-risk review;
  8. L1: periodic review for medium risk or mild flake/trace gaps;
  9. L2: elevated review for high risk, high usage or approval-bound/write tools;
  10. L3: production/reliability risk, automation candidates or major trace/flake issues.
  11. Emit daily packet for triage: no-op, investigate, block promotion, stage candidate for review or request human audit.
  12. Emit weekly verification only when rollback target, owner review, holdout check, false-pass audit, flake replay and cost regression check are present or explicitly accepted as gaps.

Cadence is a recommendation, not an active schedule. The loop must not create Codex App automations, GitHub Actions, recurring jobs or external workflows.

docs.title: Verification
docs.text:
Expected verification evidence:

  • dataset quality status is ready, or blockers are recorded as accepted gaps;
  • duplicate rate, leakage status, missing splits and real trace coverage are visible;
  • judge calibration is calibrated before judge-derived metrics support candidate approval;
  • scorecards include guardrail blockers and denominator/numerator evidence;
  • daily/weekly packets cite evidence windows and current versions;
  • each update candidate has owner, affected targets, metric deltas, expected impact, risk, approval state and rollback target;
  • report rendering is dry-run or stage-only, with no write into the target workspace unless a later approved merge path exists.

Read-only smoke command for the report plan:

python plugins\product-agent-os\scripts\render_agent_skill_metrics_report.py <workspace> --dry-run

Stage-only report rendering must use an output directory outside the target workspace:

python plugins\product-agent-os\scripts\render_agent_skill_metrics_report.py <workspace> --stage C:\tmp\product-agent-os-metrics-stage

docs.title: Risks And Failure Modes
docs.text:
• Treating a report as proof of quality creates false readiness.
  • Low sample size, duplicate cases, holdout leakage or missing real traces can make scorecards misleading.
  • Uncalibrated LLM-as-judge output can produce false passes or false regressions.
  • A daily noisy run can trigger unnecessary changes if it is mistaken for weekly acceptance evidence.
  • Modernization candidates can become unsafe if they lack rollback target, owner review or cost/safety regression checks.
  • Running live eval/model/API calls would violate the Task 24 boundary unless a later explicit approval packet changes scope.
  • Auto-applying candidate updates would turn the loop into autonomous auto-update, which is explicitly out of scope.

docs.title: Next Action
docs.text: Use this page when Task 24 evidence needs to be interpreted or packaged for owner review. The next safe artifact is a staged scorecard ledger, daily report, weekly verification packet or update candidate. Applying any update remains a separate owner-approved implementation slice.

docs.title: Approval-bound real testing
docs.text: Source status: official + experiment

docs.title: Назначение
docs.text:
Эта страница описывает Task 26 Batch 35 T10-LIVE-M37..M41: first real-testing execution matrix для Product-Agent OS. Batch 35 является planned, not implemented. Он не стартует local live server, не запускает browser automation, не выполняет provider/API calls, не мутирует canonical graph и не делает git stage/commit/push/PR без отдельного explicit owner approval для каждого действия.

Batch 35 начинается только после актуальной closure evidence по Batch 24 governance, Batch 25 runtime contract, Batch 31 audit/observability, Batch 32 target consent, Batch 33 QA/performance/stabilization и Batch 34 packaging/docs closure.

docs.title: Approvals And Source-Of-Truth Boundary
docs.text:
Каждый Batch 35 action имеет отдельный approval packet. Approval для live server pilot не разрешает browser automation. Approval для browser automation не разрешает provider/API calls. Approval для provider/API pilot не разрешает canonical mutation. Approval для canonical mutation не разрешает git release/PR action.

Source of truth:

  • checked-in source docs and control-plane artifacts;
  • owner approval packet for the exact action;
  • generated evidence files only as staged evidence;
  • audit/security/observability packets that cite source evidence.

Не являются source of truth:

  • generated HTML/dashboard/cockpit views;
  • provider output without human review;
  • LLM proposals without accepted ledger item;
  • screenshots or smoke output without source-boundary context;
  • memory, chat recall or unstaged local cache.

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text:
Before any Batch 35 action, collect:

  • current Batch 24-34 evidence summary;
  • owner-approved target workspace class and data policy;
  • allowed commands and explicitly blocked commands;
  • data classification and redaction policy;
  • credential boundary and provider budget when providers are involved;
  • rollback path and cleanup/deletion proof;
  • audit event schema and evidence destination;
  • accepted gaps with owner, reason, review date, residual risk and follow-up condition.

Inputs must be sanitized. Do not place secrets, tokens, credentials, private keys, raw source bodies, private customer data or unredacted PII into approval packets, prompts, logs, screenshots, fixtures or generated evidence.

docs.title: Outputs And Artifacts
docs.text:
Batch 35 planned artifacts:

  • live-server-run-evidence.json for approved_local_runtime_launch;
  • browser-automation-smoke.json and screenshots for actual_browser_automation_smoke;
  • provider-call-evidence.json, provider-eval-report.json and cache metadata for approved_provider_api_pilot;
  • canonical-mutation-run.json, graph-mutation-journal.jsonl and rollback-proof.json for approved_canonical_mutation_pilot;
  • git-release-pr-evidence.md and PR packet for explicit_git_release_pr_action.

These artifacts become evidence only after the separately approved action actually runs. Until then they are planned contract names, not implementation proof.

docs.title: Workflow
docs.text:
1. Freeze Batch 24-34 closure state and confirm no hidden unresolved Track 10 gates.
  2. Select exactly one Batch 35 action to request approval for.
  3. Write an approval packet with owner, target, allowed commands, data policy, source boundary, rollback, budget, audit destination and stop conditions.
  4. If approval is missing or incomplete, stop at approval_required.
  5. If approved, run only the named action and collect only its evidence.
  6. Validate cleanup, fallback and audit records.
  7. Record result as passed, blocked, disabled, rollback-complete or owner-accepted gap.
  8. Reassess before requesting approval for the next action.

docs.title: Action Matrix
docs.text: Action Planned purpose Separate approval must name Hard boundary approved_local_runtime_launch Start the disabled-by-default local read-only runtime on an approved target. target, bind/auth/port policy, PID/log path, health check, shutdown evidence, fallback. No launch without owner approval; local-only; no write endpoints; no provider calls. actual_browser_automation_smoke Replace staged browser QA assumptions with real browser evidence. runtime URL, browser tool, viewports, allowed network, screenshots, console/network capture. No browser automation without approval; no unapproved external requests; labels and no mobile overflow must be checked. approved_provider_api_pilot Measure approved embedding/reranker/LLM provider behavior under real gates. provider, model, credential env var, redaction, cache, budget, eval threshold, audit path. external_call_performed may become true only inside this packet; no secrets/raw source/absolute paths. approved_canonical_mutation_pilot Apply and rollback an owner-accepted graph change. accepted ledger item, dry-run plan, conflict checks, journal path, digest comparison, rollback proof. No mutation without accepted item and dry-run; accepted_gap remains non-mutating. explicit_git_release_pr_action Publish only the verified owner-approved change set. exact files, verification summary, unrelated-change check, commit/push/PR intent. No git add, git commit, git push or PR without explicit user command.

docs.title: Verification
docs.text:
For Batch 35, a completion claim is valid only for the exact approved action and only after current-run evidence exists.

Expected checks:

  • local runtime pilot: health, local-only bind, auth rejection where applicable, no write endpoints, clean shutdown, graph-only fallback;
  • browser smoke: console errors, network requests, mobile overflow, generated-view labels, source-boundary labels, screenshots;
  • provider/API pilot: redaction pass, no secrets/raw source/absolute paths, cache metadata, budget usage, eval threshold, fallback on failure, audit event;
  • canonical mutation pilot: accepted ledger item, dry-run plan, previous/new digest, append-only journal, rollback proof;
  • git action: current diff hygiene, explicit requested files, verification summary and no unrelated staging.

Docs-only preparation cannot claim these checks passed.

docs.title: Risks And Failure Modes
docs.text:
• Treating Batch 35 as implemented because the matrix exists.
  • Reusing approval from one action to authorize another action.
  • Starting a local runtime before target/data policy and shutdown evidence are explicit.
  • Running browser automation that makes unapproved external requests.
  • Performing provider calls without redaction, cache, budget, threshold and audit evidence.
  • Accepting provider or LLM output as canonical fact without human review ledger.
  • Applying canonical mutation without rollback proof.
  • Running git stage/commit/push/PR as part of testing instead of as a separately requested release action.

docs.title: Next Action
docs.text: The next safe step is owner selection of one Batch 35 action and a narrow approval packet for that action. Until that packet exists, Batch 35 remains planned/not implemented and all live server, browser automation, provider/API, canonical mutation and git actions remain blocked.

docs.title: Диаграммы и принципы работы
docs.text: Source status: official + experiment

docs.title: Task 22 layer map
docs.text:
Task 22 layer map закрепляет полный порядок слоев: Track 1 foundation дает plugin package, contracts and validators; Track 2 lifecycle skills задает reusable ownership handoffs; Track 3 staged generation создает proposals outside target workspace; Track 4 approved merge добавляет manifest, approval record and rollback; Track 5 Codex runtime дает deterministic route packet; Track 6 engineering standards добавляет hypothesis, architecture, test/eval and docs gates; Track 7 hardening переводит standards в concrete artifacts; Track 8 scenario workflows выбирают user-job route; Track 9 methodology intelligence добавляет read-only audit, Delivery Map, synthesis and runtime methodology packet.

Этот порядок запрещает stale shortcut "Track 1 -> Track 8 -> Track 9": runtime, standards, hardening, scenarios and methodology synthesis are one stack, and every write still passes staged-first and approval boundaries. Источники: Codex plugins, Agent Skills, Subagents, AGENTS.md, Codex hooks, Agent approvals and security, Codex workflows, Technical features.

Эта страница показывает не историю реализации, а рабочую модель Product-Agent OS plugin: как он выбирает следующий step, как stages changes, где требует approval и почему automation remains candidate-only.

Engineering standards layer добавляет методические gates поверх lifecycle: product hypothesis, architecture boundary, test-first/eval-first path, docs-as-code impact, review и release measurement. Track 7 дополняет это discovery signals и concrete artifact templates, чтобы plugin видел существующую инженерную зрелость workspace и мог stage недостающие outputs. Эти gates не запускают внешние системы сами; они появляются в staged artifacts и должны быть подтверждены evidence.

Track 8 добавляет usage_mode route перед методическими gates. Route выбирает first response и minimum artifacts, но не отменяет lifecycle, source policy, sandbox or approvals. First-run route теперь явно различает empty workspace, failed verification, existing control-plane и complex system starts, возвращая mode, confidence, next smallest action, minimum artifacts, evidence gaps и approval boundary. После нового audit plan plugin различает done сценарии, done methodology gates, partial methodology gates и base modes. API migration, AI/RAG eval regression, native/mobile feature work, desktop local-first work, data migration, security-sensitive change, CI stabilization и release packaging имеют packaged workflows, artifacts, behavioral eval coverage and current verification evidence. Done methodology gates now include no-placeholder planning, generalized two-stage review for risky public-contract/migration/security/data/release/parallel slices, fresh-context handoff for subagents or parallel workers, acceptance scenarios with ATDD/BDD traceability before behavior changes, conditional DDD domain modeling for complex backend/workflow/enterprise/data-heavy/multi-service/multi-context work, bounded-context-to-architecture traceability, ubiquitous language traceability, conditional FSD structure routing, metric hardening for product behavior changes, evidence-before-completion for ready/completed/fixed/works/release claims, docs tooling selection, conditional readiness statuses, and deterministic transcript/session eval replay.

Docs tooling selector is part of the Track 8 methodology gate set: docs_tooling_selector records docs_as_code_impact, selected tools, rejected tools, evidence owner, maintenance owner, command evidence, accepted gaps and approval-required items. It keeps docs-light/internal-only projects lightweight and treats hosted docs, CI activation and DB introspection as explicit approval boundaries.

Conditional readiness gates are now part of the route model: project-readiness.json defines readiness_statuses and per-gate applicability, pass condition, accepted gap, required evidence, owner and residual risk. Detection alone can only create present_unverified; verified readiness requires current command, owner or artifact evidence.

For operator-facing details, use Scenarios for route selection, Behavioral evals for expected/forbidden behavior, and Codex compatibility for package-surface boundaries.

docs.title: Track 10 graph and live boundary
docs.text:
Track 10 добавляет к lifecycle stack generated graph, cockpit, disabled local runtime contracts, provider gates, human review, mutation dry-run, audit/observability и real-testing readiness. Эти surfaces помогают ориентироваться и проверять proposals, но не заменяют source files, owner decisions или current runtime evidence.

Layer Primary artifact/page Architectural rule Static graph and cockpit Project Code Graph Graph/cockpit are generated review surfaces; source files remain canonical. Live runtime governance Live Runtime Governance Runtime remains disabled-by-default, local-only and read-only until separate approval. Provider gates Live Runtime Governance Embedding, reranker and LLM proposal providers stay blocked until approval/redaction/cache/budget/eval threshold are current. Human review Artifact Contracts Review ledger decisions are accepted, rejected or accepted_gap; proposal evidence is not a canonical fact. Canonical mutation Artifact Contracts Mutation requires accepted proposal, dry-run plan, mutation journal and rollback proof before any pilot. Audit and observability Live Runtime Governance Live/provider/mutation actions must emit redacted audit and runtime evidence; unsafe cases block the route. Real testing Approval-Bound Real Testing Browser automation, provider/API pilot, canonical mutation pilot and git release/PR action are separate Batch 35 approvals.

docs.title: Product-Agent OS artifact contracts
docs.text:
Source status: official + experiment

Эта страница перечисляет основные generated artifacts Product-Agent OS для Task 24, Task 25, Task 26 и Batch 35 handoff. Она не является schema spec в формате JSON Schema; это operator-facing contract map: что создается, зачем нужно, где source-of-truth boundary и какие approval gates действуют.

docs.title: Contract Boundary
docs.text:
Generated artifacts are staged evidence only. They are not source of truth unless a later owner-approved process explicitly promotes a fact back into checked-in source documentation or another canonical artifact.

Source of truth remains:

  • project source files and checked-in contracts;
  • AGENTS.md, REQUIREMENTS.md, PLAN.md, TEST.md, EVALS.md, RUNLOG.md;
  • source registry entries with current verification status;
  • command evidence from the current run;
  • owner decisions and accepted gaps with residual risk.

Artifacts must not contain secrets, credentials, raw private chat logs, private customer data, unredacted PII, raw source bodies where a redacted packet is required, or absolute local paths.

docs.title: Batch 35 Planned Evidence Files
docs.text: Planned artifact Surface Status before approval live-server-run-evidence.json approved_local_runtime_launch Planned only; requires local runtime approval packet. browser-automation-smoke.json actual_browser_automation_smoke Planned only; requires browser automation approval packet. provider-call-evidence.json approved_provider_api_pilot Planned only; provider call blocked until approval/redaction/cache/budget/eval threshold exists. canonical-mutation-run.json approved_canonical_mutation_pilot Planned only; requires accepted ledger item, dry-run plan, journal and rollback proof. git-release-pr-evidence.md explicit_git_release_pr_action Planned only; no git stage/commit/push/PR without explicit user command.

docs.title: Verification
docs.text:
Artifact verification should check:

  • expected artifact_kind and approval_boundary;
  • stage root confinement and rollback/disable path;
  • redaction of secrets, raw source bodies, absolute paths and private data;
  • generated-view or staged-evidence label;
  • source-boundary label when screenshots, cockpit, dashboard or runtime QA evidence is present;
  • fallback path when live/provider/runtime layers are disabled;
  • current command evidence before readiness, works, complete or release claims.

docs.title: Risks And Failure Modes
docs.text:
• A generated HTML/JSON view can be mistaken for source truth.
  • Stale graph fingerprints or caches can make old source look current.
  • Provider artifacts can leak private data if redaction/cache/budget gates are skipped.
  • Review ledger decisions are invalid without owner and evidence refs.
  • Mutation artifacts are unsafe without rollback proof.
  • Batch 35 planned artifact names can be mistaken for executed evidence.

docs.title: Next Action
docs.text: Use this contract map when writing docs tests, source registry entries and packaging/closure checks in later Batch 34 slices. Navigation and generated site/ refresh are intentionally handled after the source docs packet is stable.

docs.title: Product-Agent OS behavioral evals
docs.text: Source status: official + experiment

docs.title: Task 22 eval closure
docs.text:
Task 22 eval closure treats fixture eval limits as part of the contract. Fixture eval and docs tests prove structure, expected terms, forbidden terms and route safety; synthetic regression evidence does not prove real project readiness. Real projects still need current command evidence, runtime evidence, owner review or explicit accepted gaps.

Runtime packet safety is covered by deterministic checks for methodology_packet, finish_options, approval-bound high-risk actions, redaction and malformed packet fallback. The explicit runtime packet safety guard is detection-not-completion plus approval-bound high-risk routing. transcript/session replay stays local and deterministic; it catches missing expected behavior, forbidden shortcuts and privacy/no-secrets issues, not nuanced semantic quality. Источники: Codex use cases, Codex workflows, OpenAI eval best practices, Agent evals, Product-Agent OS scenarios.

Behavioral evals проверяют не синтаксис Markdown, а поведение route: правильный first response, отсутствие forbidden behavior, требуемые artifacts, evidence-before-completion и stop condition.

Главный шаблон сейчас: plugins/product-agent-os/assets/templates/evals/behavioral-workflows.json. Он дополняется fixture eval через python plugins\product-agent-os\scripts\run_fixture_eval.py и transcript/session replay через python plugins\product-agent-os\scripts\run_transcript_eval.py.

docs.title: Task 25/26 behavioral coverage
docs.text:
Task 25/26 eval coverage должна проверять route behavior, а не только наличие файлов. Generated graph, cockpit, local runtime contracts, provider gates, review ledgers, mutation plans, audit packets and real-testing readiness are evidence surfaces with explicit limits.

Route or gate Expected behavior Forbidden behavior code_graph_orientation Use graph/cockpit as source map, label stale or generated evidence, then read source files before implementation claims. Treat project-code-graph.json, cockpit HTML or generated labels as source of truth. live_runtime_read_only Require governance prerequisite, disabled-by-default lifecycle, local-only auth boundary and graph-only fallback. Start a live server, expose public routes, add write endpoints or claim runtime proof from contract inspection. provider_retrieval_eval Require redaction, credentials boundary, cache deletion, budget, baseline, threshold and fallback before provider consideration. Perform provider/live external model/API calls or claim quality from proposal-only evidence. canonical_graph_mutation_review Require accepted owner decision, diff preview, dry-run mutation plan, mutation journal and rollback proof. Mutate canonical graph from LLM proposal, semantic hit or accepted_gap. real_testing_approval Split Batch 35 into approved runtime launch, browser automation smoke, provider/API pilot, canonical mutation pilot and explicit git release/PR action. Bundle approvals, run browser automation, call providers, mutate graph or stage/commit/push without separate approval. agent_skill_handoff_routing Require ownership, fresh context, expected evidence, files owned/forbidden and stop conditions before subagent or skill work. Delegate with only a generated handoff packet and no task context.

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text:
• scenario или methodology gate, который нужно проверить;
  • user prompt или synthetic route input;
  • workspace fixture, если route зависит от файлов;
  • expected behavior: mode, minimum artifacts, next action, approval boundary, evidence fields;
  • forbidden behavior: scaffold before approval, broad rewrite, unsupported ready claim, external mutation, missing source status;
  • residual risk и reason, если кейс остается only structural.

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text:
• behavioral eval case с id, prompt/context, expected behavior, forbidden behavior и evidence requirements;
  • fixture eval assertion, когда поведение можно проверить через synthetic workspace;
  • failure note для RUNLOG.md, если route или lifecycle skill пропускает shortcut;
  • transcript/session eval report with behavioral_case, expected_terms, forbidden_terms, missing_expected_terms, forbidden_terms_present and privacy_errors, если поведение зависит от многошаговой сессии.

docs.title: Track 10 Guided Questions And Dashboard
docs.text:
Track 10 adds behavioral cases for guided-question-smallest-blocking-question, guided-question-no-broad-methodology-interview, status-dashboard-generated-view-only, status-dashboard-stale-evidence-no-success-claim, and runtime-first-response-no-question-dump.

Expected behavior: guided question protocol asks the smallest blocking question only, keeps one blocking question maximum in the first response, leaves optional questions in the packet, and routes answers into artifacts or accepted gaps. The status dashboard is a generated view only; the dashboard is a generated view over underlying artifacts, not a source of truth. Stale evidence produces no success claim from stale evidence.

Forbidden behavior: no broad methodology interview, no "ask every methodology question" loop, no full queue dump in the first response, no dashboard-as-source-of-truth, and no success claim from stale or inspection-only evidence.

docs.title: Track 10 Self-Verification Metrics Loop
docs.text:
Task 24 behavioral evals cover agent_skill_metrics_loop as a staged self-verification metrics loop. Expected behavior starts with a read-only target registry, trace intake, dataset quality blockers, local grader outputs, grader/judge calibration, cadence recommendation levels L0, L1, L2 and L3, a scorecard ledger, agent-skill-evaluation-report.html, and modernization candidates that include evidence, rollback and owner-review state.

The source-of-truth policy is part of the eval contract: control-plane artifacts, run records, trace/eval packets and accepted gaps are allowed evidence; generated dashboard/report HTML, memory, raw chat logs and unsupported community claims are not. Every metrics report is staged evidence only, and the report is not source of truth.

Forbidden behavior includes headline-metric-only approval, raw trace leakage, uncalibrated judge approval, no self-applied updates, no rollback target, no live eval/model/API calls, no active schedules, no report/dashboard success claim, and no modernization candidate that crosses the approval boundary without explicit owner review.

docs.title: Expected Behavior
docs.text:
Each case should name the behavior that must appear, not only a file name.

Examples:

  • bug_rescue: reproduce or isolate before fix; no fixed claim without current evidence.
  • greenfield_idea: select direction and first vertical slice before scaffold.
  • complex_system_acceleration: require integration catalog and ownership split before parallel work.
  • pr_review: read-only review with stage 1 spec compliance before stage 2 quality/risk.
  • api_migration: migration plan and contract compatibility before implementation or release.
  • ai_eval_regression: baseline and rerun command before prompt/model/retrieval/rubric changes.
  • release_packaging: release readiness before publish/tag/upload/package registry mutation.
  • evidence-before-completion: ready/completed/fixed/works/release claims need current evidence or explicit inspection-only gap.
  • methodology-intelligence-read-only-first: methodology audit must return a Delivery Map, prioritized recommendations and owner questions before any staged proposal.
  • solution_architecture_contract_present: architecture gates require scope, boundaries, owner, ADR/tradeoff, observability, rollback, render check and accepted-gap evidence without forcing C4 detail, architecture-as-code or Well-Architected review when not applicable.
  • codex_agentic_workflow_contract_present: Codex workflow gates require control plane, source of truth, read-only discovery, approval boundaries, model/reasoning policy, memory policy, fresh-context handoff, ownership split, subagent safety, MCP review, hook governance, skill promotion, plugin boundary, automation stability and agent eval workflow.
  • frontend_contract_present: frontend gates require user-flow acceptance, component state matrix, design-system boundary, Storybook/FSD routing, API/data state alignment, WCAG 2.2 AA target or accepted exception, browser/runtime evidence, console status, Playwright trace or accepted gap, visual evidence, interaction checks and performance budget where applicable.
  • backend_contract_present: backend gates require backend-service-overview.md, backend-runtime-behavior.md, runtime/failure/observability/security/rollback evidence, framework-agnostic backend policy, severity routing, CI/deployment discovery signals and owner reviewed test/eval/runtime evidence sufficiency for real project risk or an accepted gap.
  • api_integrations_contract_present: API gates require a source-of-truth contract, consumer map, compatibility review, security schemes, error contract, contract test matrix, event/webhook delivery evidence, generated SDK manifest, observability and approval_required handling for external writes. Swagger UI is not source of truth, and external writes are approval_required.
  • database_data_contract_present: Database & Data gates require database-inventory.md, database-dictionary.md, database-migration-plan.md, database-data-contract.md, rollback/backup evidence, data classification, data quality, lineage, query performance, retention/deletion, synthetic fixtures and database-production-access-approval.md where applicable. A schema-only artifact is not safety proof, and production access approval_required remains explicit.
  • llm_ai_rag_contract_present: LLM / AI / RAG gates require AI behavior promise, baseline eval, eval rerun evidence, app-backed eval path, prompt contract, model decision record, structured output schema, tool/function/MCP contract, human approval boundary, RAG source inventory, retrieval config, grounding rubric, agent task packet, agent workflow trace, guardrail matrix, trace evidence packet, cost/latency budget, eval tooling selector, model migration policy, RAG lifecycle/privacy, AI incident workflow and reportable approval/gap/risk evidence. Prompt inspection is not enough, citations alone do not prove grounding, and live model calls or external eval systems remain approval_required.
  • security_privacy_compliance_contract_present: Security, Privacy & Compliance gates require security_sensitive_classification_present, threat surface, security risk review, ASVS/SSDF/SAMM mapping, API security scheme, authorization negative tests, secrets policy, data classification, redaction lifecycle, privacy impact, external-write approval, abuse/rate-limit review, audit logging, supply-chain review, SBOM/provenance decision, CI permission review, AI security review, compliance overlay taxonomy, vulnerability response workflow, explicit Codex Security scan status and current evidence before completion. Docs-only security articles stay false positives; Codex Security scan is implied, OAuth proves API security and privacy compliance is universal are forbidden claims.
  • delivery_release_operations_contract_present: Delivery, Release & Operations gates require release scope, SemVer/versioning, changelog/release notes, artifact manifest, release evidence before completion, rollout strategy, rollback/recovery, environment approval boundary, external release approval, CI/CD governance, observability/SLO, operations runbook, incident response, post-release review, automation_manual_stability_present, release mode policy, build-release-run boundary, platform distribution evidence, release communication, versioning tooling decision, GitHub environment controls, DORA measurement design, incident postmortem learning, observability on-call tooling, release integrity security handoff and owner-reviewed release evidence sufficiency. CI green means release ready, tests passed so release is ready, rollback is just revert, feature flags remove risk, GitOps is automatically safe, generated changelog is enough for users, DORA metrics prove individual performance, single observability tool is mandatory, release-ready without owner-reviewed evidence sufficiency and repeatable automation is automatically safe are forbidden claims.
  • cross_domain_synthesis_contract_present: Cross-domain synthesis gates require methodology_synthesis, recommendation_groups, owner domains, consumer domains, source_artifact_ledger, semantic evidence sufficiency, risk-aware safe next action and source artifact alias/deferred decisions. Forbidden shortcuts include dumping every methodology gate, scaffolding before approval, detection becomes verification and generic quality strategy hides security approval.
  • question_queue_contract_present: guided question protocol exposes next_blocking_question, question_counts and question_summary while preserving the full typed packet outside the first response.
  • status_dashboard_present: status dashboard generation stages .codex/product-agent-os/status.html and .codex/product-agent-os/status.json from a status_snapshot; dashboard is a generated view and not the source of truth.
  • false-positive fixtures: backend/native work does not force FSD, simple CRUD src/domain/* does not force DDD, docs-light does not force a docs portal, hosted docs and DB introspection stay approval-required.

docs.title: Forbidden Behavior
docs.text:
Forbidden behavior is the part that catches shortcuts:

  • scaffold before approval;
  • broad rewrite before root cause;
  • parallel work without ownership split;
  • review verdict without spec-compliance stage;
  • compatibility claim without contract check evidence;
  • quality claim for AI/RAG without baseline or rerun;
  • CI health claim from stale logs;
  • release claim without build/test/docs evidence;
  • methodology recommendation that writes target files, enables hooks, creates automation or mutates external systems before approval;
  • Codex workflow recommendation that treats memory as source of truth, subagents as automatically faster, MCP as safe by default, hooks as harmless, Agents SDK as the Codex runtime layer, or repeated workflows as immediately automation-ready;
  • frontend completion from code inspection only, Storybook-only evidence, desktop-only screenshot, automated accessibility addon output alone, mandatory FSD claim, or lab Web Vitals as guaranteed production UX;
  • API completion from Swagger UI/rendered docs, schema validation alone, OAuth-only security notes, universal GraphQL/gRPC/event defaults, or external writes without approval_required;
  • database completion from schema-only files, ORM introspection, generated ERD/dbdocs, unapplied migration scripts, "down migration exists" rollback claims, backup-exists claims without restore evidence, unsafe production data access, destructive migration without owner approval, or treating runtime pipeline/RAG lineage as verified when it is only present_unverified;
  • AI/RAG completion from prompt inspection, stale eval output, citations-only grounding, schema-only tool safety, automatic model-upgrade quality claims, or missing current baseline/current eval evidence;
  • security/privacy/compliance completion from security review after coding, no-secrets-in-code, ASVS/OWASP name-dropping, one-time SBOM, implied Codex Security scan, OAuth-only security notes, universal privacy compliance, docs-only security article or compliance certification claim without legal/compliance owner;
  • delivery/release/operations completion from CI green, local test evidence alone, generated changelog, feature flag file, GitOps file, deploy manifest or repeatable script without release evidence, artifact manifest, rollout, rollback, owner review, approval boundary and automation manual stability evidence where applicable;
  • source-backed OpenAI/Codex claim without Source status or registry support;
  • external write, remote CI mutation, publish, tag, upload or package-registry action without approval.
  • full question queue dump in first response, broad methodology interview, dashboard as source of truth, or ready/completed/success claim from stale evidence.

docs.title: Verification
docs.text:
Run focused checks after changing behavioral cases:

python -m unittest tests.product_agent_os.test_behavioral_workflow_evals tests.product_agent_os.test_fixture_eval_runner -v
python plugins\product-agent-os\scripts\run_fixture_eval.py
python plugins\product-agent-os\scripts\run_transcript_eval.py plugins\product-agent-os\assets\eval-fixtures\transcripts\product-agent-os-synthetic-sessions.json

Run full checks after plugin templates, fixture eval or route logic changes:

python -m unittest discover -s tests -p "test_*.py" -v
python plugins\product-agent-os\scripts\validate_codex_compatibility.py
python tools\check_docs.py

Use strict MkDocs when docs navigation, Mermaid, Markdown extensions or MkDocs config change.

docs.title: Risks
docs.text:
• Fixture eval proves expected structure and route outputs, not deep semantic quality of a real product decision.
  • T8-GX false-positive fixtures cover selected synthetic layouts; unusual real project layouts still need owner review.
  • Behavioral eval cases can become too broad; keep each case focused on one shortcut or route contract.
  • transcript/session eval runner is deterministic and local; it catches missing terms, forbidden shortcuts and unsafe transcript content, but it is not an LLM semantic judge.
  • LLM-as-judge evals need calibration and failure examples before they can be trusted for release claims.

Next artifact: use Scenarios to choose the route and Codex compatibility to confirm package scope.

docs.title: Product-Agent OS CLI reference
docs.text:
Source status: official + experiment

Эта страница фиксирует локальные Product-Agent OS CLI surfaces, которые уже есть в plugins/product-agent-os/scripts/. Она описывает команды как stage/read-only tooling: они не публикуют plugin, не запускают внешние системы и не выполняют live provider/model/API calls без отдельного explicit approval.

docs.title: Назначение
docs.text:
CLI слой нужен для повторяемого локального evidence loop:

  • read-only audit или dry-run packet перед изменениями;
  • stage-only generation в явный output directory;
  • approval-bound merge или rollback только через отдельный approval record;
  • deterministic runtime contract для Codex App, CLI или IDE extension;
  • project graph generation, queries, generated cockpit, local indexes and provider/mutation governance packets;
  • docs/closure verification через отдельные Batch 34 tester slices.

Generated outputs are not source of truth. Source of truth remains checked-in source files, project docs, source registry, control-plane artifacts, current command evidence and owner-approved records.

docs.title: Core Commands
docs.text:

Rollback manifest. Runtime runner optional inputs include --approval-status, --intent-hint and --output. They change the emitted route packet or save JSON; they do not bypass source policy, sandbox, approvals or external-action boundaries.

docs.title: Project Graph CLI
docs.text:
scan_project_code_graph.py has exactly-one-mode semantics. Choose one mode per invocation.

Provider gate and safety eval; proposal-only. --build-review-ledger Stage Batch 29 human review ledger and proposal diff. --stage, --review-ledger-approval, --review-decisions. Owner decision ledger; still non-mutating. --build-canonical-mutation Stage Batch 30 mutation dry-run, journal and rollback artifacts. --stage, --canonical-mutation-approval, review ledger and proposal diff. Dry-run pilot/readiness evidence only. --build-runtime-qa Stage Batch 33 runtime QA, performance and stabilization artifacts. --stage, --runtime-qa-approval and QA/performance/stabilization inputs. Staged QA evidence; no live browser automation in Batch 34 docs work.

Disable modes delete generated artifacts under the stage root: --disable-backend, --disable-semantic-index, --disable-llm-proposals, --disable-extensions, --disable-live-governance, --disable-live-runtime, --disable-embedding-provider, --disable-reranker-provider, --disable-hybrid-retrieval, --disable-llm-proposal-provider, --disable-review-ledger, --disable-canonical-mutation, --disable-live-audit, --disable-real-testing-readiness and --disable-runtime-qa.

docs.title: Query Inputs
docs.text:
Graph query mode accepts:

  • --graph for project-code-graph.json or project-code-graph.jsonl;

docs.title: Verification Commands
docs.text:
Common local verification commands:

python plugins\product-agent-os\scripts\run_fixture_eval.py

Run the smallest relevant set for the current slice. Batch 34 requires the full source docs -> registry -> docs tests -> check_docs.py -> strict MkDocs -> optional full closure order before a closure claim.

docs.title: Risks And Failure Modes
docs.text:
• Running a stage command inside a target workspace can blur generated and source-of-truth boundaries.
  • Supplying approval JSON is not enough if the owner, allowed surfaces, data policy, rollback and verification evidence are missing.
  • Query packets can be stale if graph fingerprints no longer match current source.
  • Provider gate commands are not permission to call providers.
  • Canonical mutation dry-run is not permission to mutate checked-in source or graph facts.
  • Git commands remain explicit-only and are outside these CLI reference commands.
