docs.title: Product-Agent OS Codex compatibility
docs.text: Source status: official + experiment

docs.title: Task 22 canonical safety boundary
docs.text:
Task 22 canonical safety boundary: no live model call, no separate OpenAI API key, no standalone Agents SDK activation, no global config mutation, no silent MCP/server/hook/automation activation, no unapproved external writes, no hosted docs or DB introspection require approval bypass, and no readiness claims from detection.

Codex App, CLI, IDE extension, skills, MCP declarations and staged hooks are supported package surfaces. They are not permission to mutate target workspaces, GitHub, CI, package registries, production databases, hosted documentation, security systems or schedules without explicit approval and current verification evidence. Источники: Codex App, Codex CLI, Codex IDE extension, Codex build plugins, Agent Skills, Codex MCP, Codex hooks, Agent approvals and security.

Product-Agent OS поддерживает Codex App, CLI и IDE extension как целевые surfaces. Compatibility здесь означает: package можно проверять как Codex plugin, без требования non-Codex adapters, без separate model runner и без silent external activation.

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text:
• plugin root: plugins/product-agent-os/;
  • .codex-plugin/plugin.json;
  • bundled skills/;
  • bundled MCP config .mcp.json;
  • staged hooks under assets/templates/hooks/;
  • README.md and user-facing docs;
  • validation script plugins/product-agent-os/scripts/validate_codex_compatibility.py.

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text:
• compatibility report with supported surfaces: Codex App, CLI, IDE extension;
  • evidence that .codex-plugin/plugin.json, skills, MCP and staged hooks are present;
  • explicit result that the plugin requires no standalone Agents SDK app and no separate OpenAI API key;
  • empty list of required non-Codex adapters;
  • residual risk if docs or package boundaries change without rerunning validation.

docs.title: Track 10 compatibility boundaries
docs.text:
Compatibility means the package fits Codex surfaces. It does not approve live execution, external systems or git actions.

Boundary Compatible staged work Requires separate explicit approval Live server Validate disabled local runtime contract, auth policy, lifecycle controls and graph-only fallback. Launch server, keep process running, expose network route or collect live runtime evidence. Browser automation Stage browser smoke expectations, generated-view labels, source-boundary labels and mobile overflow checks. Run Playwright/browser automation against a live local runtime. Provider/API calls Stage embedding, reranker and LLM provider gate/eval packets with redaction/cache/budget policy. Call external model/API/provider, spend tokens or store provider cache from live data. Canonical mutation Stage review ledger, proposal diff, mutation dry-run plan, journal and rollback proof. Apply accepted mutation to canonical graph or source-controlled state. Git actions Prepare release/PR packet and closure evidence. git add, commit, push, PR creation, tag, release or package upload.

docs.title: Compatibility Contract
docs.text: Surface Supported scope Boundary Codex App Interactive local product-agent threads, steering, artifacts, skills and automations when explicitly created. Product-Agent OS does not create active automations from templates. CLI Local read/edit/run workflows, fixture evals, staged renderer and validation commands. Commands obey sandbox, approvals and local workspace policy. IDE extension Editor-context implementation and review with project docs and AGENTS.md. Plugin docs do not assume IDE-only APIs. .codex-plugin/plugin.json Required manifest and packaged plugin metadata. Manifest must not point to non-Codex runtime adapters. skills Reusable lifecycle methods loaded by Codex through progressive disclosure. Skills remain task-specific and do not silently mutate external systems. MCP Context7 declared as bundled MCP config for Codex. Credentials stay outside checked-in package; MCP is not a background service launched by Product-Agent OS scripts. staged hooks Hook templates are packaged as examples and target-project assets. staged hooks are inactive until explicit approval and target-project activation.

docs.title: Non-Goals
docs.text:
• no standalone Agents SDK runtime;
  • no separate OpenAI API key;
  • no Claude, Cursor, OpenCode, Gemini or other non-Codex adapter requirement;
  • no package manager publish, marketplace submission, active automation, hook activation, remote CI mutation or external write without explicit approval;
  • no hidden live service started by the plugin.

docs.title: Verification
docs.text:
Run the compatibility validator after manifest, README, skills, MCP, hooks or package-boundary docs change:

python plugins\product-agent-os\scripts\validate_codex_compatibility.py

Expected report shape:

{
  "status": "compatible",
  "supported_surfaces": ["Codex App", "CLI", "IDE extension"],
  "requires_non_codex_adapters": false
}

Also run full plugin verification when package files change:

python -m unittest discover -s tests -p "test_*.py" -v
python plugins\product-agent-os\scripts\run_fixture_eval.py
python tools\check_docs.py

docs.title: Risks
docs.text:
• Official Codex plugin interfaces can change; package claims must stay tied to source registry checks.
  • A compatible package can still be misused if a target project activates hooks, MCP credentials, automations or external writes without review.
  • The compatibility check proves packaging scope, not product quality or scenario readiness.
  • Hosted docs, marketplace publishing and external integrations are outside this compatibility claim unless separately approved and verified.

Next artifact: use Behavioral evals to test route behavior and Scenarios to select the correct workflow.

docs.title: Engineering standards layer
docs.text: Source status: official + verified methodology + experiment

docs.title: Task 22 standards closure
docs.text:
Task 22 standards closure defines the Track 7 artifact catalog as operational guidance: ADR, architecture-overview, domain-modeling, metric-spec, api-contract-review, component-card, database-dictionary and docs-tooling-decision templates must name owner, evidence, accepted gaps, residual risk, no-secrets expectations and verification path.

Red-Green-Refactor evidence is required where behavior or shared logic changes; docs-only and inspection-only work can record an explicit gap. The no-forced-ceremony rule remains active: mechanical edits can be not_applicable, docs-light work can avoid heavy portals, backend/native work does not force FSD, simple CRUD does not force DDD, and high-risk work needs owner_reviewed_evidence_sufficient_for_real_project_risk or explicit_gap_accepted. Источники: Codex build plugins, Agent Skills, Building an AI-Native Engineering Team, Codex: add evals to your AI application, Codex: iterate on difficult problems, Codex: keep documentation up-to-date, Agile Alliance TDD, Agile Alliance ATDD, Agile Alliance BDD, Feature-Sliced Design, C4 model, arc42, OpenAPI Initiative, OpenAPI Specification v3.2.0, AsyncAPI, Storybook Autodocs, Storybook accessibility tests, GitLab Docs architecture, GitHub Actions workflows, GitHub protected branches, Martin Fowler: Domain-Driven Design.

Эта страница фиксирует расширение product-agent-os: plugin должен вести проект не только как агентную разработку, а как управляемую инженерную систему с продуктовой гипотезой, архитектурной границей, test-first/eval-first проверками, docs-as-code, review gates и измерением результата.

docs.title: Что меняется
docs.text:
Раньше Product-Agent OS в основном отвечал на вопрос: как Codex App, CLI, IDE extension, subagents, skills, AGENTS.md, hooks, evals и automation candidates проходят lifecycle без потери контекста.

Новый слой добавляет вопрос: соответствует ли работа зрелой инженерной практике.

flowchart LR
    A["Product hypothesis"] --> B["Architecture boundary"]
    B --> C["Test-first or eval-first spec"]
    C --> D["Bounded agentic implementation"]
    D --> E["Docs-as-code update"]
    E --> F["Human review and quality gate"]
    F --> G["Release measurement"]
    G --> H["Learning loop"]

docs.title: Проверенные выводы из источников
docs.text: Область Подтверждено источниками Как использовать в plugin Codex plugin packaging Plugin имеет .codex-plugin/plugin.json и может указывать bundled skills, hooks, MCP, apps и assets. Новые стандарты добавляются как packaged templates и docs, а не как silent runtime behavior. Codex skills Skills являются форматом reusable workflows, plugin - installable distribution unit. Повторяемые методики остаются workflow templates до накопления manual success evidence. AI-native engineering Роль senior-инженера смещается к spec, architecture, guardrails, review и доменной логике. Product-Agent OS усиливает planning, review, standards и evidence вместо слепой генерации кода. TDD Test-Driven Development связывает coding, testing и design/refactoring; тест пишется до реализации. TEST.md, build-slice.md и builder instructions требуют test-first/eval-first path или явный gap. ATDD/BDD Acceptance and behavior scenarios align product, development and testing perspectives before implementation. acceptance-scenarios.md, REQUIREMENTS.md, TEST.md и EVALS.md теперь требуют requirement -> scenario -> check -> evidence owner, Given/When/Then или equivalent behavior format, business rule, edge case, non-goal и explicit gap до behavior changes. DDD Domain-Driven Design нужен для сложной domain logic, где модель, bounded context и ubiquitous language снижают риск неверной архитектуры. domain-modeling.md, architecture-overview.md, project-readiness.json, implementation-planner и discovery gap missing domain model for complex domain требуют domain_model_when_complex_domain только для complex backend/workflow/enterprise/data-heavy/multi-service/multi-context work, bounded_context_architecture_boundary_trace связывает каждый bounded context с architecture boundary или accepted gap, а ubiquitous_language_traceability связывает domain terms с requirement/source, API/event/contract, UI label, code module or owner. FSD Feature-Sliced Design задает layers, slices, segments, public API и import rule. Для применимого web UI plugin теперь обнаруживает optional fsd_structure, требует layer/slice/segment/public API/import rule в component-card.md или accepted gap, но не навязывает FSD backend, native, simple CRUD и simple MVP. Architecture docs C4 дает уровни context/container/component/code; arc42 задает структуру architecture communication. documentation-system.md требует architecture overview, ADR и диаграммы для изменений границ. API contracts OpenAPI описывает HTTP APIs; AsyncAPI описывает message-driven APIs машинно-читаемо. Backend/API changes должны обновлять source-of-truth contracts или фиксировать gap. UI docs Storybook Autodocs превращает stories в документацию; a11y addon поддерживает accessibility checks. UI changes должны иметь component states, docs, accessibility/visual checks где применимо. Docs-as-code GitLab хранит docs source рядом с product code; GitHub Actions workflow - YAML process in repo; protected branches can require reviews/status checks. Docs становятся частью PLAN.md, TEST.md, RUNLOG.md, а CI/CODEOWNERS остаются staged proposals.

docs.title: Context7 findings
docs.text:
Context7 использовался как дополнительный retrieval layer, но official status присваивается только underlying source.

  • Feature-Sliced Design: официальная документация подтверждает import rule - slice может импортировать только slices нижних layers; также подтверждает public API rule для slices.
  • Storybook: документация подтверждает autodocs tag, MDX/Doc Blocks и integration path для accessibility tests.
  • OpenAPI: спецификация подтверждает Security Scheme Object и типы security schemes, включая apiKey, http, oauth2, openIdConnect.
  • Direct web verification on 2026-05-23: latest published OpenAPI Specification is v3.2.0; v3.1.1 remains useful only as a compatibility reference.

Эти findings не заменяют primary links в source registry.

docs.title: Operating standard
docs.text:
Для любой meaningful feature plugin должен требовать:

  1. Product hypothesis: что меняем, для кого, какая метрика покажет успех, какие privacy/security constraints.
  2. Architecture boundary: где живет код, какие dependency rules, какие public contracts нельзя ломать.
  3. Test-first or eval-first path: тест, contract check, fixture или eval до изменения поведения.
  4. Bounded agentic implementation: owned files, files out of scope, stop conditions, approvals.
  5. Documentation impact: architecture, API/event contracts, UI docs, database docs, release/user docs.
  6. Review gate: correctness, security, data handling, performance, rollback, source fidelity.
  7. Measurement: post-release metrics, support signals, defects, latency, cost, user feedback.

docs.title: Что добавлено в plugin
docs.text:
Generated control-plane files теперь содержат эти поля:

Artifact Новые обязанности AGENTS.md Engineering standards baseline: hypothesis, architecture boundary, test/eval-first, docs-as-code, bounded agent work, evidence-before-completion. REQUIREMENTS.md Product hypothesis, success metrics, guardrail metrics, metric hardening, source-of-truth docs. PLAN.md Methodology gates, architecture boundary, metric hardening, evidence-before-completion, documentation impact, contract/schema/docs/eval gates. TEST.md Test-first cases, acceptance scenarios, metric hardening checks, evidence-before-completion checks, API/event/schema checks, docs checks, AI/subjective checks. EVALS.md Architecture boundary, acceptance scenario evals, metric hardening evals, evidence-before-completion evals, documentation quality, AI answer quality, retrieval quality, latency/cost/grounding thresholds. RUNLOG.md Methodology trace, metric hardening evidence, evidence-before-completion evidence and measurement notes. .codex/workflows/development-standards.md Reusable workflow for product hypothesis -> architecture -> tests/evals -> implementation -> review -> measurement. .codex/workflows/documentation-system.md Reusable docs-as-code workflow for architecture, API, UI, code reference, DB and release docs. .codex/artifact-templates/*.md Concrete templates for ADR, architecture overview, domain modeling, bounded-context-to-architecture traceability, ubiquitous language traceability, metrics, API contracts, UI component cards and database dictionaries. .codex/artifact-templates/acceptance-scenarios.md ATDD/BDD traceability from requirement to scenario, check and evidence owner before behavior changes. .codex/artifact-templates/governance-proposal.md Staged governance proposal for CODEOWNERS status and GitHub Actions least privilege without external activation.

Track 7 hardening добавляет поведенческие проверки поверх prose:

  • workspace-discovery-auditor теперь может видеть methodology signals: architecture docs, ADR, OpenAPI, AsyncAPI, Storybook, optional fsd_structure, DB docs, CODEOWNERS, CI, evals и metrics.
  • project-readiness.json фиксирует methodology gates: product hypothesis, architecture boundary, optional fsd_structure_when_ui_architecture_applies, test/eval-first evidence, docs-as-code impact и release measurement.
  • Artifact templates переводят рекомендации из research-файлов в конкретные reviewable outputs.

Track 8 hardening добавляет scenario-first routing:

  • done workflows now cover first-run intake, bug rescue, greenfield idea shaping, complex system acceleration, PR review readiness, legacy onboarding, API migration, AI/RAG eval regression, native/mobile feature work, desktop local-first work, data migration, security-sensitive change, CI stabilization and release packaging.
  • Dedicated scenario docs now describe usage_mode, first response, minimum artifacts, approval boundary and verification gates for plugin operators.
  • Dedicated behavioral eval docs now separate expected behavior, forbidden behavior, fixture eval coverage and deterministic transcript/session replay coverage.
  • Dedicated Codex compatibility docs now record Codex App, CLI, IDE extension, .codex-plugin, skills, MCP and staged hooks as the supported package boundary.
  • First-run intake keeps the first response small for empty, broken, existing control-plane and complex system starts: mode, confidence, next smallest action, minimum artifacts, evidence gaps and approval boundary.
  • Release packaging now has release-packaging.md, release-readiness.md, discovery signals, behavioral eval coverage, and publish/tag/upload/package-registry approval boundaries.
  • Acceptance scenario traceability now has acceptance-scenarios.md, lifecycle skill wording, readiness eval coverage and behavioral eval coverage before behavior changes.
  • Conditional DDD domain modeling now has domain_model discovery, domain_model_when_complex_domain readiness gate, bounded_context_architecture_boundary_trace, ubiquitous_language_traceability, implementation-planner stop condition, accepted-gap support and false-positive protection for plain domain/ folders.
  • Conditional FSD structure routing now has fsd_structure discovery, component-card.md layer/slice/segment/public API/import rule fields, implementation-planner stop condition, accepted-gap support and false-positive protection for backend, native, simple CRUD and simple MVP work.
  • Metric hardening now has metric_hardening_when_product_behavior_changes, strengthened metric-spec.md, release packet checks, generated control-plane fields, lifecycle skill enforcement and fixture eval coverage for North Star or primary value metric, input metric, counter-metric, proxy metric risk, guardrail, qualitative review, privacy classification, retention period, data minimization, owner signoff and post-release review evidence.
  • Evidence-before-completion now has evidence_before_completion, release packet checks, development standards guidance, generated control-plane fields, lifecycle skill enforcement, behavioral eval coverage and fixture eval coverage for ready/completed/fixed/works/release claims.
  • Docs tooling selector now has docs_tooling_selector, docs-tooling-decision.md, docs_as_code_impact status vocabulary, discovery routing, generated control-plane fields, lifecycle skill enforcement and fixture eval coverage for stack-aware docs choices without forced installs or unapproved external activation.
  • Standards trigger policy now has standards_trigger_policy, governance-proposal.md, ADR trigger policy, C4/arc42 applicability, OpenAPI source of truth, AsyncAPI event contract fields, SemVer impact, Keep a Changelog categories, CODEOWNERS status, GitHub Actions least privilege fields and no forced external activation.
  • Conditional readiness gates now have readiness_statuses, structured per-gate applicability, pass condition, accepted gap, required evidence, owner and residual risk in project-readiness.json, generated control-plane templates, lifecycle skills and fixture eval coverage. Detection alone can only produce present_unverified, not readiness.
  • Detailed discovery status now has methodology_applicability packets in discovery output for architecture boundary, test/eval-first evidence, docs-as-code ownership, product measurement, complex-domain DDD, applicable FSD structure, docs tooling decision and standards trigger policy.
  • Readiness gates must distinguish “route detected” from verified readiness. Completion claims require current evidence or an explicit inspection-only gap.

Track 9 security methodology adds security_privacy_compliance_when_sensitive_surface as a conditional readiness gate for authn/authz, permissions, secrets, PII, sensitive data, payment/billing, abuse controls, audit logging, supply chain, SBOM/provenance, CI permissions, AI/tool security, external writes, production data, policy changes and compliance overlays. Security/Privacy/Compliance-sensitive slices record security_privacy_compliance evidence before completion claims: threat surface, security risk review, ASVS/SSDF/SAMM mapping, authorization negative tests, secrets policy, data classification, privacy impact, external-write approval, supply-chain/SBOM/CI evidence, audit logging, compliance overlay taxonomy, vulnerability response workflow, explicit Codex Security scan status or not requested, and approval boundaries.

Track 9 delivery methodology adds delivery_release_operations_readiness_when_release_or_operations_changes as a conditional readiness gate for release/deploy/publish/package/operations work. Delivery/Release/Operations slices record delivery_release_operations evidence before release, deploy, publish, operational-ready or automation-ready claims: release scope, versioning, changelog/release notes, artifact manifest, release evidence before completion, rollout, rollback/recovery, environment approval boundary, external release approval, CI/CD governance, SLO/observability, operations runbook, incident response, post-release review, automation_manual_stability_present, release mode policy, build-release-run boundary, platform distribution evidence, release communication, versioning tooling decision, GitHub environment controls, DORA measurement design, incident postmortem learning, observability/on-call tooling, release integrity security handoff and release_evidence_sufficiency_owner_reviewed.

Track 9 cross-domain synthesis adds grouped methodology recommendations across domains. The shared packet keeps methodology_synthesis, recommendation_groups, owner domains, consumer domains, source_artifact_ledger, alias/deferred artifact decisions, semantic evidence sufficiency and risk-aware safe next action. detection alone remains present_unverified; grouped methodology recommendations do not prove readiness or semantic evidence sufficiency. High-risk, production, release, security-sensitive, AI behavior and public-contract slices need owner_reviewed_evidence_sufficient_for_real_project_risk or explicit_gap_accepted with owner, reason, review date, downstream risk and follow-up condition. This keeps approval-bound behavior visible while avoiding false positives for docs-only work, internal CLI work, backend FSD-like folders, CI-only workflows and tooling-only release files.

docs.title: Важные ограничения
docs.text:
• Data-Driven Development в source-файле не является тем же термином, что Domain-Driven Design. В core guidance используем формулировки data-informed product decisions, product hypothesis и success metric, чтобы не смешивать термины.
  • ATDD/BDD scenarios do not replace unit tests, integration tests, contract tests or evals; they are a traceability layer for behavior intent and evidence ownership.
  • Domain-Driven Design не навязывается простому CRUD или simple MVP. Product-Agent OS требует domain modeling, bounded-context-to-architecture traceability и ubiquitous language traceability только при complex backend/workflow/enterprise/data-heavy/multi-service/multi-context signals или при явном owner decision.
  • Feature-Sliced Design не навязывается backend, native, simple CRUD или маленьким MVP. Plugin требует architecture boundary, а FSD является сильным default только для растущего web UI или explicit owner decision.
  • Docs-as-code не означает автоматическое создание CI, CODEOWNERS, GitHub Actions или публикации. Product-Agent OS может stage proposals, но не активирует external workflows без explicit approval.
  • Docs tooling selection records selected tools, rejected tools, evidence owner, maintenance owner and approval boundaries; docs-light/internal-only work can be not_applicable.
  • AI/RAG quality нельзя закрывать только unit tests. Для retrieval, grounding, hallucination risk, latency и cost нужны evals или явно записанный gap.
  • llm_ai_rag_readiness_when_ai_behavior_changes нельзя закрывать prompt inspection, citations-only grounding, stale eval output или automatic model-upgrade quality claim; live model calls, external eval services, vector DB access и tool writes остаются approval-bound.
  • security_privacy_compliance_when_sensitive_surface нельзя закрывать docs-only security article, no-secrets-in-code claim, OAuth-only note, one-time SBOM, implied Codex Security scan или generic compliance/certification wording. Legal, contractual and internal-policy overlays need owner, evidence, non-goals, gaps and review cadence.
  • delivery_release_operations_readiness_when_release_or_operations_changes нельзя закрывать CI green, local test evidence alone, generated changelog, feature flag, GitOps, deployment manifest, rollback-is-revert, repeatable script или automation candidate wording. DORA metrics prove individual performance, mobile signing alone, single-tool observability and release-ready without owner-reviewed evidence sufficiency are also unsupported shortcuts. Publish, tag, release creation, artifact upload, deploy, package registry mutation, marketplace/store submission, CI/CD environment mutation and active automation stay approval-bound.

docs.title: Definition of done для Product-Agent OS slice
docs.text:
Slice можно считать готовым к review только если:

  • product hypothesis и success metric ясны или помечены not applicable;
  • product behavior metrics have counter-metric, guardrail, qualitative review, privacy classification, retention period, data minimization, owner signoff and post-release review evidence, or an explicit not-applicable reason;
  • architecture boundary и ownership названы;
  • для complex backend/workflow/enterprise/data-heavy/multi-service/multi-context work есть domain-modeling artifact или accepted gap;
  • test-first/eval-first evidence есть или gap явно принят;
  • затронутые source-of-truth docs обновлены или gap записан;
  • docs tooling impact is recorded as not_applicable, present_unverified, present_verified, proposal_staged, explicit_gap_accepted or approval_required;
  • standards trigger impact is recorded through standards_trigger_policy when ADR/C4/arc42/OpenAPI/AsyncAPI/SemVer/Keep a Changelog/CODEOWNERS/GitHub Actions context applies;
  • conditional readiness gates record not_applicable, applicable_missing, present_unverified, present_verified, proposal_staged, explicit_gap_accepted or approval_required with applicability reason, owner and residual risk;
  • AI/RAG behavior changes record llm_ai_rag evidence: behavior promise, baseline/current eval, prompt/model/schema/tool/RAG/grounding/trace/guardrail/cost evidence, current-run evidence or an accepted gap;
  • Security/Privacy/Compliance-sensitive slices record security_privacy_compliance evidence: classification, threat surface, ASVS/SSDF/SAMM mapping, authz negative tests, secrets/data/privacy handling, supply-chain/SBOM/CI review, audit logging, compliance overlay, vulnerability response and explicit Codex Security scan status or accepted gap;
  • Delivery/Release/Operations slices record delivery_release_operations evidence: release scope, versioning, changelog, artifact manifest, rollout, rollback, environment approval, CI/CD governance, SLO/observability, operations, incident/postmortem, post-release review, approval boundary, release mode policy, build-release-run boundary, platform distribution evidence, tooling decisions, release integrity handoff, release_evidence_sufficiency_owner_reviewed and automation manual stability evidence when automation is proposed;
  • команды, exit codes, artifacts и residual risks записаны в RUNLOG.md;
  • approvals, security, privacy, migration и rollback risks не скрыты.

docs.title: Live runtime governance
docs.text: Source status: official + experiment

docs.title: Назначение
docs.text:
Эта страница описывает governance-контур Product-Agent OS для Task 26 Batch 24-33: от approval packet и data classification до disabled-by-default local runtime, provider gates, review ledger, canonical mutation dry-run, audit/observability, real-testing readiness и runtime QA.

Документ является операторским guide. Он не запускает live server, не выполняет browser automation, не делает provider/API calls, не мутирует canonical graph и не выполняет git stage/commit/push/PR. Все generated artifacts являются staged evidence only и не являются source of truth.

docs.title: Approvals And Source-Of-Truth Boundary
docs.text:
Source of truth остаются checked-in Markdown/JSON/JSONL control-plane artifacts, официальная документация OpenAI для Codex App, CLI, IDE extension, approvals, sandbox, MCP и project-authored source files. Generated graph/runtime/provider artifacts являются review views и evidence packets.

Любой live/runtime/provider/mutation шаг требует approval packet с:

  • explicit_approval: true;
  • owner и allowed surfaces;
  • data classification и redaction boundary;
  • credential boundary: credentials только через environment или trusted local config, без secrets в docs, prompts, fixtures, caches или logs;
  • cache policy, TTL, invalidation и deletion proof;
  • token/cost/latency budget и fallback on exceed;
  • eval thresholds;
  • rollback path;
  • residual risks и accepted gaps.

Без полного approval packet действие остается approval_required, blocked или деградирует в graph-only fallback.

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text:
Минимальные входы для live governance:

  • Task 26 plan rows T10-LIVE-M01..M34;
  • Batch 24 governance packet from project_graph_live_governance.py;
  • Batch 25 local read-only runtime packet from project_graph_live_runtime.py;
  • Batch 26-28 provider gates for embeddings, reranker/hybrid retrieval and LLM proposals;
  • Batch 29 human review ledger and proposal diff preview;
  • Batch 30 canonical mutation dry-run, journal and rollback proof;
  • Batch 31 audit/security/observability/handoff packets;
  • Batch 32 real-testing readiness, target consent, pilot harness and Codex surface smoke;
  • Batch 33 browser QA, performance budget and stabilization ledger.

Inputs must not include raw secrets, credentials, raw private source bodies, raw private chat logs, private customer data or unredacted PII.

docs.title: Outputs And Artifacts
docs.text:
Expected artifacts are staged evidence packets, not canonical truth:

  • live-runtime-approval.json, data-classification.json, cache/budget policies;
  • live runtime contract with local-only, read-only routes and disabled_by_default_not_started;
  • embedding provider gate and eval baseline;
  • reranker provider gate and hybrid retrieval pipeline;
  • LLM proposal provider gate and safety eval;
  • graph-review-ledger.json and proposal-diff.json;
  • mutation_plan.json, graph-mutation-journal.jsonl and rollback proof;
  • audit-log.jsonl, security-privacy.json, runtime-observability.json, agent-skill-handoff.json;
  • real-testing-readiness.json, real-testing-targets.json, pilot-harness.json, codex-surface-smoke.json, real-testing-pilot-matrix.json;
  • project-code-graph-runtime-browser-qa.json, project-code-graph-performance-budget.json, project-code-graph-stabilization-ledger.json.

docs.title: Workflow
docs.text:
1. Validate Batch 24 governance before any live surface.
  2. Keep Batch 25 runtime disabled by default, local-only, read-only, authenticated where required, with graph-only fallback and clean shutdown evidence before real launch is considered.
  3. Gate Batch 26 embedding provider with redaction, cache, budget and eval threshold. If threshold fails, keep semantic_retrieval_or_graph_only.
  4. Gate Batch 27 reranker and hybrid retrieval with bounded candidates, explainable fusion and no canonical mutation.
  5. Gate Batch 28 LLM proposal provider as proposal-only structured JSON. Provider output is never canonical fact and unsafe output routes to incident/fallback.
  6. Route Batch 29 proposals through human review ledger: accepted, rejected or accepted_gap with evidence refs.
  7. Use Batch 30 only as dry-run mutation planning unless accepted proposal, conflict checks, append-only journal and rollback proof are present.
  8. Record Batch 31 redacted append-only audit events, negative security/privacy checks, runtime health, latency, provider errors, budget usage, degraded mode and handoff ownership.
  9. Use Batch 32 to prove real-testing readiness, owner-approved target/data policy, dry-run pilot harness, Codex App/CLI/IDE extension smoke and Track 8 use-case pilot mapping.
  10. Use Batch 33 to record browser QA expectations, console/network checks, mobile overflow, generated-view labels, source-boundary labels, performance budget and stabilization status.

docs.title: Verification
docs.text:
Governance is acceptable only when evidence shows:

  • provider_call_allowed: false and external_call_performed: false unless a later separately approved execution packet changes the specific surface;
  • no live server launch in Batch 24-34 docs/governance work;
  • no browser automation in Batch 24-34 docs/governance work;
  • no canonical graph mutation outside approved dry-run/staged copy paths;
  • no git stage/commit/push/PR;
  • generated artifacts are labeled as staged evidence and not source of truth;
  • budget breach disables live layer or records owner-accepted gap;
  • no open P0/P1 before closure;
  • fallback remains usable when live/provider layers are disabled.

For docs-only Batch 34 work, read-only inspection is enough unless the owning Batch 34 tester later runs focused docs checks.

docs.title: Risks And Failure Modes
docs.text:
• Generated views may look authoritative if source-boundary and generated-view labels are missing.
  • Provider payloads can leak secrets, paths or raw source if redaction is bypassed.
  • Credentials can leak if stored in docs, fixtures, prompts, caches or logs.
  • Cache can make stale evidence look current without fingerprint invalidation and deletion proof.
  • Provider eval can be misleading if it lacks baseline, threshold or fallback.
  • LLM proposals can hallucinate or overstate unsupported claims.
  • Human review ledger is invalid if accepted proposals lack owner decision and evidence refs.
  • Canonical mutation is unsafe without dry-run, conflict checks, journal and rollback proof.
  • Runtime QA is incomplete if mobile overflow, console/network, source-boundary labels or performance budget are missing.

docs.title: Next Action
docs.text: Use this page as the Batch 24-33 governance checklist before Batch 35. The next safe artifact is an approval-bound Batch 35 packet that names exactly one planned action, its owner, allowed target, data policy, command scope, rollback and verification evidence.

docs.title: Methodology Intelligence
docs.text: Source status: local product design + experiment

docs.title: Task 22 final methodology contract
docs.text:
Task 22 final methodology contract закрывает Track 9 как read-only methodology intelligence layer. The runtime route may carry methodology_packet, finish_options, owner_questions, safe_next_action, methodology_synthesis and source_artifact_ledger, but those packets are recommendation and routing evidence, not target-project mutation.

The staged artifact boundary remains strict: methodology recommendations can produce a report, owner question or staged proposal, but approval_required actions such as release, deploy, publish, DB access, security scan, external write, hook activation or automation activation stay blocked until explicit owner approval and current evidence exist.

Methodology Intelligence is the Track 9 layer of Product-Agent OS. It reads workspace evidence, maps it to the methodology atlas, and returns a read-only route packet before any staged artifact or target-project write is proposed.

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text:
• Workspace files and lightweight signals such as stack markers, control-plane files, docs files, API specs, release files and deployment markers.
  • Product-Agent OS methodology catalog entries for business, requirements, architecture, quality, Codex / agentic workflow, frontend, backend, API, data, AI, security and delivery domains.
  • Current user request, when it changes applicability or risk classification.
  • Existing lifecycle artifacts such as AGENTS.md, REQUIREMENTS.md, PLAN.md, TEST.md, EVALS.md and RUNLOG.md.

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text:
• methodology_applicability packet with maturity_level, complexity_profile, applicable domains, missing gates, owner questions and residual risks.
  • Delivery Map that groups recommendations into immediate blockers, high-risk gaps, useful maturity improvements and non-applicable items.
  • Cross-Domain Synthesis packet with methodology_synthesis, recommendation_groups, source_artifact_ledger and risk-aware safe next action.
  • methodology-audit-report.md as a human-readable report template for current evidence and next actions.
  • methodology-applicability.json as the planned stable machine-readable packet for lifecycle skills.
  • Questions for owner when evidence is missing, ambiguous or approval-bound.

docs.title: Read-Only First
docs.text:
The audit is read-only by default. It can inspect the target workspace and generate reports, but it must not write into the target project, enable hooks, create automations, contact external systems or change GitHub/CI/package registries. If a recommendation needs files, the next step is a staged proposal with explicit owner approval.

maturity_level describes how much Product-Agent OS evidence is present, from early/uninitialized workspaces to projects with current requirements, plan, tests, evals and runlog. complexity_profile records why a workspace looks simple, product-heavy, multi-service, data-sensitive, release-oriented, AI/RAG-heavy or governance-heavy.

docs.title: Delivery Map
docs.text:
Delivery Map turns methodology findings into an execution order:

Priority Meaning Required behavior P0_blocker Missing evidence blocks responsible implementation or completion claims. Stop at read-only report or staged proposal. P1_high_risk Work can continue only with explicit risk handling, owner question or artifact gap. Add the gate to plan, tests, evals or review packet before build/release. P2_recommended Useful improvement for maturity, maintainability or observability. Stage when it fits the current slice. P3_optional_maturity Helpful for advanced teams, but not required for the immediate task. Keep as backlog unless owner asks. not_applicable Domain or gate does not fit the workspace or request. Record reason; do not force process.

docs.title: Methodology Recommendations
docs.text:
Recommendations must name the domain, reason, evidence used, priority, suggested artifact and verification path. A good recommendation says what to inspect next and what artifact would make the gap measurable.

Examples:

  • business/product work needs a hypothesis, success metric, counter-metric and measurement owner;
  • complex domain work needs domain model and bounded-context traceability;
  • solution architecture work needs scope, context/container boundaries, boundary owner, ADR/tradeoff evidence, public contract trace, data ownership, trust boundary review, observability, rollback and diagram render evidence when applicable;
  • AI/RAG work needs baseline eval, dataset policy, grounding evidence and cost/latency guardrails;
  • Security/Privacy/Compliance work needs threat surface, security-sensitive classification, data classification, authorization negative tests, privacy impact, supply-chain evidence, Codex Security scan status and compliance overlay ownership;
  • release or migration work needs rollback, compatibility and owner approval evidence.

docs.title: Cross-Domain Synthesis
docs.text:
Cross-Domain Synthesis groups repeated methodology recommendations into recommendation_groups so operators see the owner artifact first instead of a dump of every methodology gate. Each group keeps owner domains, consumer domains, merged gates, evidence requirements, residual risk and the selected risk-aware safe next action.

The machine packet is methodology_synthesis. It includes source_artifact_ledger for source-era artifact names, source artifact alias/deferred decisions, semantic evidence sufficiency and a read-only write policy. Source artifacts such as context-map.md, ui-flow-spec.md, threat-model.md, runbook.md, slo.md and CHANGELOG.md are classified as canonical templates, aliases, existing non-template project artifacts or deferred candidates with an owner and reason.

Risk-aware safe next action means approval, security, release, production-data and destructive-change blockers can outrank generic quality strategy. Generic quality evidence remains visible, but it must not hide a more specific owner action. Detection alone remains present_unverified; it is never upgraded to readiness evidence without owner-reviewed proof.

Semantic evidence sufficiency is shared across high-risk, production, release, security-sensitive, AI behavior and public-contract slices. It requires owner_reviewed_evidence_sufficient_for_real_project_risk or explicit_gap_accepted with owner, reason, review date, downstream risk and follow-up condition. This keeps approval-bound behavior explicit while avoiding heavy-process false positives for docs-only, internal CLI, backend FSD-like folders, CI-only workflows and tooling-only release files.

docs.text:

Requirements/Domain requirements_domain_contract_present requirement-registry.md, stakeholder-owner-map.md, story-slice-map.md, requirements-traceability-matrix.md, business-rules.md, example-map.md, domain-modeling.md, domain-review-record.md. Delivery/Release/Operations reports also preserve release mode policy, build-release-run boundary, platform distribution evidence, release communication, versioning tooling decision, GitHub environment controls, DORA measurement design, incident postmortem learning, observability/on-call tooling, release integrity security handoff and owner-reviewed release evidence sufficiency. Detection of those terms is not readiness evidence by itself.

docs.title: Approval Boundary
docs.text:
Methodology Intelligence can recommend staged_only or approval_required, but it cannot silently move from advice to mutation. Hosted docs, production database access, remote CI mutation, package publishing, release creation, tags, artifact upload, deploys, package registry mutation, active automations, hook activation and external writes remain approval-bound.

Owner questions are part of the output, not a failure. They keep ambiguity visible: who owns a missing methodology gate, which requirement is source-backed, which system is production, which data is sensitive, and which risk is accepted rather than fixed in the current slice.

docs.title: Verification
docs.text:
For docs-only changes to this page, run:

python -m unittest tests.product_agent_os.test_product_agent_os_docs -v
python tools\check_docs.py
$env:PYTHONPATH='C:\tmp\codex_docs_mkdocs'; $env:NO_MKDOCS_2_WARNING='1'; python -m mkdocs build --strict

For implementation changes to methodology audit or catalog behavior, also run focused Product-Agent OS unit tests and fixture evals:

python -m unittest tests.product_agent_os.test_methodology_catalog tests.product_agent_os.test_methodology_audit tests.product_agent_os.test_fixture_eval_runner -v
python plugins\product-agent-os\scripts\run_fixture_eval.py

docs.title: Risks
docs.text:
• Static workspace signals can miss product intent, hidden dependencies, regulatory context and production risk.
  • Over-eager methodology routing can force heavy process onto simple work; every domain recommendation needs applicability and false-positive handling.
  • Read-only reports can become stale quickly; completion or release claims still need fresh command, runtime, eval or owner evidence.
  • methodology-applicability.json is planned as a stable packet, but domain slices can refine its schema before Track 9 synthesis.

docs.title: Packaging and closure
docs.text: Source status: official + experiment

docs.title: Назначение
docs.text:
Эта страница фиксирует Batch 34 T10-LIVE-M35..M36: Packaging, Docs, Source Registry, Closure And Batch 35 Handoff. Batch 34 делает систему понятной, проверяемой и готовой к owner handoff перед approval-bound real testing, но сам по себе не запускает Batch 35 и не является доказательством live execution.

Batch 34 закрывает docs updated packet, packaging/install smoke definition, required verification, generated site/ rebuild rule и handoff packet для Batch 35.

docs.title: Source-of-truth boundary
docs.text:
Source of truth:

  • checked-in Product-Agent OS source docs;
  • Track 10 plan and accepted Batch 34 matrix;
  • source registry and control-plane artifacts after их отдельного owner-approved/docs-maintainer slice;
  • current command evidence from docs tests, tools/check_docs.py, strict MkDocs, optional full closure and packaging/install smoke;
  • explicit owner approval packets for any later live/browser/provider/canonical/git action.

Not source of truth:

  • generated site/ pages by themselves;
  • packaging/install smoke as a release or publish approval;
  • plugin-cache contents without checked-in source comparison;
  • staged evidence without owner review;
  • planning matrix presence without implementation and verification evidence.

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text:
Batch 34 closure consumes:

  • Task 24 modernization loop docs and metrics-report boundary;
  • Task 25 project code graph, cockpit, static search, backend gate, semantic retrieval, deterministic proposal and extension-closure docs;
  • Task 26 Batch 24-33 governance/runtime/provider/review/mutation/audit/real-testing-readiness/runtime-QA evidence;
  • Batch 34 Detailed Task Matrix B34-DOC-M01..M15;
  • plugin README install and packaging guidance;
  • MkDocs navigation/docs-check requirements from the Builder/Tester slice;
  • known gaps: docs-maintainer plugin-cache gap and Mermaid external asset gap when still unresolved.

docs.title: Outputs And Artifacts
docs.text:
Expected Batch 34 outputs:

  • updated docs pages for Product-Agent OS source docs;
  • source registry/backlog/control-plane sync from the owning docs-maintainer slice;
  • updated docs contract tests and tools/check_docs.py from the owning Builder/Tester slice;
  • regenerated site/ using the regular MkDocs site_dir;
  • packaging/install smoke evidence packet;
  • Batch 35 approval packet draft;
  • explicit list of actions not performed without approval.

This worker page covers only the docs packet. It does not update navigation, tests, registry, README, site/, git state or plugin distribution.

docs.title: Packaging And Install Smoke
docs.text:
Packaging/install smoke is evidence only. It should answer:

  • plugin manifest exists and points to the expected bundled skills/MCP metadata;
  • checked-in docs-maintainer guidance is available, or the docs-maintainer plugin-cache gap is recorded;
  • local install path or marketplace candidate can be inspected without publishing;
  • staged templates and scripts remain package-readable;
  • no secrets, credentials or private data are bundled;
  • plugin hooks and automations remain inactive unless explicitly approved;
  • install smoke result records command, environment, output summary, gaps and residual risk.

Install smoke does not publish the plugin, write to external systems, create a marketplace release, upload artifacts, activate hooks, create automations or approve Batch 35.

docs.title: Workflow And Cadence
docs.text:
Batch 34 verification order is fixed:

  1. Source docs.
  2. Source registry.
  3. Docs contract tests.
  4. python tools\check_docs.py.
  5. Strict MkDocs build.
  6. Optional full closure.
  7. Packaging/install smoke.
  8. Batch 35 handoff packet.

The generated documentation site must be rebuilt with the regular MkDocs site_dir:

python -m mkdocs build --strict

Using only a disposable --site-dir is not enough when Batch 34 explicitly requires site/ refresh.

docs.title: Required Verification
docs.text:
Minimum Batch 34 closure evidence:

  • focused docs contract test result for new pages, required source status and safety boundaries;
  • python tools\check_docs.py;
  • strict MkDocs build into site/;
  • git diff --check;
  • packaging/install smoke packet;
  • explicit Batch 35 handoff packet.

Optional full closure when risk or scope requires:

  • full unittest with long timeout;
  • fixture eval;
  • transcript eval;
  • Codex compatibility validation;
  • reviewer pass over generated site/, long-line IA and accepted gaps.

Do not claim Batch 34 is complete unless the current run has matching command evidence or clearly states which verification was not run.

docs.title: Batch 35 Handoff
docs.text:
Batch 35 remains approval-bound real testing execution. The handoff packet should list separate approval surfaces:

  • approved_local_runtime_launch;
  • actual_browser_automation_smoke;
  • approved_provider_api_pilot;
  • approved_canonical_mutation_pilot;
  • explicit_git_release_pr_action.

Each surface needs owner, approved target, data policy, redaction/cache/budget boundary where relevant, rollback/disable path, expected evidence, residual risk and stop condition.

Batch 35 can start only after Batch 24 governance, Batch 25 runtime contract, Batch 31 audit/observability, Batch 32 target consent, Batch 33 QA/performance/stabilization and Batch 34 packaging/docs closure are current.

docs.title: Actions Not Performed Without Approval
docs.text:
Batch 34 does not perform these actions without a separate explicit owner approval:

  • no live server launch;
  • no browser automation;
  • no provider calls;
  • no live external model/API calls;
  • no canonical graph mutation;
  • no plugin publication;
  • no external write;
  • no package registry or marketplace upload;
  • no hook activation;
  • no active schedules, automations or GitHub Actions creation;
  • no git add, commit, push or PR;
  • no Batch 35 execution.

docs.title: Risks And Failure Modes
docs.text:
• Treating packaging smoke as publish approval can create an unauthorized release.
  • Rebuilding a disposable site but not site/ leaves stale generated docs.
  • Missing docs registry/control-plane sync can make source-backed claims drift.
  • Plugin-cache mismatch can hide missing checked-in skills, especially docs-maintainer.
  • Mermaid external asset dependency can break offline documentation expectations.
  • Batch 35 can accidentally start live execution if approval surfaces are bundled together instead of separated.

docs.title: Next Action
docs.text: After Batch 34 docs and packaging evidence are current, the next safe artifact is the Batch 35 approval packet draft. Real testing execution, provider/API calls, canonical mutation and git release/PR actions remain blocked until their separate approvals exist.

docs.title: Project Code Graph
docs.text:
Source status: official + experiment

Эта страница фиксирует локальный Project Code Graph слой Product-Agent OS для Task 25 Batch 13-23. Он помогает быстро ориентироваться в кодовой базе через сгенерированный граф, query packets, cockpit и локальные индексы, но не заменяет исходные файлы, checked-in документацию, тесты, approval records или решения owner.

docs.title: Назначение
docs.text:
Project Code Graph отвечает за offline-навигацию по проекту:

  • сканирует workspace и строит file-level graph с узлами файлов, contains edges, fingerprints, spans и observation records;
  • добавляет Python AST overlays для package/module/class/function/method, import/call/test edges и unresolved call summaries;
  • добавляет docs/contracts/schema overlays для Markdown, OpenAPI/Swagger, AsyncAPI, DBML, SQL, JSON, YAML, Mermaid и PlantUML;
  • выдает bounded query packets для чтения графа без повторного чтения raw source bodies;
  • рендерит static cockpit как generated view для обзорной навигации;
  • добавляет extension surface для search index, backend gate, semantic retrieval, deterministic LLM proposals и closure evidence.

docs.title: Source-of-truth boundary
docs.text:
Generated graph artifacts are not source of truth. Они являются orientation evidence и cache-bound generated views.

Source of truth остается в исходных файлах проекта, checked-in документации, schema/contracts, тестах, approval packets, RUNLOG/TEST/EVALS evidence и явно принятых owner decisions. Граф, cockpit HTML/JSON, search/backend/semantic indexes, LLM proposal packets и extension closure reports не должны использоваться как самостоятельное доказательство архитектуры, runtime behavior, coverage, security posture или готовности релиза.

Без отдельного explicit approval запрещены live server, browser automation, provider/API calls, canonical graph mutation, git stage/commit/push/PR и любые external writes. Query и stage modes должны оставаться локальными, deterministic и generated-artifact-only.

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text:
Основной вход:

  • <workspace> для scan_project_code_graph.py;
  • optional previous manifest/graph для freshness, provenance и temporal edge invalidation/supersession;
  • existing project-code-graph.json или project-code-graph.jsonl для query mode;
  • approval packets только для approval-bound extension modes: backend, semantic index, LLM proposals и Batch 23 closure evidence.

Scanner читает локальные файлы проекта, но graph/query packets исключают raw source bodies по умолчанию и редактируют absolute paths или secret-like values. Stage output должен быть явной директорией, предпочтительно вне target workspace.

docs.title: Outputs And Artifacts
docs.text:
Базовые артефакты Batch 13-18:

  • .codex/product-agent-os/project-code-graph.json - основной graph JSON с write_policy: read_only, metadata, nodes, edges и observations.
  • .codex/product-agent-os/project-code-graph.jsonl - bounded JSONL serialization для agent consumption.
  • .codex/product-agent-os/project-cockpit.html - offline generated cockpit, review-only.
  • .codex/product-agent-os/project-cockpit.json - structured cockpit model and projection.
  • Graph analysis report из project_graph_analysis.py - source-free orientation report, не доказательство completeness.
  • Status/runtime summaries из query packets и cockpit model - compact health/orientation summaries.

Extension artifacts Batch 19-23:

  • .codex/product-agent-os/project-code-graph-search-index.json - offline static search index with stale-index blocking and rollback path.
  • .codex/product-agent-os/project-code-graph-backend.json - disabled-by-default local query backend store; no active server by default.
  • .codex/product-agent-os/project-code-graph-semantic-index.json - local deterministic semantic retrieval cache; external embedding/cross-encoder providers remain approval-bound.
  • .codex/product-agent-os/project-code-graph-llm-proposals.json - staged local deterministic semantic extraction proposals with provenance, uncertainty and unsupported-claim labels.
  • .codex/product-agent-os/project-code-graph-extension-closure.json - Batch 23 verification, rollback/data deletion proof and graph-only fallback report.

docs.title: Operating Modes And Commands
docs.text:
Базовый scanner и stage-only generation:

python plugins\product-agent-os\scripts\scan_project_code_graph.py <workspace> --dry-run
python plugins\product-agent-os\scripts\scan_project_code_graph.py <workspace> --stage C:\tmp\product-agent-os-graph-stage

Graph-only queries читают существующий JSON/JSONL artifact:

python plugins\product-agent-os\scripts\scan_project_code_graph.py <workspace> --query status --graph C:\tmp\product-agent-os-graph-stage\.codex\product-agent-os\project-code-graph.json
python plugins\product-agent-os\scripts\scan_project_code_graph.py <workspace> --query neighbors --graph C:\tmp\product-agent-os-graph-stage\.codex\product-agent-os\project-code-graph.json --node-id function:app.main.main
python plugins\product-agent-os\scripts\scan_project_code_graph.py <workspace> --query search --graph C:\tmp\product-agent-os-graph-stage\.codex\product-agent-os\project-code-graph.json --text "runtime"

Supported query kinds include neighbors, path, trace, impact, affected_tests, changed_since, why_changed, read_order, hotspots, node, status and search. Query packets are bounded by --max-results, --max-depth, --max-tokens, filters and hub suppression.

Extension modes:

docs.title: Verification
docs.text:
Минимальная verification evidence для изменения этого слоя:

  • graph schema validation через project_graph_ontology.py;
  • redaction checks: no raw source bodies, no absolute local paths, no secret-like values in returned packets;
  • query packet checks for supported query kinds and bounded payloads;
  • cockpit validation: eight-page structure, generated-view wording, no external assets, static fallback path;
  • search-quality evals: symbol recall, top-k/MRR, trace labels, affected-test precision, edge density and thresholds;
  • extension validation: stale index blocking, disabled backend lifecycle, local deterministic semantic retrieval, proposal labels, rollback/data deletion proof and graph-only fallback.

Batch 18 recorded focused/full closure for graph/cockpit/search/status/runtime, fixture/lifecycle/docs suites, full unittest, fixture eval, transcript eval, Codex compatibility, strict MkDocs and diff hygiene. For new changes, rerun only the smallest relevant checks unless ownership expands.

docs.title: Risks And Failure Modes
docs.text:
• Dynamic dispatch, framework wiring, runtime routes and actual execution behavior are not fully proven by static graph edges.
  • Semantic hits and LLM proposals are orientation evidence; unsupported or uncertain claims must stay labeled and reviewable.
  • Stale graph/index artifacts can mislead readers if source files changed after generation.
  • Local backend store is a generated file-store and remains disabled by default; it is not a production server.
  • Cockpit is static generated output; visual completeness does not prove source correctness.
  • Stage directories inside a target workspace can blur source/generated boundaries unless explicitly approved.
  • Future provider-backed retrieval, live runtime, canonical mutation and release actions require separate approval packets and rollback plans.

docs.title: Task 22 scenario closure
docs.text:
Task 22 scenario closure связывает user-job routes with methodology packets and finish_options. Routes such as bug_rescue, greenfield_idea, api_migration, ai_eval_regression, security_sensitive_change and release_packaging must return a safe_next_action, minimum artifacts, approval boundary and evidence requirements without forcing unrelated methodology gates.

Finish options are bounded by lifecycle status: read-only routes can ask for context, stage a proposal or stop for approval; they cannot claim completion, create external writes or start automation from detection alone. Источники: Codex workflows, Codex use cases, Agent approvals and security, Product-Agent OS plugin, Behavioral evals, Codex compatibility.

Эта страница отвечает на практический вопрос: какой route должен выбрать Product-Agent OS plugin, когда Codex App, CLI или IDE extension видит реальный workspace и пользователь просит не просто "написать код", а довести работу до проверяемого результата.

Сценарий не заменяет lifecycle. Он выбирает первый малый шаг, minimum artifacts, approval boundary и verification gates. Если evidence нет, route должен вернуть gap, а не готовность.

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text:
• цель пользователя или intent_hint, если он передан в Codex runtime runner;
  • read-only workspace audit: файлы, stack, test/build commands, docs, CI, contracts, control-plane files;
  • текущие AGENTS.md, REQUIREMENTS.md, PLAN.md, TEST.md, EVALS.md, RUNLOG.md;
  • source policy, sandbox, approvals и known external-system boundaries;
  • предыдущие failure notes, если они уже записаны в RUNLOG.md.

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text:
• usage_mode.primary, secondary, confidence и routing reasons;
  • first response: один ближайший полезный шаг без широкого scaffold, rewrite или external mutation;
  • minimum artifacts: конкретные файлы или packets, которые нужны до build/review/release;
  • approval boundary: что можно делать read-only или staged-only, а что требует explicit approval;
  • verification gates: команды, evals, screenshots, logs, owner review или accepted gap;
  • residual risk, если route основан на detection, а не на verified evidence.

docs.title: Guided Question Protocol And Status Dashboard
docs.text:
Guided question protocol uses typed question_queue packets so the first response can show only next_blocking_question, question_counts and question_summary. It asks one blocking question maximum, keeps recommended and optional questions in the packet, and routes answers into artifacts or accepted gaps. Guided questions are not workspace evidence and do not replace read-only audit, current command evidence, runtime evidence, owner review or accepted gaps.

The status snapshot is the JSON source for a generated dashboard view. The dashboard stages .codex/product-agent-os/status.html and .codex/product-agent-os/status.json through the existing approval flow. status.html is generated view only: underlying artifacts remain the source material, the dashboard is not an editable database, and stale or inspection-only evidence cannot produce a success claim.

docs.title: Task 24 Self-Verification And Modernization Loop
docs.text:
Task 24 adds the agent_skill_metrics_loop route for agent, skill, prompt/policy pack, router/tool policy and harness-version review. This self-verification metrics loop starts from a read-only target registry, explicit run evidence, trace intake, dataset quality checks, local grader summaries and grader/judge calibration. It can stage scorecard ledger records, daily or weekly packets, agent-skill-evaluation-report.html, and modernization candidates, but every output is staged evidence only.

The route uses source-of-truth policy: control-plane artifacts, run records, trace/eval packets and accepted gaps can support the metrics loop; dashboard HTML, report HTML, memory, raw chat logs and unsupported community claims cannot. The report is not source of truth and cannot turn stale or generated evidence into a completion claim.

The approval boundary stays strict. Product-Agent OS records cadence recommendation values L0, L1, L2 and L3, but it creates no active schedules. It performs no live eval/model/API calls, makes no external writes, applies no modernization candidates by itself, and allows no self-applied updates. Owner review, rollback target and explicit approval state are required before any proposed update moves beyond staged review.

docs.title: Scenario Matrix
docs.text: usage_mode When it applies first response minimum artifacts approval boundary verification gates first-run-intake Empty workspace, broken verification, existing control-plane or complex first launch. Name mode, confidence, next smallest action and evidence gaps. Intake summary, current lifecycle state, next action. No scaffold, broad fix or parallel work before route is accepted. Read-only audit, control-plane check, source policy. bug_rescue User reports broken behavior, failing tests or regression. Reproduce or isolate before changing code. bug-rescue-report.md, failure evidence, root-cause hypothesis. No fix claim without reproduction evidence. Failing command/log, focused regression check, current evidence. greenfield_idea Idea-stage or empty product direction. Shape one vertical slice before scaffold. greenfield-idea-brief.md, selected direction, non-goals. Scaffold requires explicit approval. Acceptance scenarios, first slice plan, lightweight-mode decision. complex_system_acceleration Existing multi-surface app, integrations, multiple services or unclear ownership. Build map before parallelization. integration-catalog.md, ownership split, release gates. No parallel work with overlapping files or unclear external-system owners. Integration inventory, ownership review, release risk gates. pr_review Review or merge-readiness request. Stay read-only and review changed files. PR review readiness, changed-files map, pr-risk-review.md. No push, PR creation, merge or external comment without approval. Two-stage review: spec compliance before quality/risk. legacy_onboarding Old, undocumented or unknown repository. Orient before refactor. onboarding-map.md, entry points, run commands, docs debt. No cleanup/refactor until map and verification status are explicit. Present-unverified labels, source map, run command evidence. api_migration HTTP API, event contract, generated client or consumer change. Plan compatibility before implementation. migration-plan.md, api-contract-review.md, consumers, rollout. Release or breaking change needs owner review and approval. Contract check, backward compatibility, deprecation and rollout evidence. ai_eval_regression AI/RAG quality, prompt, model, retrieval, dataset or judge changes. Baseline first. ai-eval-spec.md, dataset policy, rubric, thresholds. No quality claim from inspection-only evidence. Baseline, rerun command, latency/cost/grounding and failure examples. native_mobile_feature iOS, Android or native mobile behavior. Record platform assumptions before implementation. Platform runtime check, permissions, offline/device plan. Permission, signing or store changes require approval. Build command, simulator/emulator or device logs, screenshots, manual gap. desktop_local_first Desktop app, filesystem, local DB, indexing or packaging. Map local data and OS assumptions first. Local data risk note, runtime log check, recovery path. Filesystem access, packaging, signing and distribution require approval. App logs, build/run command, privacy and rollback evidence. data_migration Schema, backfill, sensitive data, retention or production data risk. Plan migration and rollback before execution. migration-plan.md, database-dictionary.md, data quality checks. Production DB/data access and migration execution require approval. Dry run, backup, validation, owner review, rollback evidence. security_sensitive_change Authn/authz, payment, billing, secrets, PII, abuse controls or permissions. Threat surface and owner review before build. security-risk-review.md, approval boundary, rollback plan. Security scans or external security mutations only when explicitly requested. Tests, audit logging, rate limit, privacy and owner review evidence. ci_stabilization Failing, flaky or unstable CI. Gather failure evidence before changing code. ci-stabilization-report.md, failing job, local reproduction. Remote CI reruns, settings and branch rules require approval. Logs, deterministic/flaky classification, isolation plan, rerun evidence. release_packaging Package, SDK, plugin, app, mobile, desktop or open-source release. Build release readiness before publish. release-readiness.md, package metadata, changelog, artifacts. Publishing, tagging, release creation, upload or package registry mutation require approval. Build/test/docs evidence, security/license notes, rollback and owner review. docs_only Documentation update without behavior change. Update source-backed docs and run docs checks. Source status, affected docs, registry entry when source-backed claims changed. Hosted docs, CI activation and sharing changes require approval. python tools\check_docs.py, strict MkDocs when nav/build-sensitive. standard_feature Bounded feature work without special scenario risk. Use normal lifecycle route. Requirements, plan, test/eval evidence. Writes follow sandbox and project approval policy. Unit/integration/contract checks, docs impact, review. maintenance Small upkeep, formatting or status sync. Keep scope mechanical and evidence explicit. RUNLOG note or control-plane sync. No unrelated refactor. Focused command or explicit inspection-only gap.

docs.title: Database & Data methodology routing
docs.text:
Database/data work keeps the Track 8 data_migration route for compatibility, but Track 9 also adds a dedicated Database & Data methodology packet. When schema, migration, ORM, warehouse, data quality, lineage, retention, backup/restore or production-data signals appear, the route should stage or request database-specific evidence before implementation or execution.

Minimum staged artifacts include database-inventory.md, database-dictionary.md, database-migration-plan.md, database-data-contract.md, database-backup-restore-evidence.md, database-lineage-map.md, database-query-performance-review.md, database-retention-deletion-policy.md, database-synthetic-fixtures-policy.md and database-production-access-approval.md when production data, production DB access, backup restore or destructive migration is involved.

Approval boundary stays explicit: DB introspection, production DB access, production data access, migration execution, destructive cleanup, backup restore and retention mutation are not automatic actions.

docs.title: LLM / AI / RAG methodology routing
docs.text:
AI/RAG work keeps the Track 8 ai_eval_regression route for compatibility, but Track 9 also adds a dedicated LLM / AI / RAG methodology packet. When prompts, models, eval configs, structured outputs, tool/function/MCP calls, RAG corpora, retrieval, vector stores, embeddings, grounding, agent traces, guardrails or latency/cost signals appear, the route should stage or request AI/RAG-specific evidence before implementation or quality claims.

Minimum staged artifacts include ai-behavior-spec.md, prompt-contract.md, model-decision-record.md, eval-run-report.md, ai-dataset-manifest.md, structured-output-schema.md, ai-tool-contract.md, rag-source-inventory.md, rag-retrieval-config.md, rag-eval-report.md, grounding-rubric.md, agent-task-packet.md, agent-workflow-map.md, guardrail-matrix.md, trace-evidence-packet.md, ai-cost-latency-budget.md and the existing ai-eval-spec.md when user-visible AI behavior changes. agent-handoff-contract.md is a legacy/source alias to agent-task-packet.md, not a duplicate generated contract.

Eval tooling remains conditional: Promptfoo, OpenAI Evals, pytest/Jest app-backed evals, Ragas and LangSmith are recorded as selected, rejected or deferred choices based on stack/privacy/CI fit. Model migration records snapshot or approved alias, prompt migration impact, compatibility checks, rollback, minimum threshold and sampling parameter rationale. RAG evidence records deletion path, retention, source exclusion, stale-source pruning, privacy owner, vector store lifecycle and deletion propagation. Failed evals, hallucination reports, unsafe outputs, tool misuse or data exposure route to an AI incident workflow with severity, mitigation, follow-up eval and Security/Privacy handoff.

Approval boundary stays explicit: live model calls, external eval services, vector DB access, raw prompts/traces/customer text, tool writes, shell/money/data exposure and irreversible side effects are not automatic actions.

docs.title: Security, Privacy & Compliance methodology routing
docs.text:
Security-sensitive work keeps the Track 8 security_sensitive_change route for compatibility, but Track 9 also adds a dedicated Security, Privacy & Compliance methodology packet. When authn/authz, permissions, secrets, PII, sensitive data, payment/billing, abuse controls, audit logging, supply chain, SBOM/provenance, CI permissions, AI/tool security, external writes, production data, policy changes or compliance overlays appear, the route should stage or request security-specific evidence before implementation or completion claims.

Minimum staged artifacts include security-risk-review.md, threat-surface.md, asvs-ssdf-mapping.md, authz-negative-test-matrix.md, secrets-policy.md, data-classification-register.md, privacy-impact-record.md, api-security-review.md, abuse-rate-limit-plan.md, supply-chain-review.md, sbom-manifest.md, ci-permissions-review.md, audit-logging-review.md, ai-security-review.md, compliance-overlay.md, vulnerability-response-record.md and approval-record.md when the corresponding risk applies. Source-era names such as threat-model.md, asvs-mapping.md, secrets-inventory.md, authz-matrix.md, audit-log-policy.md and compliance-applicability-matrix.md are aliases, not duplicate generated contracts.

Codex Security scans remain explicit opt-in: the route may recommend a scan or record not requested, but it must not imply that a scan ran from security terminology alone. Compliance overlays record applicability, owner, evidence, non-goals, gaps and review cadence without claiming legal compliance or certification.

Approval boundary stays explicit: payment/billing, production data, secret rotation, policy changes, external security-system mutations, external writes, publish actions and Codex Security scans are not automatic actions.

docs.title: Delivery, Release & Operations methodology routing
docs.text:
Release packaging keeps the Track 8 release_packaging route for compatibility, but Track 9 also adds a dedicated Delivery, Release & Operations methodology packet. When release, deploy, publish, package, versioning, changelog, artifact, rollout, rollback, CI/CD environment, release mode policy, build-release-run boundary, platform distribution evidence, release communication, versioning tooling, GitHub environment controls, SLO/observability, observability/on-call tooling, runbook, incident, postmortem, DORA, release integrity or automation promotion signals appear, the route should stage or request delivery-specific evidence before any release readiness, deployment, publishing or automation claim.

Minimum staged artifacts include versioning-policy.md, release-readiness.md, release-artifact-manifest.md, rollout-plan.md, rollback-recovery-plan.md, environment-matrix.md, deployment-plan.md, ci-cd-workflow-inventory.md, observability-map.md, slo-spec.md, operations-runbook.md, incident-record.md, postmortem.md, post-release-review.md, approval-record.md and automation-candidate.md when automation promotion is proposed.

Approval boundary stays explicit: publish, tag, release creation, artifact upload, deploy, package registry mutation, marketplace/store submission, CI/CD environment mutation and active automation remain approval_required. Automation candidates require manual success evidence, stable inputs/outputs, owner, verification, approval requirements, value evidence and rollback/disable path; active automation is still not created by the route.

Final release/operations depth also requires owner-reviewed release evidence sufficiency for the real risk. Mobile signing, DORA dashboard notes, release tooling config, generated release notes or a single observability tool remain present_unverified until platform owner evidence, team/process measurement design, selected/rejected/deferred tooling decisions, alert path and accepted gaps are recorded.

docs.title: Verification
docs.text:
• Route selection is covered by discovery tests, usage_mode fixture checks, and T8-GX false-positive fixtures for selected methodology/tooling gates.
  • Scenario behavior is covered by behavioral-workflows.json and run_fixture_eval.py.
  • Frontend methodology routing is covered by frontend_contract_present and the synthetic frontend-ui-app fixture: UI completion requires user-flow, component state, visual/accessibility/runtime/interaction evidence or an accepted gap, not Storybook-only or inspection-only evidence.
  • Backend methodology routing is covered by backend_contract_present and the synthetic backend-service-app fixture: backend completion requires backend-service-overview.md, backend-runtime-behavior.md, runtime/failure evidence, observability/SLO/health evidence, security/rollback evidence and owner reviewed sufficiency or accepted gap, not package docs or logs-only evidence.
  • API & Integrations methodology routing is covered by api_integrations_contract_present and synthetic API fixtures: API completion requires api-inventory.md, api-contract-review.md, api-consumer-map.md, api-contract-test-matrix.md, external-integration-approval.md and related compatibility/security/error/event/SDK evidence, not Swagger UI or schema-only evidence.
  • Database & Data methodology routing is covered by database_data_contract_present and synthetic database fixtures: database completion requires inventory, dictionary, schema source, migration plan, expand-contract, data contract, rollback/backup, classification, data quality, lineage, performance, retention, synthetic fixtures and production access approval evidence where applicable.
  • LLM / AI / RAG methodology routing is covered by llm_ai_rag_contract_present and synthetic AI/RAG fixtures: AI/RAG completion requires baseline/current eval, prompt/model/schema/tool/RAG/grounding/trace/guardrail/cost evidence, handoff/tooling/migration/lifecycle/incident evidence and current-run evidence, not prompt inspection, stale eval output, citations-only grounding, filename-only diffs or automatic model-upgrade quality claims.
  • Security, Privacy & Compliance methodology routing is covered by security_privacy_compliance_contract_present and synthetic security fixtures: security completion requires security-sensitive classification, threat surface, ASVS/SSDF/SAMM mapping, authz negative tests, secrets/data/privacy evidence, supply-chain/SBOM/CI evidence, audit logging, compliance overlay taxonomy, vulnerability response workflow, explicit Codex Security scan status and owner/approval evidence, not docs-only security articles or implied scan/compliance claims.
  • Delivery, Release & Operations methodology routing is covered by delivery_release_operations_contract_present and synthetic release fixtures: release/deploy/publish/package/operations completion requires release scope, versioning, changelog, artifact manifest, release evidence, rollout, rollback, CI/CD governance, SLO/observability, operations, incident, post-release review, release mode policy, build-release-run boundary, platform distribution evidence, release communication, DORA team/process measurement, release integrity security handoff, owner-reviewed release evidence sufficiency and approval evidence, not docs-only release notes, CI files, deployment manifests, feature flags, GitOps files, mobile signing alone, DORA individual quota, tooling files without owner evidence or repeatable automation scripts alone.
  • Docs and source claims are checked by tools/check_docs.py, source policy and strict MkDocs when navigation changes.
  • Completion language must pass evidence-before-completion: current command evidence, current eval evidence, current runtime evidence, owner evidence or explicit inspection-only gap.

docs.title: Risks
docs.text:
• Workspace signals can identify a likely scenario but cannot prove readiness by themselves.
  • A scenario may be correct while the selected minimum artifacts are low quality; owner review still matters.
  • Approval boundaries are project-specific. Product-Agent OS can mark them, but the user or workspace policy decides whether to proceed.
  • Transcript/session eval runner now replays synthetic or redacted session fixtures with deterministic expected/forbidden term checks and privacy/no-secrets guards; semantic judgment still needs reviewer or future calibrated judge coverage.

Next artifact: use Behavioral evals to validate that the scenario route resists shortcuts and produces the expected evidence.
