docs.title: Safety Rules
docs.text:
All Track 2 skills must state:

  • do not store secrets, tokens, credentials, private keys, private customer data, or raw private chat logs;
  • do not mutate global config;
  • do not perform destructive commands;
  • do not create active automations;
  • do not write generated infrastructure directly in this track;
  • do not claim verification passed without command evidence from the current run;
  • ask for approval before external writes, permission changes, deployment, billing, auth, database, or production operations.

docs.title: Validation Strategy
docs.text:
Track 2 is verified with Python unittest tests that inspect packaged skill files and references. The tests should not execute Codex skills. They validate:

  • all required skill directories and SKILL.md files exist;
  • every skill has required frontmatter fields;
  • every skill has required body headings;
  • every skill has agents/openai.yaml with display name, short description, default prompt, and allow_implicit_invocation: false;
  • orchestrator routing covers every lifecycle state from contracts.py;
  • no skill claims it can perform out-of-scope writes for Track 2;
  • no skill stores or asks to store secrets;
  • no skill creates active automations;
  • reference files exist and include lifecycle, handoff, source policy, and complexity routing content;
  • references named in skill bodies resolve to existing files.

The final verification commands are:

python -m unittest discover -s tests -p "test_*.py" -v
python tools\check_docs.py
$env:PYTHONPATH='C:\tmp\codex_docs_mkdocs'; python -m mkdocs build --strict

docs.title: Acceptance Criteria
docs.text:
Track 2 is complete when:

  • packaged lifecycle skills exist under plugins/product-agent-os/skills/;
  • each skill is concise and follows the common contract;
  • each skill has UI metadata in agents/openai.yaml;
  • routing covers all lifecycle states from Track 1 contracts;
  • skills produce staged packets and do not silently write project infrastructure;
  • tests validate structure, routing, boundaries, references, UI metadata, and source or secret policy;
  • docs checks and strict MkDocs build pass.

docs.title: Self-Review
docs.text: This design is intentionally limited to lifecycle skills. It does not include generated project infrastructure, project-scoped agents, hooks, active automations, or an Agents SDK runner. Those remain separate tracks so each layer can be tested and reviewed independently.

docs.title: Product-Agent OS Production Hardening Design
docs.text:
Source status: official + experiment

Sources: Product-Agent OS plugin spec, Track 1 core plan, Track 2 lifecycle skills design, Track 3 generated infrastructure design, Track 3 implementation plan, source registry.

This design defines Track 4 for the product-agent-os plugin. It starts from the completed Track 3 baseline: deterministic staged infrastructure rendering, dry-run JSON output, staged artifact generation, fixture eval coverage, generated templates, validators, and clean verification on 2026-05-14.

docs.title: Goal
docs.text:
Track 4 turns the staged-first infrastructure generator into a production-hardened workflow that can be used on real projects without weakening the safety model.

The output is a hardened Product-Agent OS layer with:

  • a safe approved merge workflow for applying staged artifacts;
  • a staged artifact manifest that records provenance, digests, renderer validation, and intended write policy;
  • an explicit approval record that is separate from the merge plan id;
  • stronger fixture evals and failure-log regression cases;
  • source-policy validation for docs and generated guidance;
  • automation promotion gates that keep recurring work candidate-only until evidence and approval exist;
  • an optional Agents SDK runner design path that remains separate from the default plugin workflow.

docs.title: Design Choice
docs.text:
Use a gated hardening layer.

Track 4 should keep Track 3's default behavior unchanged: render plans and staged artifacts first, then require explicit approval before project writes. Production behavior is added through separate validators, merge plans, approval records, and eval reports.

Rejected approaches:

  • Direct apply by default: faster for greenfield projects, but too risky for existing AGENTS.md, .codex/config.toml, hooks, workflows, and user-authored project conventions.
  • Only add more templates: safe, but does not solve the real production gaps: approved merge, regression evidence, source drift, and automation readiness.
  • Build a full Agents SDK runtime immediately: powerful, but it expands the risk surface before the plugin's local hardening layer is proven.

Recommended approach:

  1. Harden local merge and validation first.
  2. Expand fixture evals around real failure modes.
  3. Add source and automation gates as deterministic validators.
  4. Keep the Agents SDK runner as an optional Track 4B design/prototype path, not part of default plugin activation.

docs.title: Existing Foundation
docs.text:
Track 1 already provides:

  • plugin manifest and package skeleton under plugins/product-agent-os/;
  • lifecycle state and handoff contracts in contracts.py;
  • workspace discovery in discovery.py and detect_project.py;
  • validation wrappers for control-plane files, agents, and hooks;
  • merge_markdown.py for managed Markdown sections;
  • fixture projects and fixture eval runner.

Track 2 already provides:

  • lifecycle skills under plugins/product-agent-os/skills/;
  • shared references for lifecycle state, handoff, source policy, and complexity routing;
  • static tests that prevent lifecycle skills from creating infrastructure, active automations, hooks, MCP servers, or an Agents SDK runner.

Track 3 already provides:

  • templates.py template registry;
  • infrastructure.py dry-run and stage renderer;
  • render_infrastructure.py CLI wrapper;
  • templates for control-plane files, .codex/config.toml, agents, hooks, workflows, evals, runlog archive, automation candidates, and PR/release packets;
  • renderer actions: create, update, leave_unchanged, blocked;
  • validation for agents, hooks, hook lifecycle config, eval JSON, staged config, and unresolved substitution markers;
  • fixture behavior checks for existing config, duplicate managed sections, monorepo ownership, source registry warning, unsafe write, and failed verification evidence.

docs.title: Problem Statement
docs.text:
Track 3 proves that Product-Agent OS can produce safe staged proposals. It does not yet prove that the proposals can be applied safely to a real project.

Production use introduces additional risks:

  • a staged artifact can be stale by the time a user approves it;
  • a merge can escape the workspace through path traversal, symlinks, or malformed staged paths;
  • user-authored files can be overwritten if unmarked content is treated as generated content;
  • source-backed documentation can drift from official OpenAI docs or local source registry entries;
  • automation candidates can become active recurring work without enough manual evidence;
  • fixture evals can pass structurally while missing behavior-level regressions;
  • an Agents SDK runner can blur ownership, approvals, and secrets unless it is isolated from default plugin behavior.

Track 4 must close these gaps without turning Product-Agent OS into an uncontrolled writer.

docs.title: Scope
docs.text: Track 4 adds five workstreams.

docs.title: 1. Safe Approved Merge
docs.text:
Add a merge workflow that can apply staged artifacts only after an explicit approval step.

Required capabilities:

  • produce a merge plan from a workspace and a Track 3 staging directory;
  • require a staged manifest generated by the renderer before any apply command;
  • require an explicit approval record before any apply command;
  • verify target paths stay inside the workspace;
  • reject symlink escapes and parent-directory traversal;
  • compute target and staged content digests;
  • detect stale targets before applying a plan;
  • preserve user-authored content outside managed sections;
  • apply managed Markdown section updates only when the target has a safe marker state or an approved append strategy;
  • keep unmarked .toml, .json, .py, and hook files as companion proposals unless a later narrower rule proves a safe merge;
  • keep hook activation as a separate approval gate;
  • write backups and a rollback manifest before any project write;
  • provide a rollback command that can restore a recorded apply only when current digests still match the post-apply manifest;
  • report every write, skip, and block in a machine-readable result.

docs.title: 2. Stronger Fixture Evals
docs.text:
Expand fixture evals from structural renderer checks into behavior-level regression checks.

Required capabilities:

  • convert documented failure logs into deterministic regression cases;
  • fixture cases for stale merge plans, symlink escape attempts, path traversal, invalid staged manifest, broken rollback backup, missing approval, invalid source policy, and invalid automation promotion;
  • stable JSON results with expected checks, observed decisions, evidence paths, and failure reasons;
  • golden behavior summaries that explain why a fixture is ok, blocked, or needs_approval;
  • full fixture eval remains deterministic and requires no network access or secrets.

docs.title: 3. Source-Policy Hardening
docs.text:
Add deterministic source-policy checks for docs and generated guidance.

Required capabilities:

  • verify every non-index docs page keeps Source status:;
  • verify source-backed Product-Agent OS pages declare official docs, local specs, or source registry entries;
  • keep community claims under insight cards or explicitly marked community or experiment;
  • reject source-policy output that stores secrets, credentials, private customer data, or raw private chat logs;
  • mark freshness risk for current APIs, models, security, approvals, hooks, Agents SDK, MCP, and automation behavior;
  • produce a source-policy report that separates supported facts, assumptions, unsupported claims, and missing context;
  • classify semantic source ambiguity as needs_review instead of pretending deterministic text scanning can prove every factual claim.

docs.title: 4. Automation Promotion Gates
docs.text:
Harden automation candidates without creating active schedules.

Required capabilities:

  • parse automation candidate packets;
  • require owner, cadence, stable inputs, stable outputs, verification, failure modes, rollback or disable path, write policy, and explicit approval status;
  • require at least two manual successful runs or equivalent fixture evidence before a candidate can be marked ready for manual approval;
  • classify promotion state as candidate_only, ready_for_manual_approval, or blocked;
  • never create Codex App automations, GitHub Actions, schedules, recurring jobs, or external workflows inside Track 4 validators.

docs.title: 5. Optional Agents SDK Runner Design
docs.text:
Define an optional runner path for teams that need programmable orchestration.

Track 4 may add a design packet and validation contract for an Agents SDK runner. It should not make the runner part of the default Product-Agent OS plugin path.

Required design boundaries:

  • Manager agent owns lifecycle state and final output;
  • specialist agents are tools or handoff targets with explicit ownership;
  • every durable runner role has model and reasoning policy, escalation rules, downgrade rules, and cost or latency budget;
  • Codex MCP is treated as an execution backend, not as an approval bypass;
  • guardrails validate handoff completeness, source fidelity, tool boundaries, and secret retention;
  • sessions and tracing are application-level concerns and must not replace checked-in project rules, RUNLOG.md, or source registry records;
  • traces and sessions must have redaction and retention rules before real project use;
  • dependency installation and network access are separate setup steps, not implicit fixture behavior;
  • OpenAI credentials are read from environment or platform configuration only and never written to templates, fixtures, docs, memory, or runlogs.

docs.title: Use-Case Alignment
docs.text:
Track 4 maps to official use-case archetypes recorded in Codex use cases deep analysis.

Track 4 workstream Use-case group Why it matters Safe approved merge Tooling; PR and production review Creates an agent-friendly local CLI and prevents unreviewed production changes. Stronger fixture evals AI quality; PR and production review Converts hardening behavior into repeatable regression checks. Source-policy hardening Knowledge and product; PR and production review Keeps docs and generated guidance grounded in source status and reviewable claims. Automation promotion gates Operations and collaboration Prevents premature recurring work and aligns automation with verified operations. Optional Agents SDK runner Tooling; long-running creation Provides a later programmable orchestration path without making it the default plugin runtime.

Implementation plans for Track 4 should reference these groups when adding new playbooks, skills, plugin metadata, or automation candidates.

docs.title: Out Of Scope
docs.text:
Track 4 does not:

  • silently mutate user projects;
  • replace user-authored files without managed-section boundaries and explicit approval;
  • change global Codex config;
  • enable packaged hooks automatically;
  • install dependencies or use network access during fixture evals;
  • create active automations, scheduled jobs, GitHub Actions, recurring Codex App automations, or external workflows;
  • store secrets, credentials, private customer data, raw private chat logs, or absolute user-specific paths;
  • claim project tests, builds, hooks, evals, or automations work unless the current run produced evidence;
  • implement a full production Agents SDK app as part of the default hardening path.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
Track 4 adds a hardening layer beside the existing renderer.

flowchart TD
    A["Workspace audit"] --> B["Track 3 renderer"]
    B --> C["Staged artifacts"]
    B --> D["Dry-run infrastructure plan"]
    C --> E["Track 4 merge planner"]
    D --> E
    E --> F{"Safe to apply?"}
    F -->|"No"| G["Blocked merge report"]
    F -->|"Needs approval"| H["Approval packet"]
    H --> I["Approved merge apply"]
    I --> J["Backup and rollback manifest"]
    I --> K["Applied project files"]
    C --> L["Fixture eval hardening"]
    D --> M["Source-policy validator"]
    D --> N["Automation promotion validator"]
    O["Optional Agents SDK runner design"] --> P["Separate gated prototype"]

The renderer remains the source of staged artifacts. Track 4 does not duplicate template rendering. It consumes renderer output, validates it more strictly, and controls the approved transition from staged artifacts to project files.

docs.title: Merge Workflow Contract
docs.text:
Track 4 should add a merge planner module and CLI wrapper.

Proposed files:

plugins/product-agent-os/scripts/product_agent_os/merge_infrastructure.py
plugins/product-agent-os/scripts/merge_infrastructure.py
tests/product_agent_os/test_merge_infrastructure.py

CLI contract:

python plugins\product-agent-os\scripts\merge_infrastructure.py <workspace> <stage-dir> --plan
python plugins\product-agent-os\scripts\merge_infrastructure.py <workspace> <stage-dir> --apply --approval-file <approval-file>
python plugins\product-agent-os\scripts\merge_infrastructure.py <workspace> <stage-dir> --rollback <rollback-manifest>

Plan mode is read-only. Apply mode writes only when:

  • the user explicitly selected --apply;
  • the staged manifest exists and matches the current staged files;
  • the approval file exists and names the current merge plan id;
  • the approval file names the approved target paths and write scope;
  • every write decision is included in the approved target path list;
  • the target digest still matches the digest recorded during plan generation;
  • every target path resolves inside the workspace;
  • no target parent or target file is a symlink;
  • validation passes for staged content and merge decisions;
  • every write has a rollback entry.

Approval id alone is not sufficient. A merge plan id proves that a plan is stable; it does not prove that the user approved the write. Track 4 approval is represented as a separate approval record.

Plan output should include an approval record template that a user or higher-level approved workflow can complete. The merge tool must not infer approval from its own plan output.

Staged manifest shape:

stage_manifest:
  schema_version: 1
  renderer: "product-agent-os"
  renderer_version: ""
  workspace_audit_digest: ""
  infrastructure_plan_digest: ""
  generated_at: ""
  validation:
    ok: true
    checks: []
    errors: {}
  files:
    - target_path: "AGENTS.md"
      staged_path: "AGENTS.md"
      action: "create | update | leave_unchanged | blocked"
      write_policy: "staged_only | approved_write_required | blocked"
      digest: "sha256:..."
      managed_section: "project-rules"

Approval record shape:

approval:
  schema_version: 1
  merge_plan_id: ""
  approved_by: "user"
  approved_at: ""
  approved_targets:
    - "AGENTS.md"
  approved_actions:
    - "create_file"
    - "append_managed_section"
    - "replace_managed_section"
  accepted_risks: []
  denied_targets: []
  notes: ""

The approval record is local evidence for the merge command. It is not a substitute for platform-level sandbox or filesystem approvals when those are required by the current runtime.

Merge plan shape:

merge_plan:
  id: "stable digest from workspace, stage manifest, and generated_at"
  status: "needs_approval | blocked | applied"
  workspace: ""
  stage_root: ""
  generated_at: ""
  decisions:
    - target_path: "AGENTS.md"
      staged_path: ""
      action: "create_file | append_managed_section | replace_managed_section | companion_only | blocked"
      reason: ""
      target_digest_before: ""
      staged_digest: ""
      approval_required: true
      rollback_entry: ""
  blocked:
    - target_path: ""
      reason: ""
  warnings: []
  verification:
    ok: true
    checks: []
    errors: {}

Allowed merge actions:

Action Allowed when Write behavior create_file target does not exist and parent path is safe create file after backup manifest records absence append_managed_section target is Markdown, has no conflicting markers, and user approved append append managed Product-Agent OS section replace_managed_section target has exactly one matching managed section replace only that section companion_only target exists without safe managed merge path no project write; keep staged proposal blocked path, marker, digest, validation, or approval is unsafe no project write

Rollback requirements:

  • before writing, copy existing target content or record that the file was absent;
  • store rollback manifest under the staging directory, not in global user config;
  • for created files, rollback can remove only files whose current digest still matches the generated digest;
  • for updated files, rollback can restore only when the current digest matches the post-apply digest;
  • rollback reports are evidence artifacts, not hidden state.

Rollback manifest shape:

rollback_manifest:
  schema_version: 1
  merge_plan_id: ""
  applied_at: ""
  entries:
    - target_path: "AGENTS.md"
      action: "created | updated"
      existed_before: false
      digest_before: ""
      digest_after: "sha256:..."
      backup_path: ""
  verification:
    ok: true
    checks: []

Rollback mode is conservative. It refuses to restore or remove a file when the current target digest differs from the recorded post-apply digest, because that means another actor changed the file after apply.

docs.title: Hook Activation Gate
docs.text:
Track 3 stages hook scripts and .codex/hooks/hooks.json as target-project assets. Track 4 may merge hook files into a workspace, but activation remains a separate decision.

Rules:

  • hook scripts can be merged only after validator success and explicit approval;
  • .codex/hooks/hooks.json defaults to companion_only unless the approval record includes enable_hooks;
  • enabling hooks requires an approval record that names hook events, scripts, blocking behavior, and rollback path;
  • pre_tool_use_policy.py blocking rules must stay narrow and auditable;
  • hook activation must never happen from plugin-root lifecycle config;
  • fixture eval must include one case where hook scripts are staged but hook activation is not approved, and one case where approval enables hook config safely.

Hook approval extension:

approval:
  enable_hooks: false
  approved_hook_events: []
  blocking_hooks:
    - "PreToolUse"
  hook_rollback: "remove or restore .codex/hooks/hooks.json when current digest matches post-apply digest"

docs.title: Fixture Eval Hardening
docs.text:
Track 4 should extend run_fixture_eval.py rather than replace it.

Additional fixture projects:

plugins/product-agent-os/assets/fixtures/stale-merge-plan/
plugins/product-agent-os/assets/fixtures/path-traversal-stage/
plugins/product-agent-os/assets/fixtures/symlink-escape/
plugins/product-agent-os/assets/fixtures/hook-activation-unapproved/
plugins/product-agent-os/assets/fixtures/hook-activation-approved/
plugins/product-agent-os/assets/fixtures/source-policy-conflict/
plugins/product-agent-os/assets/fixtures/automation-candidate-valid/
plugins/product-agent-os/assets/fixtures/automation-candidate-invalid/
plugins/product-agent-os/assets/fixtures/rollback-required/
plugins/product-agent-os/assets/fixtures/failure-log-regression/

Fixture result shape:

fixture: ""
ok: true
profile: ""
renderer_status: ""
merge_status: ""
source_policy_status: ""
automation_status: ""
expected_checks:
  safe_paths: true
  stale_digest_blocked: true
  source_policy_enforced: true
  automation_candidate_gated: true
evidence:
  files_inspected: []
  commands: []
  reports: []
risks: []

Behavior-level checks:

  • dry-run still writes no files;
  • stage mode writes only under the requested staging directory;
  • merge plan mode writes no files;
  • apply mode requires staged manifest and approval record;
  • unapproved apply is blocked;
  • stale target digest is blocked;
  • symlink and path traversal attempts are blocked;
  • existing unmarked .codex/config.toml remains companion-only;
  • hook scripts can be merged without activating .codex/hooks/hooks.json unless enable_hooks is approved;
  • failed verification evidence remains visible;
  • failure log entries can generate deterministic regression cases;
  • invalid automation candidate remains candidate-only or blocked;
  • source-policy conflict does not become an official claim.

docs.title: Failure-Log Regression Contract
docs.text:
Product-Agent OS should turn real hardening failures into future deterministic checks.

Input sources:

  • current RUNLOG.md;
  • .codex/runlogs/archive/;
  • fixture eval reports;
  • rollback manifests;
  • source-policy reports;
  • automation promotion reports.

Regression case shape:

regression_case:
  id: "stale-merge-plan-blocked"
  source: "RUNLOG.md#2026-05-14"
  failure_summary: ""
  reproduction_fixture: "stale-merge-plan"
  command: "python plugins\\product-agent-os\\scripts\\run_fixture_eval.py"
  expected_status: "blocked"
  expected_checks:
    stale_digest_blocked: true
  evidence_to_preserve:
    - "merge_plan.id"
    - "target_digest_before"
    - "blocked reason"

Rules:

  • a failure-log regression must name the original evidence source;
  • regression fixtures must use synthetic data only;
  • sensitive logs are summarized, not copied raw;
  • every regression case must have an expected command and observable expected result;
  • failure-log conversion may propose fixture additions but must not silently edit production projects.

docs.title: Source-Policy Validator
docs.text:
Track 4 should add a deterministic source-policy validator.

Proposed files:

plugins/product-agent-os/scripts/product_agent_os/source_policy.py
plugins/product-agent-os/scripts/validate_source_policy.py
tests/product_agent_os/test_source_policy.py

CLI contract:

python plugins\product-agent-os\scripts\validate_source_policy.py <workspace>

Report shape:

source_policy_report:
  status: "ok | needs_review | blocked"
  files:
    - path: ""
      source_status: "official | official + experiment | community | experiment | missing"
      supported_facts: []
      assumptions: []
      unsupported_claims: []
      missing_context: []
      freshness_risks: []
  registry_updates_required: []
  secret_findings: []
  errors: []

Rules:

  • docs pages must include Source status: unless exempt by project docs policy;
  • OpenAI, Codex, Agents SDK, model, approvals, hooks, MCP, and automation behavior claims require official sources or an explicit freshness risk;
  • Context7 is accepted as official only when the underlying source is official;
  • community claims require insight-card handling with trust_level and verification_status;
  • generated examples cannot contain secrets, private customer data, raw private chat logs, or absolute user-specific paths;
  • missing or stale source evidence yields needs_review unless the claim is safety-sensitive, in which case it yields blocked.

Deterministic boundary:

  • the validator can prove document structure, required markers, source registry references, forbidden literals, stale checked_at dates, and known unsupported-source patterns;
  • the validator cannot prove full semantic truth for every sentence;
  • when semantic truth is uncertain, output must be needs_review with a specific file path and reason;
  • only explicit high-risk patterns, forbidden literals, missing source status, or unsafe promotion of community claims should become blocked.

docs.title: Automation Promotion Validator
docs.text:
Track 4 should add an automation candidate validator.

Proposed files:

plugins/product-agent-os/scripts/product_agent_os/automation_policy.py
plugins/product-agent-os/scripts/validate_automation_candidate.py
tests/product_agent_os/test_automation_policy.py

CLI contract:

python plugins\product-agent-os\scripts\validate_automation_candidate.py <candidate-file>

Report shape:

automation_promotion_report:
  status: "candidate_only | ready_for_manual_approval | blocked"
  candidate_file: ""
  required_fields_present: true
  manual_success_count: 0
  owner_present: true
  cadence_present: true
  verification_present: true
  failure_modes_present: true
  rollback_or_disable_present: true
  write_policy_present: true
  explicit_approval_present: false
  errors: []
  warnings: []

Promotion rules:

  • candidate_only is the default state;
  • ready_for_manual_approval requires stable inputs, stable outputs, owner, cadence, verification, failure modes, rollback or disable path, explicit write policy, and at least two manual successful runs or equivalent fixture evidence;
  • blocked is required for missing owner, missing verification, missing rollback or disable path, ambiguous writes, external side effects without approval, or any secret-like content;
  • validator output must not create schedules or call automation APIs.

docs.title: Optional Agents SDK Runner Boundary
docs.text:
Track 4 should include only a bounded runner design unless the user separately approves implementation.

Proposed design artifact:

docs/superpowers/specs/2026-05-14-product-agent-os-agents-sdk-runner-design.md

Possible future implementation root:

plugins/product-agent-os/scripts/agents_sdk_runner/

Runner responsibilities:

  • read Product-Agent OS control-plane artifacts;
  • create a Manager agent that owns lifecycle routing;
  • expose specialist roles as tools or handoff targets;
  • call Codex MCP only within explicit sandbox and approval policy;
  • validate handoff payloads before continuing;
  • keep sessions and tracing separate from checked-in project memory;
  • fail closed when credentials, sources, approval state, or write ownership are unclear.
  • record model, reasoning, tool, handoff, latency, failure, and approval events in traces without storing secrets.

Runner non-goals:

  • no default dependency installation;
  • no default network access in plugin verification;
  • no credential creation or storage;
  • no direct replacement for Codex App, CLI, project skills, or .codex/agents;
  • no automation scheduling from inside the runner.

Runner design must define:

  • dependency setup path and offline test fallback;
  • model and reasoning defaults per role;
  • environment variable names for credentials without exposing values;
  • session retention and redaction policy;
  • tracing retention and redaction policy;
  • eval suite for handoff completeness, source fidelity, tool boundary, approval handling, and secret retention;
  • rollback or shutdown path for partial runner execution.

docs.title: Security And Approval Model
docs.text:
Track 4 must preserve least privilege.

Approval required for:

  • applying staged files to a workspace;
  • appending managed sections to unmarked Markdown files;
  • enabling hooks;
  • creating or updating automation schedules outside Track 4 validators;
  • writing external systems;
  • changing source-of-truth docs, registry records, or release artifacts;
  • using an Agents SDK runner against a real workspace.

Blocked by default:

  • path traversal and symlink escape;
  • stale merge plans;
  • destructive commands embedded in generated assets;
  • global Codex config mutation;
  • broad network access in tests or fixture evals;
  • secret-like literals in templates, fixtures, examples, docs, runlogs, automation candidates, or runner config;
  • active automation without manual stability evidence and explicit approval.

docs.title: Testing Strategy
docs.text:
Track 4 tests should remain deterministic unittest tests.

Required tests:

  • staged manifest is required before apply;
  • approval record is required before apply and cannot be replaced by a bare plan id;
  • approval record must name approved targets and actions;
  • merge planner produces read-only plans;
  • apply mode rejects missing approval record;
  • apply mode rejects approval records that do not match the current merge plan id;
  • apply mode rejects stale target digest;
  • apply mode rejects path traversal and symlink escape;
  • managed Markdown section replacement preserves user content outside markers;
  • unmarked Markdown append requires explicit approval;
  • unmarked .codex/config.toml stays companion-only;
  • hook scripts can be applied without enabling hook lifecycle config;
  • hook lifecycle config requires enable_hooks approval;
  • backups and rollback manifest are created before writes;
  • rollback mode restores created or updated files only when current digests match the post-apply digest;
  • rollback refuses to overwrite changed post-apply content;
  • source-policy validator detects missing source status and unsupported OpenAI behavior claims;
  • source-policy validator returns needs_review for semantic ambiguity instead of claiming proof;
  • source-policy validator separates official, community, experiment, and unsupported claims;
  • automation validator blocks incomplete candidates;
  • automation validator classifies complete candidates as ready for manual approval without creating a schedule;
  • fixture eval includes merge, hook activation, source-policy, automation, rollback, and failure-log regression statuses;
  • optional Agents SDK runner design is not part of default plugin activation.

Required verification commands after implementation:

python -m unittest discover -s tests -p "test_*.py" -v
python plugins\product-agent-os\scripts\run_fixture_eval.py
python tools\check_docs.py
$env:PYTHONPATH='C:\tmp\codex_docs_mkdocs'; python -m mkdocs build --strict

docs.title: Acceptance Criteria
docs.text:
Track 4 is complete when:

  • the plugin can generate a merge plan from Track 3 staged artifacts without writing to the workspace;
  • Track 3 stage output includes a manifest or Track 4 can create a verified manifest from staged artifacts before apply;
  • apply requires a separate approval record with approved target paths, actions, accepted risks, and approval timestamp;
  • approved apply mode writes only allowed files and sections inside the workspace;
  • stale, ambiguous, unsafe, or unapproved merge plans are blocked;
  • hook lifecycle config is not activated unless the approval record explicitly enables hooks;
  • every apply creates a rollback manifest and evidence report;
  • rollback can be executed and refuses unsafe restore conditions;
  • failure-log regression cases can be generated or validated from synthetic evidence;
  • fixture eval covers merge safety, stale state, path safety, hook activation, source-policy conflict, automation readiness, rollback behavior, and failure-log regression behavior;
  • source-policy validator produces deterministic ok, needs_review, or blocked reports;
  • automation validator keeps candidates candidate-only until evidence and explicit approval are present;
  • active automations are not created by Track 4 code;
  • optional Agents SDK runner remains isolated from the default plugin path;
  • full verification pack exits 0 in the current run.

docs.title: Residual Risks
docs.text:
Even after Track 4, Product-Agent OS still cannot prove that every generated workflow is product-correct for every real project. It can prove stronger safety properties around merge behavior, evidence, source policy, and automation readiness.

The optional Agents SDK runner remains a higher-risk architecture layer. It should move forward only after local hardening is implemented and a separate plan defines dependencies, credential handling, MCP boundaries, evals, and rollback.

Automation promotion remains a human-owned decision. Track 4 can validate readiness and produce an approval packet, but it should not infer business ownership, legal acceptability, customer impact, or operational cadence without explicit user input.

docs.title: Implementation Handoff
docs.text:
Implementation should be split into focused tasks:

  1. Stage manifest and approval record contracts.
  2. Merge plan data model and read-only planner.
  3. Approved apply mode with backup and rollback manifest.
  4. Rollback command and safety checks.
  5. Hook activation gate.
  6. Merge, hook, rollback, and failure-log fixture cases.
  7. Source-policy validator and tests.
  8. Automation promotion validator and tests.
  9. Fixture eval result expansion.
  10. Optional Agents SDK runner design artifact.
  11. Documentation, navigation, and full verification.

Each task must start with failing tests where practical, preserve Track 3 staged-first behavior, and avoid unrelated refactors.

docs.title: Spec Self-Review
docs.text:
Coverage:

  • stage manifest and approval record are specified as separate contracts;
  • safe approved merge is specified through merge plan, apply, rollback, and path-safety contracts;
  • hook activation is separated from hook file merge;
  • fixture eval hardening has explicit new fixtures and expected behaviors;
  • failure-log regression has input sources and case shape;
  • source-policy hardening has report shape and blocking rules;
  • automation gates have report shape and promotion states;
  • optional Agents SDK runner has a boundary and non-goals;
  • verification commands match project rules.

Scope check:

  • Track 4 is broad but still one coherent hardening layer around an existing plugin package;
  • the optional runner is explicitly separated so the implementation plan can defer it or place it in a gated final task.

Ambiguity check:

  • default behavior remains staged-first;
  • active automation creation is out of scope;
  • direct writes require explicit apply mode plus approval record;
  • bare merge plan id is not treated as user approval;
  • unmarked user-authored files are preserved unless a safe managed Markdown append is explicitly approved.

docs.title: Product-Agent OS Codex Runtime Runner Design
docs.text:
Source status: official + experiment

Sources: Product-Agent OS plugin spec, Product-Agent OS production hardening design, Product-Agent OS production hardening plan, Product-Agent OS Agents SDK runner boundary, source registry, Codex plugins, Codex skills, Codex subagents, Codex hooks, Agent approvals and security, Codex workflows.

This design supersedes the Track 5 standalone Agents SDK runner idea. The plugin will run only inside Codex surfaces: Codex App, CLI, IDE extension, plugin skills, subagents, hooks, staged renderer, approval-gated merge, and local validators. Track 5 therefore implements a Codex runtime runner, not an API-backed application and not a separate OpenAI Agents SDK service.

docs.title: Read-Only Analysis
docs.text:
The original Product-Agent OS spec defined four implementation tracks and treated Agents SDK as an advanced optional surface. Track 4 kept that path design-only because the default Product-Agent OS plugin already had a safer local workflow: lifecycle skills, staged infrastructure, explicit approval records, safe merge, rollback, source-policy validation, automation promotion validation, and fixture eval.

The current implementation confirms that this local Codex-first layer is the strongest foundation. Track 1-2 provide contracts, discovery, validators, lifecycle skills, and handoff references. Track 3 provides staged templates and renderer. Track 4 provides manifest-bound merge/apply/rollback and policy validators. The clean baseline before this spec change was: python -m unittest discover -s tests -p "test_*.py" -v ran 194 tests with OK, python plugins\product-agent-os\scripts\run_fixture_eval.py exited 0, and python tools\check_docs.py passed.

The implementation gap is now narrower: Product-Agent OS needs a Codex-only orchestrator that can read control-plane artifacts, choose the next lifecycle action, validate handoffs, route to packaged skills or project-scoped subagents, and emit evidence. It must not introduce separate API credentials, external runtime dependency installation, or an out-of-Codex agent service.

docs.title: Goal
docs.text:
Implement the smallest useful Codex runtime runner that turns Product-Agent OS from a set of skills and validators into a coherent local orchestration layer inside Codex.

The runner must:

  • read Product-Agent OS context from AGENTS.md, REQUIREMENTS.md, PLAN.md, TEST.md, EVALS.md, and RUNLOG.md;
  • infer lifecycle state and recommended next action;
  • route to packaged Product-Agent OS skills and generated subagent role configs;
  • validate structured handoffs before lifecycle advancement;
  • validate source policy, approval state, ownership boundaries, tool boundaries, and redaction;
  • produce a machine-readable codex_runner_result;
  • run deterministically in tests without network, external credentials, or package installation;
  • write nothing by default and never create active automations.

docs.title: Non-Goals
docs.text:
Track 5 does not:

  • implement a standalone OpenAI Agents SDK app;
  • call OpenAI APIs directly;
  • require API keys, external credentials, or environment-provided model access;
  • install openai-agents or other runtime dependencies;
  • run Codex as an MCP server from outside Codex;
  • make an external service, deployment target, or HTTP server;
  • bypass Codex sandbox, approvals, or plugin boundaries;
  • change global Codex config;
  • create Codex App automations, GitHub Actions, schedules, recurring jobs, or external workflows;
  • store secrets, private customer data, raw private chat logs, raw traces, or absolute user-specific paths.

docs.title: Design Choice
docs.text:
Use a Codex-only contract runner.

Rejected approaches:

  • Standalone Agents SDK runner: unnecessary for a plugin that will run only in Codex, and it would add credential, dependency, network, tracing, and deployment concerns.
  • Codex MCP bridge: useful when an external Agents SDK app wants Codex as a backend, but not needed when the plugin is already executing in Codex.
  • Implicit skill auto-runner: convenient, but too opaque. The runner must return a route packet and require explicit handoff/approval gates rather than silently invoking broad workflows.

Recommended approach:

  1. Add a dependency-free codex_runtime_runner package under the plugin scripts.
  2. Make it read-only by default and contract-first.
  3. Route lifecycle actions to existing Product-Agent OS skills, templates, validators, and generated subagent role configs.
  4. Extend fixture eval with runner status and regression checks.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    A["Codex workspace"] --> B["Control-plane loader"]
    B --> C["Lifecycle state detector"]
    C --> D["Route planner"]
    D --> E["Policy validators"]
    E --> F{"Safe next action?"}
    F -->|"No"| G["Blocked or needs context result"]
    F -->|"Yes"| H["Skill or subagent route packet"]
    H --> I["Handoff validator"]
    I --> J["Codex runner result"]
    J --> K["Fixture eval and RUNLOG evidence"]

The runner is a local helper, not a new runtime surface. Codex remains the execution plane. Existing skills remain the method layer. Existing safe merge and rollback remain the write gate.

docs.title: Proposed Files
docs.text:
Create:

  • plugins/product-agent-os/scripts/codex_runtime_runner/__init__.py - package marker and public version.
  • plugins/product-agent-os/scripts/codex_runtime_runner/contracts.py - request, route, handoff, result, and policy schemas.
  • plugins/product-agent-os/scripts/codex_runtime_runner/context_loader.py - safe control-plane reader.
  • plugins/product-agent-os/scripts/codex_runtime_runner/state.py - lifecycle state inference.
  • plugins/product-agent-os/scripts/codex_runtime_runner/routes.py - route planner from lifecycle state to skill or subagent task.
  • plugins/product-agent-os/scripts/codex_runtime_runner/guards.py - deterministic validators for source, approval, ownership, handoff, automation, and claims.
  • plugins/product-agent-os/scripts/codex_runtime_runner/redaction.py - deterministic redaction for secrets, private data markers, raw chat markers, and local absolute paths.
  • plugins/product-agent-os/scripts/codex_runtime_runner/cli.py - CLI implementation.
  • plugins/product-agent-os/scripts/run_codex_runtime_runner.py - CLI wrapper.
  • plugins/product-agent-os/scripts/validate_codex_runtime_runner.py - deterministic runner contract validator.
  • tests/product_agent_os/test_codex_runtime_runner_contracts.py
  • tests/product_agent_os/test_codex_runtime_runner_cli.py
  • tests/product_agent_os/test_codex_runtime_runner_guards.py
  • tests/product_agent_os/test_codex_runtime_runner_fixture_eval.py

Modify:

  • tests/product_agent_os/test_plugin_structure.py - prove runner exists but is not default-activated by plugin manifest.
  • plugins/product-agent-os/scripts/run_fixture_eval.py - add codex_runtime_runner_status and runner evidence.
  • mkdocs.yml - add this design to implementation specs navigation.
  • docs/sources/registry.md - refresh source cards used by Track 5.

Do not modify:

  • .codex-plugin/plugin.json capabilities unless a later review proves the plugin UI should expose a runner command.
  • Track 4 merge/apply/rollback behavior.
  • Automation policy that keeps recurring work candidate-only.

docs.title: Runner Mode
docs.text:
The runner has one default deterministic mode.

Command:

python plugins\product-agent-os\scripts\run_codex_runtime_runner.py <workspace> --contract

Behavior:

  • read safe control-plane files;
  • infer current lifecycle state;
  • build a route packet;
  • validate source policy and handoff requirements;
  • validate whether the next action is read-only, staged-only, approval-required, or blocked;
  • emit status: "route_ready" | "needs_context" | "needs_approval" | "blocked";
  • write nothing unless an explicit --output <file> path points inside a staging directory.

There is no live API mode. Model execution is supplied by the current Codex session or subagent mechanism, not by a separate runner process.

docs.title: Runner Request
docs.text:
codex_runner_request:
  schema_version: 1
  workspace: ""
  task:
    goal: ""
    lifecycle_state: ""
    constraints: []
    allowed_sources: []
    expected_artifacts: []
  routing:
    preferred_surface: "Codex App | CLI | IDE extension | codex exec | subagent | skill"
    allow_subagents: false
    allow_workspace_writes: false
  approval:
    required: false
    approval_file: ""
    approval_status: "not_required | required | approved | rejected | stale"

docs.title: Route Packet
docs.text:
codex_route_packet:
  lifecycle_state: ""
  next_action: ""
  recommended_skill: ""
  recommended_subagent_role: ""
  runtime_surface: ""
  write_policy: "read_only | staged_only | approved_write | blocked"
  required_inputs: []
  expected_outputs: []
  verification: []
  approval_requirements: []
  stop_conditions: []

docs.title: Handoff
docs.text:
codex_runner_handoff:
  lifecycle_state: ""
  role: ""
  goal: ""
  constraints: []
  sources_used: []
  assumptions: []
  verified_claims: []
  unsupported_claims: []
  files_touched: []
  files_proposed: []
  commands_run: []
  verification_evidence: []
  approval_requirements: []
  open_risks: []
  recommended_next_role: ""
  stop_reason: ""

docs.title: Runner Result
docs.text:
codex_runner_result:
  schema_version: 1
  status: "route_ready | needs_context | needs_approval | blocked | completed | failed"
  workspace: ""
  lifecycle_state: ""
  route_packet: {}
  handoffs: []
  files_touched: []
  files_proposed: []
  verification_evidence: []
  source_policy_status: ""
  approval_status: ""
  redactions:
    count: 0
    categories: []
  errors: []
  warnings: []
  next_action: ""

The result schema is the core Track 5 contract. Fixture eval should grade this contract first; Codex execution quality can be judged only after deterministic gates pass.

docs.title: Routing Policy
docs.text:
The runner chooses the next Product-Agent OS action from lifecycle state and current artifacts:

State Default route Write policy uninitialized workspace-discovery-auditor read_only infrastructure_planned requirements-author staged_only requirements_ready implementation-planner staged_only plan_ready agent-team-designer staged_only team_ready test-eval-designer staged_only build_active builder subagent or build slice packet approved_write quality_gate risk-reviewer read_only review_ready pr-release-operator staged_only release_ready learning-loop-maintainer staged_only learning_ready automation-promoter staged_only maintenance project-lifecycle-orchestrator read_only

The runner may recommend a subagent only when ownership boundaries are explicit. It must not spawn subagents itself from deterministic tests; it returns a route packet that Codex can execute in the active session.

docs.title: Guardrails And Validators
docs.text:
Required validators:

  • validate_codex_runner_request - schema, surface, write policy, and approval state.
  • validate_control_plane_context - required Product-Agent OS artifacts and lifecycle consistency.
  • validate_route_packet - recommended skill or subagent is valid for lifecycle state.
  • validate_handoff - reuse and extend Product-Agent OS handoff fields.
  • validate_source_policy - block or mark needs-review before durable source-backed claims.
  • validate_approval_boundary - no workspace writes or hook activation without approval.
  • validate_automation_boundary - active automation creation remains blocked.
  • validate_redaction - no secret-like literals, private customer data markers, raw private chat markers, or absolute user-specific paths in persisted outputs.
  • validate_result_contract - every completion claim has current-run evidence.

docs.title: Fixture Eval Extension
docs.text:
Extend fixture eval with runner fields:

codex_runtime_runner_status: "route_ready | needs_context | needs_approval | blocked | not_applicable"
codex_runtime_runner_checks:
  contract_mode_offline: true
  route_matches_lifecycle_state: true
  approval_required_for_writes: true
  handoff_incomplete_blocked: true
  active_automation_blocked: true
  secret_redaction_enforced: true

New synthetic fixtures:

  • codex-runner-ready - complete control-plane context produces route_ready.
  • codex-runner-missing-context - missing PLAN.md or acceptance criteria produces needs_context.
  • codex-runner-handoff-incomplete - missing constraints or verification_evidence is blocked.
  • codex-runner-approval-required - build/write route without approval produces needs_approval.
  • codex-runner-automation-blocked - active automation request is blocked.
  • codex-runner-secret-redaction - secret-like and absolute-path strings are redacted in result.

All fixtures must use synthetic data only.

docs.title: Security And Approval Model
docs.text:
Default policy:

  • read-only unless the route explicitly says staged_only or approved_write;
  • no network access;
  • no external dependency installation;
  • no direct API calls;
  • no active automation creation;
  • no project write from the runner itself;
  • outputs redacted before persistence;
  • failures return machine-readable status and no traceback in normal CLI output.

Blocked by default:

  • global Codex config mutation;
  • hook activation without Track 4 approval;
  • merge/apply without approval record;
  • active automation creation;
  • external system writes;
  • raw private chat logs;
  • secret-like literals in outputs;
  • absolute user-specific paths in persisted artifacts;
  • claiming implementation success without current-run evidence.

docs.title: Testing Strategy
docs.text:
Deterministic Track 5 tests remain unittest and standard-library-only.

Required tests:

  • runner contracts validate valid and invalid request/result payloads;
  • package imports with only Python standard library;
  • contract mode runs offline against a fixture workspace;
  • lifecycle state maps to the expected Product-Agent OS skill route;
  • build/write routes require approval;
  • incomplete handoff is rejected;
  • source-policy blocked prevents route readiness;
  • active automation request is blocked;
  • redaction removes secret-like literals and local absolute paths;
  • fixture eval includes codex_runtime_runner_status;
  • plugin structure test proves runner exists but is not default-activated;
  • normal verification commands do not require network, API credentials, or dependency installation.

Required verification after implementation:

python -m unittest discover -s tests -p "test_*.py" -v
python plugins\product-agent-os\scripts\run_fixture_eval.py
python tools\check_docs.py
$env:PYTHONPATH='C:\tmp\codex_docs_mkdocs'; python -m mkdocs build --strict

docs.title: Acceptance Criteria
docs.text:
Track 5 is complete when:

  • plugins/product-agent-os/scripts/codex_runtime_runner/ exists and imports with standard library only;
  • contract mode returns a valid codex_runner_result;
  • route packets correctly map lifecycle states to Product-Agent OS skills or subagent roles;
  • workspace writes, hook activation, merge/apply, and automation remain approval-gated;
  • runner validators catch incomplete handoffs, blocked source policy, missing approval, active automation requests, and secret retention;
  • fixture eval reports Codex runtime runner status and catches regressions;
  • plugin manifest and lifecycle skills do not make the runner default-active;
  • source registry and docs navigation include this Track 5 spec;
  • full verification pack exits 0.

docs.title: Residual Risks
docs.text:
Even after Track 5, a Codex-only runner cannot prove product correctness for every project. It can prove that lifecycle routing, handoff shape, source policy, approval boundary, redaction, and fixture eval behavior are stable.

The runner intentionally delegates actual model work to Codex. Quality still depends on the active Codex surface, selected model, prompt context, project artifacts, and verification evidence.

docs.title: Implementation Handoff
docs.text:
Implementation should be split into focused tasks:

  1. Codex runner contracts and result schema.
  2. Context loader and lifecycle state detector.
  3. Route planner for skills and subagent role recommendations.
  4. Redaction and deterministic guard validators.
  5. Contract-mode CLI wrapper.
  6. Fixture eval extension and synthetic runner fixtures.
  7. Plugin structure tests proving the runner is present but inactive by default.
  8. Documentation, source registry refresh, navigation, and full verification.

Each task should start with failing tests where practical, preserve Track 4 safety behavior, and avoid unrelated refactors.

docs.title: Spec Self-Review
docs.text:
Coverage:

  • standalone API-backed runner is removed from scope;
  • Codex-only execution boundary is explicit;
  • current Track 1-4 implementation and clean baseline are recorded;
  • route packet, handoff, result, approval, source, automation, and redaction policies are explicit;
  • fixture eval and verification requirements are defined.

Scope check:

  • Track 5 is one coherent Codex plugin orchestration layer, not a deployment platform or external app;
  • no deterministic test requires network, credentials, or third-party dependencies;
  • actual Codex model execution remains in the active Codex session, not in a separate runner process.

Ambiguity check:

  • default Product-Agent OS workflow remains unchanged;
  • no API keys or external credentials are used;
  • the runner may exist in the repo while remaining inactive by default;
  • writes and automations remain approval-gated through existing Product-Agent OS controls.

docs.title: Track 9 Methodology Intelligence Design
docs.text:
Source status: local product design + methodology research synthesis

Sources: Methodologies for Large Projects, Business & Product, Requirements & Domain, Solution Architecture, Frontend, Backend, API & Integrations, Database & Data, LLM / AI / RAG, Quality, Testing & Evals, Security, Privacy & Compliance, Delivery, Release & Operations, Codex / Agentic Workflow, Product-Agent OS plugin docs.

docs.title: Goal
docs.text:
Track 9 turns Product-Agent OS from a scenario workflow plugin into a methodology-aware product engineering system. When connected to a user project, it should first understand the workspace, classify project complexity and delivery maturity, build a project delivery map, then recommend the right methodologies, documentation artifacts, readiness gates, owners, evidence, approvals and next actions.

The product goal is to replace chaotic vibe-coding on real projects with a guided path toward product-ready software: clear intent, scoped architecture, useful artifacts, current evidence, reviewable risks and staged changes that are safe to show to users, teams or stakeholders.

docs.title: Core Product Principle
docs.text:
Track 9 must cover all aspects of development without forcing all methodology on every project.

The operating rule is:

cover every methodology domain
force only what is clearly applicable
record gaps and assumptions honestly
stage artifacts only after approval

docs.title: Existing Foundation
docs.text:
Track 8 already provides scenario routing, conditional readiness statuses, evidence-before-completion, acceptance scenarios, conditional DDD, bounded-context traceability, ubiquitous language traceability, conditional FSD routing, metric hardening, docs tooling selection, standards trigger policy, transcript/session evals and detailed methodology_applicability packets.

Track 9 builds on that foundation instead of replacing it. Scenario routing still answers "what situation is this project or request in?" Methodology intelligence answers "which engineering disciplines, artifacts and evidence are proportionate for this project's complexity, risk and maturity?"

docs.title: High-Level Flow
docs.text:
Track 9 uses a two-step onboarding flow.

User connects Product-Agent OS to workspace
    ↓
Read-only audit
    ↓
Complexity and maturity classification
    ↓
Delivery Map
    ↓
Methodology applicability analysis
    ↓
Human-readable audit report + machine-readable JSON
    ↓
User approval
    ↓
Staged artifacts and control-plane proposals

The first step is read-only. It produces recommendations and questions. The second step stages artifacts only after explicit approval.

docs.title: Classification Model
docs.text:
Track 9 uses two independent axes.

maturity_level describes the delivery and governance level:

Level Meaning baseline MVP, solo owner or low-risk internal work; minimum requirements, plan, checks and runlog. team Multiple engineers, subagents or workstreams; ownership, handoffs, architecture boundary and docs impact matter. production Real users, deployments, data, release process or operations; security, rollback, release readiness and runtime evidence matter. regulated PII, payments, healthcare, finance, minors, enterprise governance, legal/compliance or audit requirements.

complexity_profile describes the system and change complexity:

Profile Meaning simple Small project or narrow change with few dependencies and low blast radius. standard Normal product or service with tests, docs, API/UI/data surfaces or repeatable delivery. complex Multiple subsystems, integrations, teams, domains, workflows, data stores or runtime environments. high_risk Security, privacy, money, production data, irreversible migration, public contract, AI behavior, release or operational risk.

The classifier records:

  • observed_signals: facts discovered in files and workspace structure;
  • intent_signals: user request or prompt intent, never treated as proof by itself;
  • unknowns: facts that cannot be proven from workspace state;
  • questions_for_owner: questions that should be answered by the user or project owner;
  • provisional_assumptions: conservative assumptions used to choose a safe next step;
  • confidence: confidence for each classification and domain recommendation;
  • blocked_until_answered: whether missing answers block staging or implementation;
  • safe_next_action: what Product-Agent OS can do without overclaiming.

docs.title: Delivery Map
docs.text:
The read-only audit produces a Delivery Map rather than a passive repository summary.

The Delivery Map includes:

  • surface map: stack, package managers, entrypoints, test commands, docs, CI, runtime manifests and generated folders;
  • system map: domains, subsystems, UI/API/data/AI surfaces, data stores, external integrations, deploy/runtime surfaces and ownership gaps;
  • lifecycle map: current Product-Agent OS lifecycle state, control-plane status, existing evidence and missing files;
  • methodology map: applicable domains, missing gates, unverified artifacts, accepted gaps and approval-required actions;
  • next-action map: prioritized actions that connect a reason, methodology, artifact, owner, evidence and approval boundary.

docs.title: Audit Outputs
docs.text:
The read-only audit produces two outputs:

  1. methodology-audit-report.md Human-readable report for the user. It explains project classification, Delivery Map, methodology recommendations, questions, assumptions, risks and next actions.

  2. methodology-applicability.json Machine-readable contract for plugin scripts, lifecycle skills, fixture evals and later staged artifact generation.

The JSON output must be stable enough for tests and fixture evals. Markdown is for humans and must not become the source parser for plugin behavior.

docs.title: Recommendation Model
docs.text:
Recommendations are prioritized actions, not a list of documents to generate.

Each recommendation records:

  • priority: P0_blocker, P1_high_risk, P2_recommended, P3_optional_maturity or not_applicable;
  • reason: why this matters for this project;
  • methodology domain;
  • readiness gate;
  • recommended artifact;
  • evidence required;
  • evidence owner;
  • approval boundary;
  • accepted gap option;
  • residual risk;
  • safe next action.

This prevents document spam. An artifact is recommended only when it closes a gate, reduces a risk, supports ownership, records evidence or enables a concrete next action.

docs.title: Methodology Domains
docs.text:
Track 9 includes every methodology file under docs/methodologies.

Slice Source file Product-Agent OS purpose T9-D1 business-product.md Product hypothesis, value, opportunities, metrics, guardrails and measurement. T9-D2 requirements-domain.md Requirements quality, acceptance scenarios, business rules, domain model, traceability and change impact. T9-D3 solution-architecture.md Architecture boundaries, views, ADRs, quality attributes, tradeoffs, ownership and fitness checks. T9-D4 quality-testing-evals.md Risk-based tests, evals, current evidence, runtime/manual/visual evidence and CI quality gates. T9-D5 codex-agentic-workflow.md Control-plane maturity, model/reasoning policy, handoffs, subagents, MCP, hooks, skills, plugins and automation promotion. T9-D6 frontend.md UI behavior, component states, Storybook applicability, visual/a11y evidence, responsive checks, performance and FSD boundaries. T9-D7 backend.md Service boundaries, modular monolith vs microservices, runtime behavior, queues, observability, SLOs and rollback. T9-D8 api-integrations.md OpenAPI/AsyncAPI/GraphQL/gRPC contracts, consumers, compatibility, errors, generated clients and external writes. T9-D9 database-data.md Database inventory, schema source, migrations, transactions, data quality, classification and production access. T9-D10 llm-ai-rag.md AI behavior spec, eval baseline, prompts, models, tools, RAG sources, grounding, datasets, approvals and cost/latency. T9-D11 security-privacy-compliance.md Threat surface, ASVS/SSDF, authorization tests, secrets, privacy impact, supply chain, audit logging and compliance overlays. T9-D12 delivery-release-operations.md Release readiness, versioning, changelog, artifact manifest, rollout, rollback, CI/CD governance, runbooks and operations.

The order is intentional: product intent, requirements, architecture, quality and Codex workflow come before technical domains. Security/privacy and delivery/operations remain cross-cutting overlays but still receive dedicated domain slices.

docs.title: Domain Slice Contract
docs.text: Each domain slice follows the same implementation contract.

docs.title: Catalog Entries
docs.text:
Each domain adds machine-readable catalog entries:

  • domain id;
  • purpose;
  • applicability triggers;
  • non-applicability triggers;
  • maturity impact;
  • complexity impact;
  • related Track 8 scenarios;
  • related artifacts;
  • readiness gates;
  • eval fields;
  • conflict and overlap notes.

docs.title: Discovery Signals
docs.text:
Each domain defines:

  • file, folder, manifest and config signals;
  • prompt intent hints;
  • signals that only support present_unverified;
  • unknowns that should become questionnaire entries;
  • false-positive risks.

docs.title: Readiness Gates
docs.text:
All gates reuse the existing status vocabulary:

  • not_applicable;
  • applicable_missing;
  • present_unverified;
  • present_verified;
  • proposal_staged;
  • explicit_gap_accepted;
  • approval_required.

Detection alone can only produce present_unverified. present_verified requires current command evidence, owner evidence, artifact evidence or a clearly recorded accepted gap.

docs.title: Artifact Templates
docs.text:
Each domain adds or extends artifact templates only when they are tied to a gate or recommendation. Templates must be synthetic, source-safe and secret-free.

Examples include product briefs, requirement traceability matrices, architecture review records, frontend state matrices, backend runtime behavior docs, API consumer maps, database migration plans, AI eval specs, security risk reviews and release readiness packets.

docs.title: Lifecycle Skill Updates
docs.text:
Each domain updates relevant lifecycle skills:

  • workspace-discovery-auditor observes signals and unknowns;
  • requirements-author captures product, requirement and domain evidence;
  • implementation-planner blocks build work when applicable gates are missing;
  • agent-team-designer maps ownership and handoff boundaries;
  • test-eval-designer selects checks and evals;
  • risk-reviewer reviews missing evidence, accepted gaps, conflicts and risky changes;
  • pr-release-operator includes release, contract, security and operations impact;
  • learning-loop-maintainer records lessons and domain decisions;
  • automation-promoter refuses promotion without maturity evidence and rollback.

docs.title: Tests And Evals
docs.text:
Each domain slice must add:

  • focused unit tests for catalog/discovery/gate behavior;
  • fixture eval coverage;
  • false-positive tests when the domain can be over-applied;
  • docs sync;
  • Product-Agent OS docs updates when user behavior changes;
  • source registry updates when source-backed claims change.

docs.title: Adaptive Deep-Dive Loop
docs.text:
The Track 9 queue is a living backlog. Each methodology file is inspected before implementation and can expand into multiple sub-slices.

T9-Dn-0: domain deep audit
    ↓
T9-Dn-1..N: implementation sub-slices
    ↓
T9-Dn-final: domain verification and docs sync

Each domain deep audit records:

  • concepts already covered by Track 8;
  • new concepts;
  • duplicate or overlapping gates;
  • new artifacts;
  • existing artifacts that need extension;
  • likely false positives;
  • required tests and evals;
  • open questions;
  • items deferred to cross-domain synthesis.

The backlog may change when a deep audit finds hidden sub-tasks, cross-domain overlap, false positives, duplicate artifacts, insufficient tests or a changed product direction. Every change must be recorded in RUNLOG.md or a Track 9 status/backlog document with rationale.

docs.title: Cross-Domain Synthesis
docs.text:
After all 12 domains are integrated, Track 9 runs a synthesis slice.

The synthesis pass must:

  • deduplicate gates;
  • merge overlapping artifacts;
  • identify conflicting recommendations;
  • define priority rules;
  • normalize naming and vocabulary;
  • map mutually exclusive frameworks;
  • add cross-domain false-positive fixtures;
  • verify that recommendations stay proportionate;
  • update docs and final Track 9 baseline.

Known overlap areas:

  • metric hardening appears in product, quality and delivery;
  • security review appears in backend, API, data, AI, delivery and compliance;
  • architecture boundary appears in requirements, architecture, frontend, backend, API and data;
  • evidence-before-completion appears everywhere;
  • release readiness appears in delivery, security, docs, package/plugin and operations contexts;
  • accepted gaps and residual risk appear in every methodology.

docs.title: Safety Rules
docs.text:
Track 9 follows these safety rules:

  1. Read-only first. Workspace onboarding produces audit output only.

  2. Recommendation before generation. Product-Agent OS explains why an artifact or methodology is applicable before staging it.

  3. Explicit approval before staged artifacts. No target workspace writes happen without approval. Staged artifacts remain reviewable proposals.

  4. Conditional methodology. DDD, FSD, security/compliance, release governance and other frameworks are conditional.

  5. No false readiness. Observed files, directories or prompt intent do not prove readiness.

  6. No document spam. Documents exist to close gates, reduce risk, record ownership or enable next action.

  7. No secrets or private data. Reports, fixtures, templates, prompts, memory notes and examples must not contain secrets, private keys, tokens, customer data, raw private chats or absolute user-specific paths.

  8. Evidence before completion. Ready, completed, fixed, works and release claims require current evidence or an explicit inspection-only/test-gap label.

docs.title: Verification Strategy
docs.text:
Every Track 9 implementation slice must run verification proportional to touched files.

For docs-only or design docs:

python tools\check_docs.py

For plugin scripts, templates, fixtures or tests:

python -m unittest discover -s tests -p "test_*.py" -v
python plugins\product-agent-os\scripts\run_fixture_eval.py
python plugins\product-agent-os\scripts\run_transcript_eval.py plugins\product-agent-os\assets\eval-fixtures\transcripts\product-agent-os-synthetic-sessions.json
python plugins\product-agent-os\scripts\validate_codex_compatibility.py

For navigation, Mermaid, Markdown extensions or MkDocs-sensitive changes:

$env:PYTHONPATH='C:\tmp\codex_docs_mkdocs'; $env:NO_MKDOCS_2_WARNING='1'; python -m mkdocs build --strict

docs.title: Definition Of Done For A Domain Slice
docs.text:
A domain slice is done when:

  • its methodology file has been deeply audited;
  • applicable concepts are represented in catalog, discovery, gates, templates, skills or evals;
  • duplicates and overlaps are recorded for synthesis;
  • false-positive risks are covered by tests or explicitly deferred;
  • user-facing docs explain behavior where needed;
  • current verification evidence is recorded;
  • residual risks are explicit.

docs.title: Definition Of Done For Track 9
docs.text:
Track 9 is done when:

  • all 12 methodology files complete the domain integration loop;
  • the plugin has a unified methodology catalog;
  • read-only audit produces methodology-audit-report.md and methodology-applicability.json;
  • recommendations are prioritized and linked to artifacts, gates, owners, evidence and approvals;
  • staged artifacts are generated only after approval;
  • cross-domain synthesis resolves duplicates, conflicts and naming drift;
  • regression fixtures cover high-risk false positives;
  • Product-Agent OS docs explain Track 9 onboarding and methodology selection;
  • full test, fixture eval, transcript eval, compatibility, docs and MkDocs baseline passes.

docs.title: Non-Goals
docs.text:
Track 9 does not:

  • activate hooks, automations, GitHub Actions, external writes, package publishing or release actions without explicit approval;
  • make every methodology mandatory for every project;
  • replace human product, domain, security, legal or architecture ownership;
  • claim semantic correctness from artifact presence alone;
  • infer production, compliance, privacy or business risk from files without recording uncertainty;
  • use Markdown reports as the parser for plugin behavior;
  • store private customer data, raw private chat logs or secrets in generated artifacts.

docs.title: Initial Risks
docs.text:
• Scope risk: 12 domains create a large implementation surface. Mitigation: domain-by-domain slices and adaptive deep audits.
  • False-positive risk: methodology signals can over-apply gates to simple projects. Mitigation: non-applicability triggers, false-positive fixtures and accepted gaps.
  • Duplication risk: many domains share gates and artifacts. Mitigation: synthesis backlog and final cross-domain synthesis pass.
  • User-experience risk: recommendations can become overwhelming. Mitigation: priority levels, safe next action and staged generation only after approval.
  • Verification risk: deterministic tests can prove contract shape but not methodology quality. Mitigation: owner review fields, residual risks and future semantic evals.
  • Stale-doc risk: methodology docs and plugin catalog can drift. Mitigation: docs sync checks and Track 9 status/backlog evidence.

docs.title: Open Design Decisions For Implementation Planning
docs.text:
These decisions are scoped for implementation planning, not unresolved design gaps:

  • Whether methodology_catalog lives as JSON only or as Python data with generated JSON.
  • Exact file paths for read-only audit outputs and staged artifact output.
  • Whether each domain deep audit gets a dedicated status document or one combined Track 9 backlog.
  • How much of the catalog is generated from docs/methodologies versus hand-authored in plugin assets.
  • Which domain slice receives the first executable implementation after foundation.
